Penpulimab-kcqx
N/A
Programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) blocking antibody
N/A
Akeso Biopharma Co., Ltd.
10 mg/mL, 10 mL
In combination with either cisplatin or carboplatin and
gemcitabine for the first-line treatment of non-keratinizing
nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC): 200 mg as an intravenous
infusion every 3 weeks.

As a single agent for non-keratinizing NPC with disease
progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and at
least one other prior line of therapy: 200 mg as an intravenous
infusion every 2 weeks.
Applicant Proposed Penpulimab-kcqx, in combination with gemcitabine and
Indication(s)/Population(s) cisplatin or carboplatin, is indicated as first-line treatment of
patients with recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal
carcinoma (NPC).
Penpulimab-kcqx, as a single agent, is indicated for the
treatment of adults with metastatic non-keratinizing NPC with
disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy
and at least one other prior line of therapy.

Recommended Penpulimab-kcqx, in combination with either cisplatin or
Indication(s)/Population(s) carboplatin and gemcitabine, is indicated for the first-line
(if applicable) treatment of adults with recurrent or metastatic nonkeratinizing nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC).
Penpulimab-kcqx, as a single agent, is indicated for the
treatment of adults with metastatic non-keratinizing NPC and
disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy
and at least one other prior line of therapy.

Penpulimab

1. Executive Summary
1.1. Product Introduction and Regulatory Background
Penpulimab-kcqx (hereafter referred to as penpulimab) is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody
directed against programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1), thereby blocking the
immunosuppressive interaction between PD-1 and programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) and
programmed cell death ligand 2 (PD-L2). It is not approved for any indication in the U.S.
An initial Biologics Licensing Application (BLA) was submitted for penpulimab as a single-agent
for patients with previously treated nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) on July 16, 2021, based
on the results of the single-arm trial, Study AK105-202. FDA issued a Complete Response on
January 19, 2024, as penpulimab did not demonstrate a clear advantage over currently
available therapeutic options due to changes in the treatment landscape for NPC, to grant
accelerated approval. Additionally, deficiencies were identified in CGMP operations in the
penpulimab drug substance and drug product manufacturing facility, and in the manufacture of
penpulimab.
On February 27, 2024, the Applicant requested a Type B meeting under IND 138576 to discuss
whether an interim analysis of the randomized trial, Study AK105-304, could be conducted to
support a BLA for penpulimab in combination with either cisplatin or carboplatin and
gemcitabine for the first-line treatment of patients with recurrent or metastatic NPC. The
Applicant also wanted to discuss plans to address the chemistry, manufacturing, and controls
deficiencies identified in the Complete Response Letter. The meeting was granted with
preliminary comments from the FDA issued to the Applicant on April 12, 2024. After additional
email communications between the Applicant and FDA on April 17, 2024, and April 19, 2024,
agreement was reached to cancel the Type B meeting.
In the current Class 2 BLA resubmission, the Applicant is seeking two indications in NPC with
two different dosing regimens. For the Applicant’s proposed indication for use “in combination
with gemcitabine and cisplatin or carboplatin, as first-line treatment of patients with recurrent
or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma”, the proposed dosage regimen is penpulimab 200 mg
intravenously (IV) once every three weeks (Q3W).
The Applicant’s proposed indication for penpulimab as a single agent is for “the treatment of
adults with metastatic non-keratinizing NPC with disease progression on or after platinumbased chemotherapy and at least one other prior line of therapy”. The Applicant proposed
dosage regimen is penpulimab 200 mg IV once every two weeks (Q2W).

1.2. Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness
The Applicant intends for this marketing application to support approval of penpulimab for two
indications: 1) in combination with either cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine for the firstline treatment of patients with metastatic or recurrent NPC and 2) as a single agent for the
treatment of adult patients with metastatic non-keratinizing NPC with disease progression on
or after platinum-containing chemotherapy and at least one other prior line of therapy.
The primary study providing evidence in support of the first-line indication is Study AK105-304.
In Study AK105-304, 291 adult patients with metastatic or recurrent WNPC who had not
received previous systemic chemotherapy for recurrent or metastatic disease were randomized
(1:1) to receive either penpulimab in combination with cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine
Q3W for up to 6 cycles followed by single-agent penpulimab Q3W or placebo Q3W in
combination with cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine Q3W for up to 6 cycles followed by
single-agent placebo Q3W. Treatment was administered until disease progression,
unacceptable toxicity, or a maximum of 24 months. The primary efficacy endpoint was
progression free survival (PFS) by blinded independent review committee (BICR) per RECIST
v.1.1, with a key secondary endpoint of overall survival (OS). At an interim analysis of PFS based
on 189 events (85% information fraction [IF]), the trial demonstrated a statistically significant
and clinically meaningful improvement in BICR-assessed PFS favoring the penpulimab arm, with
a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.45 (95% CI 0.33, 0.62, p-value <0.0001), corresponding to a median PFS
of 9.6 months (95% CI 7.1, 12.5) in the penpulimab arm and 7.0 months (95% CI 6.9, 7.3) in the
placebo arm. Although the observed 2.6-month improvement in median PFS is modest for an
add-on therapy, the treatment effect, as measured by the HR, was consistent across subgroups
and withstood rigorous sensitivity analyses, highlighting the robustness and reliability of the
results. These results are also supported by a longer median DOR in the penpulimab arm of 9.8
months (95% CI: 7, 17.4) compared to 5.7 months (95% CI: 5.5, 6.7) in the placebo arm. While a
statistically significant improvement in OS has not been demonstrated in Study AK105-304, the
OS results at the first formal interim analysis (70% IF) indicate no detrimental effect of
penpulimab on OS. At this interim analysis, the OS HR was 0.91 (95% CI: 0.64, 1.31), with
median OS not reached in the penpulimab arm and 31.3 months (95% CI: 27.4, NE) in the
placebo arm. Notably, 80% of patients receiving placebo either crossed over to open-label
treatment with penpulimab or received another anti-PD-(L)1 antibody as the next subsequent
therapy upon confirmed disease progression, which may impact interpretability of the OS
results. OS will be tested again at a second prespecified interim analysis (80% IF) and a final
analysis.
Study AK105-202 provides the primary efficacy data in support of the indication for the
treatment of patients with non-keratinizing NPC with disease progression on or after platinumcontaining chemotherapy and at least one other prior line of therapy. In Study AK105-202, 125
patients with metastatic non-keratinizing NPC received penpulimab 200 mg IV Q2W until
disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or a maximum of 24 months. The major efficacy

FDA will apply this policy in a flexible manner according to the nature of the drug and data

population of U.S. patients with NPC (see Postmarketing Commitments later in this review for
details).

1.3. Benefit-Risk Assessment (BRA)
Benefit-Risk Summary and Assessment
There were 133,354 new cases of NPC diagnosed globally in 2020, and approximately 80,000 people died from NPC in 2020. More than 75% of
the global cases of NPC develop in South and East Asia, compared with 1.6% in Northern America. NPC is rare in the U.S., with <1 case per
100,000 people each year. The World Health Organization classifies NPC in three major subtypes: non-keratinizing undifferentiated, nonkeratinizing differentiated, and keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma. While the non-keratinizing undifferentiated subtype of NPC is the
predominant subtype in both Southern China (95%) and the U.S. (63%), the keratinizing subtype of NPC is uncommon in Southern China (2%)
relative to the US (25%).
The prognosis for patients with recurrent, unresectable, or metastatic NPC is poor. On October 27, 2023, FDA approved toripalimab (a
monoclonal antibody targeting programmed cell death protein 1 [PD-1]) with cisplatin and gemcitabine for the first-line treatment of adults
with metastatic or recurrent, locally advanced NPC, based on the randomized, double-blind JUPITER-02 trial. In the JUPITER-02 trial, toripalimab
with cisplatin and gemcitabine demonstrated a median PFS of 11.7 months and a median OS not yet reached. Patients who received placebo
with cisplatin and gemcitabine had a median PFS of 8.0 months and median OS of 33.7 months. On the same day, FDA also approved
toripalimab as a single agent for adult patients with recurrent unresectable or metastatic NPC with disease progression on or after a platinumcontaining therapy based on the results of the open-label, multicohort POLARIS-02 trial, which demonstrated an ORR as assessed by BICR of
21% and a median DOR of 14.9 months. Despite these recent approvals, metastatic NPC remains a fatal, incurable disease, and an unmet need
exists for patients with advanced NPC.
Penpulimab is a monoclonal antibody targeting PD-1, an immune checkpoint inhibitor with an established pharmacological class of PD-1
blocking antibody. The proposed dosage regimen for penpulimab in combination with cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine is 200 mg
intravenously (IV) once every 3 weeks (Q3W). The Applicant’s proposed dosage regimen for penpulimab when administered as a single agent is
200 mg IV Q2W. The Applicant’s proposed indications for penpulimab are: 1) penpulimab, in combination with either cisplatin or carboplatin
and gemcitabine, for the first-line treatment of adults with recurrent or metastatic NPC, and 2) penpulimab, as a single agent, for the treatment

The primary study supporting the first-line indication is Study AK105-304, in which 291 patients with recurrent or metastatic NPC were
randomized 1:1 to receive either penpulimab 200 mg IV Q3W in combination with 6 cycles of cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine (n=144)
or placebo with cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine (n=147). The primary efficacy endpoint was PFS by BICR per RECIST v1.1, with a key
secondary endpoint of OS. An interim analysis of PFS was initially proposed at 155 events (70% IF) but was conducted at 189 events (85% IF)
instead. This overrun was a result of a change in the analysis population that stemmed from difficulty enrolling patients outside of Asia, due to
the rarity of NPC in other parts of the world, and the approval of toripalimab plus cisplatin and gemcitabine during the conduct of the trial.
These changes in the analysis plan were deemed acceptable to the FDA review team for this particular application. At the interim analysis of
PFS based on 189 events, the trial demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in BICR-assessed PFS favoring
the penpulimab arm, with a HR of 0.45 (95% CI 0.33, 0.62, p-value <0.0001), corresponding to a median PFS of 9.6 months (95% CI 7.1, 12.5) in
the penpulimab arm and 7.0 months (95% CI 6.9, 7.3) in the placebo arm. In total, 31% and 11% of patients were alive and progression free
after 12 months of follow-up in the penpulimab and placebo arms, respectively. The presence of a tail in the Kaplan-Meier PFS curves, which
begin to separate at approximately 7 months, suggests that some patients may derive prolonged PFS benefit or that there is potentially late
treatment effect with penpulimab, which are not captured by median PFS alone. The PFS treatment effect, as measured by the HR, was
consistent across subgroups and withstood rigorous sensitivity analyses, highlighting the robustness and reliability of the results. The ORR was
68% (95% CI: 60, 76) for the penpulimab arm and 64% (95% CI: 56, 72) for the placebo arm. There was a longer median DOR in the penpulimab
arm of 9.8 months (95% CI: 7, 17.4) compared to 5.7 months (95% CI: 5.5, 6.7) in the placebo arm.
While a statistically significant improvement in OS has not been demonstrated in Study AK105-304, the OS results at the first formal interim
analysis (70% IF) indicate no detrimental effect of penpulimab on OS. At this interim analysis, the OS HR was 0.91 (95% CI: 0.64, 1.31), with
median OS not reached in the penpulimab arm and 31.3 months (95% CI: 27.4, NE) in the placebo arm. Notably, 49% of patients receiving
placebo crossed over to open-label treatment with penpulimab upon confirmed disease progression, and an additional 31% of patients on the
placebo arm received an anti-PD-(L)1 antibody as the next subsequent therapy outside of Study AK105-304, which may impact interpretability
of the OS results. OS will be tested again at a second prespecified interim analysis (80% IF) and a final analysis.

discontinuation of penpulimab were acute myocardial infarction, acute kidney injury, brain edema, diabetic ketoacidosis, increased potassium,
increased lipase, and thrombocytopenia (0.7% each).
The evaluation of safety for penpulimab as a single agent included analyses of safety data for 130 patients with NPC treated with penpulimab
200 mg IV Q2W as a single agent in Study AK105-202 and a monotherapy pooled population of 372 patients with advanced solid tumors
(including the 130 patients with NPC) or classical Hodgkin lymphoma treated with penpulimab 200 mg IV Q2W. Among the 372 patients who
received single agent penpulimab, the most common (≥20%) adverse reactions were anemia (25%) and hypothyroidism (23%). Among the 130
patients with NPC treated with penpulimab 200 mg IV Q2W as a single agent in Study AK105-202, the most common (≥20%) adverse reactions
were hypothyroidism (39%) and musculoskeletal pain (25%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 22% of these 130 patients. Serious adverse
reactions in ≥1% were pneumonia (3.8%), pneumonitis (1.5%), respiratory failure (1.5%), and rash (1.5%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in
1% of patients with NPC treated with single-agent penpulimab, including a case each of pneumonitis, septic shock, colitis, and hepatitis.

Keratinizing and non-keratinizing NPC are biologically distinct subtypes with different etiologies, molecular profiles, and responses to
treatment. Non-keratinizing NPC is strongly associated with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection and typically demonstrates higher sensitivity to
immunotherapy and chemotherapeutic agents. In contrast, keratinizing NPC is more frequently linked to environmental factors such as
smoking and exhibits different treatment response patterns. Given almost no clinical data available for penpulimab in patients with keratinizing
NPC, FDA recommends that the indications are limited to patients with non-keratinizing histology.

•

metastatic non-keratinizing NPC.

•

platinum-based chemotherapy and at least one other prior line of therapy.

Nasopharyngeal carcinoma originates in the nasopharynx from the base of
the skull to the palate.
There were 133,354 cases worldwide in 2020 with the majority of cases
(>75%) in South and East Asia and 1.6% in Northern America, and
approximately 80,000 people died from NPC in 2020. NPC is rare in the
United States, with <1 case per 100,000 people each year.
There are three major histologic subtypes of NPC based on the WHO
classification, with differences in subtype distribution between North
America and China: Type 1 keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma (25% vs
2%), Type 2 non-keratinizing differentiated carcinoma (12 vs 3%), and
Type 3 non-keratinizing undifferentiated carcinoma (63% vs 95%).
For metastatic NPC, the median OS is 29.1 months with first-line platinumbased chemotherapy alone. A statistically significant OS improvement was
also observed with median OS not reached (95% CI: 38.7 months, not
estimable) for toripalimab-tpzi in combination with platinum-based
chemotherapy (based on the POLARIS-02 trial).

Conclusions and Reasons
The incidence of NPC is substantially higher in
Southeast Asia relative to the U.S. A higher
proportion of patients with NPC in North
America develop the keratinizing squamous
subtype compared with China, where the vast
majority of patients develop the nonkeratinizing undifferentiated subtype.
The prognosis for metastatic NPC remains poor
with limited therapeutic options.

Conclusions and Reasons

Toripalimab-tpzi, in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine, is
approved for the first-line treatment of metastatic or recurrent NPC based
on results from the JUPITER-02 trial. The trial demonstrated a median PFS
of 11.7 months with toripalimab-tpzi versus 8.0 months with placebo,
both in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine (HR 0.52; 95% CI:
0.36–0.74; p=0.0003). A statistically significant OS improvement was also
observed with median OS not reached (95% CI: 38.7 months, not
estimable) for the toripalimab-tpzi-containing regimen and 33.7 months
(95% CI: 27.0, 44.2) for the placebo-containing regimen (HR 0.63 [95% CI:
0.45, 0.89], p-value=0.0083).
Toripalimab-tpzi is also approved for NPC with disease progression on or
after a platinum-containing chemotherapy based on an ORR of 21% (95%
CI 15, 28) and median DOR of 14.9 months (95% CI: 10.3, not estimable) in
the POLARIS-02 trial.
Prior to the approval of toripalimab-tpzi, in the metastatic setting,
standard of care treatment for first line therapy was cisplatin plus
gemcitabine, with a reported median PFS of 7.0 months and median OS of
29.1 months.

Metastatic NPC represents a life-threatening
disease. For patients with metastatic or
recurrent NPC, FDA approved toripalimab-tpzi
in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine
in the first line setting and toripalimab-tpzi as a
single agent with disease progression on or
after a platinum-containing therapy.

AK105-202.

The efficacy of single-agent penpulimab was evaluated in Study AK105202, an open-label, multicenter, single-arm trial conducted in a single
country (China). A total of 125 patients with unresectable or metastatic

2. Therapeutic Context
2.1. Analysis of Condition
NPC is a rare malignancy in most parts of the world but is endemic in Southeast Asia, Eastern
Asia (especially Southern China) and North Africa (Chen YP, et al. 2019). According to the
International Agency for Research on Cancer, in 2018, there were about 129,000 new cases of
NPC and >70% of new cases are in Eastern and Southeast Asia, with an age-standardized rate of
3.0 per 100,000 in China to 0.4 per 100,000 in populations that are mainly Caucasian (Bray F, et
al. 2018). Among the U.S. population, Chinese American accounted for approximately 36% of
new cases of NPC according to the U.S. SEER 18 registries. NPC remains an important cause of
cancer-related death worldwide with an incidence of approximately 50,000 deaths annually
(Carioli G, et al. 2017; Tang LL, et al. 2016).
NPC is currently classified by the World Health Organization (WHO) into 3 major histological
subtypes: keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma (WHO type 1), differentiated nonkeratinizing
carcinoma (WHO type 2), and undifferentiated carcinoma (WHO type 3) (Ou SI, et al. 2007).
Nonkeratinizing NPC, for which Epstein Barr virus (EBV) is an etiologic factor, constitutes most
cases in endemic areas (>95%), including Southeast Asia, Eastern Asia and North Africa. The
keratinizing subtype is more closely associated with cigarette smoking/alcohol consumption
and accounts for a higher proportion of cases in nonendemic regions including the U.S (Wang Y,
et al. 2013; Argirion I, et al. 2020). It has been noted that the incidence of the nonkeratinizing
subtype is increasing in North America (Argirion I, et al. 2020), and similarly, findings of
nonkeratinizing carcinoma being the predominant histology have been reported among white
populations living in Europe (Svajdler Jr M, et al. 2016; Ruuskanen M, et al. 2019; Slevin F, et al.
2020). Despite differences in etiology and histology, current clinical management of NPC is
consistent across the histologic subtypes.
The FDA’s Assessment:
There were approximately 133,354 cases of NPC diagnosed worldwide in 2020 with the
majority of cases (>75%) in South and East Asia and 1.6% in Northern America, and
approximately 80,000 people died from NPC in 2020 (Globocan, 2020). NPC is rare in the United
States, with <1 case per 100,000 people each year (Cancer.Net, 2022). A review of data from
the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) registry reported by Sun et al (2017)
identified 3919 patients with histologically confirmed NPC between 2004 and 2013. Among the
3919 patients, median age was 54 years (range 44, 63) and 71% of patients were male.
Information on race was included for 3672 patients with 49% White, 12% Black, and 39% Asian
(including 18% Chinese ethnicity). Information on histology was included for 1087 patients; of
these patients, 83% had non-keratinizing and 17% had keratinizing NPC.

2.2. Analysis of Current Treatment Options
The Applicant’s Position:
Guidelines for RM-NPC are consistent between the U.S. and China. Before the approval of PD-1
inhibitors in RM-NPC, the NCCN Head and Neck Cancer Clinical Practice Guidelines®
recommend platinum-based chemotherapy regimens for first-line treatment of RM-NPC, with
gemcitabine-cisplatin (GC) representing the preferred platinum-based regimen (category 1
recommendation). Other recommended regimens of first-line include cisplatin/5-FU, cisplatin
or carboplatin/ docetaxel or paclitaxel, carboplatin/ cetuximab or gemcitabine/ carboplatin
(NCCN Head and Neck Cancer Clinical Practice Guidelines®, V4, 2024). Although a high
percentage of patients with NPC initially respond to chemotherapy, the duration of response is
usually short (<6 months on average); median PFS for first-line GP treatment is only 7 months
(Zhang L, 2016).
PD-1 inhibitors (toripalimab, camrelizumab and tiselelizumab) combined with chemotherapy
were firstly approved by the NMPA in China in the first-line treatment of RM-NPC, while in
October 2023 FDA also approved toripalimab in combination with chemotherapy in the same
indication. The recommendations on RM-NPC from clinical guidelines have converged again in
the U.S. and China.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA agrees with the Applicant that on October 27, 2023, FDA granted traditional approval to
toripalimab-tpzi in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine for the first-line treatment of
adults with metastatic or recurrent, locally advanced NPC based on the results of the JUPITER02 trial. The median PFS was 11.7 months for patients treated with toripalimab-tpzi with
cisplatin and gemcitabine versus 8.0 months for patients treated with placebo with cisplatin
and gemcitabine (PFS HR 0.52; 95% CI 0.36, 0.74; p=0.0003). A statistically significant OS
improvement was also observed with median OS not reached (95% CI: 38.7 months, not
estimable) for the toripalimab-tpzi-containing regimen and 33.7 months (95% CI: 27.0, 44.2) for
the placebo-containing regimen (HR 0.63 [95% CI: 0.45, 0.89], p-value=0.0083). On October 27,
2023, FDA also granted traditional approval to toripalimab-tpzi as a single agent for the
treatment of adults with recurrent unresectable or metastatic NPC with disease progression on
or after a platinum-containing chemotherapy based on results of the POLARIS-02 trial. In 172
patients, the ORR by BICR was 21% (95% CI: 15, 28) and median DOR was 14.9 months (95% CI:
10.3, not estimable).

3. Regulatory Background
3.1. U.S. Regulatory Actions and Marketing History
The Applicant’s Position:
Penpulimab has been approved for marketing in three oncology indications in China, including
second or later lines of classic Hodgkin lymphoma(cHL), second or later lines of nasopharyngeal
carcinoma (NPC) and first-line non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Penpulimab is not currently
approved or marketed in the US . The clinical development program for penpulimab is being
conducted under Investigational New Drug (IND) 138576 with Division of Regulatory Operations
-Oncologic Diseases for DO2, and the relevant regulatory history is included in Section 3.2.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position.

3.2. Summary of Presubmission/Submission Regulatory Activity
The Applicant’s Position:
Penpulimab is a Anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody which received the Phase I Study May Proceed
letter on Apr 11, 2018, under IND 138576, for the treatment of advanced solid tumors.
The FDA granted penpulimab Fast Track designation (FTD) on October 13, 2020, for the
development of penpulimab, as systemic monotherapy for metastatic NPC patients who had
progressed after two or more prior lines of therapy including platinum-containing
chemotherapy. Orphan Drug Designation was granted by the FDA on February 23, 2021, for the
treatment of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Breakthrough Therapy Designation (BTD) was granted
on March 24, 2021.
The penpulimab BLA (# 761258) was submitted in July 2021 for an accelerated approval for the
treatment of patients with metastatic NPC who have progressed after two or more prior lines
of therapy including platinum-containing chemotherapy. The PDUFA date was July 16, 2022.
During the BLA review period, the phase III protocol AK105-304 was submitted to the IND
138576 in August 2021, which intended to confirm the clinical benefit and to support full
approval of penpulimab for the treatment of patients with metastatic or recurrent NPC. FDA
completed four rounds of comments on the protocol and SAP, and both FDA and Sponsor
reached agreement on the protocol and the SAP. No issues were outstanding.
During the BLA review period, FDA stated that the submission on May 30, 2022, constituted a
major amendment and therefore the PDUFA date was extended to October 16, 2022.

5. Nonclinical Pharmacology/Toxicology
5.1. Executive Summary
Penpulimab is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that targets programmed cell death protein
1 (PD-1); its established pharmacologic class is PD-1-blocking antibody. PD-1 is expressed on
activated T and B cells, natural killer cells, and myeloid lineage cells. Binding of PD-1 to its
ligands, programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) and PD-L2, inhibits T-cell activity, T-cell
proliferation, and cytokine production. In the tumor microenvironment, PD-1 signaling
contributes to the inhibition of T cell-mediated immune surveillance of tumors. Thus, blockade
of PD-1 signaling in the tumor microenvironment is intended to enhance tumor
immunosurveillance and anti-tumor immune responses.
In in vitro studies, penpulimab bound to human and cynomolgus monkey PD-1 but did not bind
rodent PD-1, supporting the use of cynomolgus monkeys as the single pharmacologically
relevant species for toxicity assessment. In cellular assays, penpulimab blocked the binding of
human PD-1 to human PD-L1 and PD-L2 and also competitively bound to PD-1 expressed on the
surface of human PD-1-transfected 293T cells. Additionally, penpulimab induced the secretion
of interleukin-2 (IL-2) and interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) in a mixed culture of peripheral blood
mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and dendritic cells (DCs) and in a mixed culture of PBMCs, DCs, and
Raji Burkitt lymphoma cells. Penpulimab also enhanced IFN-γ secretion by cytomegalovirus
(CMV)-responsive human PBMCs during the recall response to CMV antigen.
Given that pempulimab does not bind mouse PD-1, the Applicant investigated the in vivo
antitumor activity of pempulimab in a human PD-1 knock-in genetically engineered mouse
model (HuGEMM) implanted subcutaneously with MC38 mouse colon adenocarcinoma cells.
Intraperitoneal administration of pempulimab at doses of 0.8 and 8 mg/kg twice a week for a
total of 5 doses resulted in tumor growth inhibition (TGI) compared to the isotype control.
The Applicant also evaluated the antitumor activity of penpulimab in immunodeficient mice
implanted subcutaneously with Raji cells expressing PD-L1 or a Raji-PD-L1/PBMC mixture.
Intravenous (IV) administration of penpulimab (10 mg/kg) on Days 7, 13, and 21 resulted in
greater TGI compared to the isotype control.
The Applicant evaluated the safety of penpulimab in cynomolgus monkeys in GLP-compliant
repeat-dose toxicology studies of up to 13 weeks duration. In the 6- and 13-week studies,
monkeys received IV infusion of pempulimab at doses up to 60 mg/kg once every 2 weeks.
There were no mortalities or penpulimab-related findings of toxicological significance. Target

organs of toxicity in the 6-week study were the kidney (increased cortical tubular pigment or
pigmented interstitial macrophages), spleen (increased cellularity), adrenal gland (cortical
hypertrophy), parotid salivary gland (acinar cell atrophy), thymus (increased weight); and in the
13-week study was lymph nodes (erythrophagocytosis and increased cellularity). The incidence
of anti-drug antibody formation was 63.33% in the 6-week study and 93.33% in the 13-week
study, which may explain the limited findings noted in the 13-week study. In clinical trials done
to support the approval of penpulimab in the proposed patient population, toxicities associated
with penpulimab were primarily immune-mediated adverse reactions that are predicted by its
mechanism of action. At the recommended clinical dose of 200 mg, the human AUC0-336 was
26200 µg*h/mL.
Based on its mechanism of action and data from the literature, there is potential for enhanced
immune responses to infection following treatment with penpulimab. Mycobacterium
tuberculosis (Mtb)-infected PD-1 knockout mice exhibited decreased survival compared to wildtype mice, which correlated with increased bacterial proliferation and inflammatory responses
in these animals. It is unclear whether decreased survival resulted from an inability to mount an
appropriate antibacterial response or a failure to control the immune response leading to
normal tissue destruction and organ failure (Lazar-Molnar, et al. 2010). Furthermore, in mouse
models of lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) infection, the absence of PD-1 pathway
signaling led to fatal CD8+ T cell-mediated killing of virally infected vascular endothelial cells,
systemic vascular leakage, and ultimately cardiovascular collapse (Frebel et al. 2012; Mueller et
al. 2010). Similarly, PD-L1-deficient mice died early after chronic systemic LCMV infection
(Barber et al. 2006). In addition, blockade of PD-1 with an anti-PD-1 antibody in Mtb infection in
monkeys can exacerbate the infection and lead to death and severe pulmonary stress in
infected monkeys (Kauffman et al. 2021). A brief description of these data was included in
Section 13.2 of the label to convey these potential risks to prescribers.
No reproductive or embryo-fetal developmental toxicology studies were conducted with
penpulimab. Rather, the Applicant provided a literature-based assessment of the potential
reproductive toxicity of penpulimab, consistent with the alternative approach described in the
FDA Guidance for Industry Oncology Pharmaceuticals: Reproductive Toxicity Testing and
Labeling Recommendations. Data from the literature demonstrate that the PD-1/PD-L1
pathway plays a critical role in maintaining maternal immunological tolerance to the fetus
during pregnancy. Blockade of PD-1/PD-L1 signaling in murine models of pregnancy resulted in
an increased incidence of fetal loss but no fetal malformations; however, late onset
autoimmunity can occur in PD-1-deficient mice. Based on these findings, the potential risks of
administering penpulimab during pregnancy include increased rates of abortion or stillbirth and
an increased risk in offspring of developing immune-related disorders or altering the normal
immune response. As a result, the pharmacology/toxicology team recommends a warning for
embryo-fetal toxicity in the prescribing information. Based on a half-life of penpulimab of 23.9
days, females of reproductive potential are advised to use effective contraception during
treatment with PENPULIMAB-KCQX and for 4 months after the last dose. The Applicant did not

B. In Vivo Studies
Because pempulimab does not bind to mouse PD-1, male C57BL/6 mice were genetically
engineered to express a chimeric human/mouse PD-1 gene; these mice have a functional
human PD-1 with expression regulated by the mouse PD-1 promoter. The Applicant
investigated the in vivo antitumor activity of penpulimab in this human PD-1 knock-in
genetically engineered mouse model (HuGEMM) implanted subcutaneously with MC38 mouse
colon adenocarcinoma cells (Study E3174-B1701). Nivolumab (manufactured by Brystol-Myers)
was used as a comparator control. Intraperitoneal administration of 0.8 and 8 mg/kg
penpulimab twice a week for a total of 5 doses resulted in 74.1% and 54.5% TGI, respectively,
compared to the isotype control (FDA – Figure ). Pempulimab exhibited similar in vivo
antitumor activity as nivolumab. There were no mortalities, and body weights remained stable
during treatment.

5.5. Toxicology
5.5.1. General Toxicology
The Applicant’s Position:
In 6-week repeat-dose toxicity study, no apparent toxicity was observed in cynomolgus
monkeys following intravenous infusion of penpulimab at 4, 15, or 60 mg/kg once every two
weeks for 6 weeks. Treatment-related histopathological change of kidneys (increased cortical
tubular pigment or pigmented interstitial macrophages) was noted in some animals but no
impact on kidney functions. Pigment in the cortical tubular epithelium of the kidneys is not
reported as a common background finding in cynomolgus monkeys. In this study, there were no
apparent changes in clinical chemistry, urinalysis, or organ weights which would indicate an
impact of treatment on kidney function. There were also no other histopathological changes
associated with the pigment which were indicative of damage to the kidneys. These changes
were therefore considered not to be adverse. The no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL)
was considered to be 60 mg/kg.
In 13-week repeat-dose toxicity study, no apparent toxicity and histopathological change of
kidney was observed in cynomolgus monkeys following intravenous infusion of penpulimab at
4, 15, or 60 mg/kg once every two weeks for 13 weeks, the NOAEL was considered to be
60 mg/kg.
The FDA’s Assessment:
In general, FDA agrees with the Applicant’s assessment of the toxicology data. In the 6-week
repeat-dose toxicology study, clinical chemistry findings included a dose-dependent decrease in
total bilirubin and increase in creatine kinase levels at all dose levels in males, which were
present at the end of the recovery period. In addition to the kidney, as noted by the Applicant,
other target organs of toxicity in the 6-week study were the spleen (increased cellularity of the
red and white pulp), adrenal gland (cortical hypertrophy), parotid salivary gland (acinar cell
atrophy), and thymus (increased weight). Changes in the adrenal gland, spleen, and thymus
(females) were present at the end of the recovery period. Of the 30 monkey serum samples
tested, 19 were ADA-positive with an incidence of 63.33%.
In the 13-week toxicity study, histological findings included erythrophagocytosis and increased
cellularity in the lymph nodes (inguinal, mandibular, mesenteric), which were present at the
end of the recovery period. Limited findings may be reflective of ADA formation. Of the 30
monkey serum samples tested, 28 were ADA-positive with an incidence of 93.33%.

The Applicant’s Position:
Carcinogenicity studies were not conducted with penpulimab, which is consistent with its use in

use in other indications, an assessment of its carcinogenic potential may be warranted;

rodents.

The Applicant’s Position:
Fertility, embryonic fetal development or pre- and postnatal developmental toxicity studies
were not conducted with penpulimab. As described in ICH Guidance S9, fertility and early

studies on the pharmaceutical’s effect on reproductive organs were used as the basis of the
assessment of impairment of fertility. In the 6-week and 13-week repeat-dose toxicity studies,
there were no notable effects in the male and female reproductive organs.

Version date: January 2020 (ALL NDA/ BLA reviews)
Disclaimer: In this document, the sections labeled as “Data” and “The Applicant’s Position” are

Reference ID: 5577575

NDA/BLA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation- BLA 761258
Penpulimab
Embryo-fetal development toxicity studies were not conducted with penpulimab. Literature
data shows that a central function of the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway is to preserve pregnancy by
maintaining maternal immune tolerance to the fetus. Blockade of PD-L1 signaling has been
shown in murine models of pregnancy to disrupt tolerance to the fetus and to increase fetal
loss. There are potential reproductive risks when giving penpulimab during pregnancy,
including increased rates of miscarriage or stillbirth. Penpulimab is an IgG1 antibody drug with
high affinity to human FcRn, thus it is expected to cross the placenta during third-trimester
pregnancy in human, though the exposure of penpulimab in fetus under treatment dose level is
undetermined. Based on its mechanism of action, fetal exposure to penpulimab may increase
the risk of developing immune-mediated disorders or altering the normal immune response
and immune-mediated disorders have been reported in PD-1 knockout mice.
Pre- and postnatal toxicity studies were not conducted with penpulimab. As described in ICH
Guidance S9, pre- and postnatal toxicity toxicity study is not warranted for marketing of
pharmaceuticals for the treatment of patients with advanced cancer.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA agrees that dedicated reproductive and developmental toxicity studies are not needed to
support this BLA submission. To address the potential effects of penpulimab on embryo-fetal
development, the Applicant submitted an assessment of the potential reproductive toxicity of
penpulimab using a weight-of-evidence approach. FDA agreed in January 2021 that this
approach appeared reasonable.
The PD-1/PD-L1 pathway plays a critical role in maintaining maternal immunological tolerance
to the fetus during pregnancy (Guleria et al. 2005). PD-L1 is expressed in the human placenta
throughout pregnancy and at the maternal-fetal interface in fetal villous syncytiotrophoblasts
and extravillous cytotrophoblasts (Petroff et al. 2003). Blockade of PD-L1 signaling in murine
models of pregnancy disrupts tolerance to the fetus, resulting in increased fetal loss (Guleria et
al. 2005).
Penpulimab is a humanized IgG1 antibody, and human IgG is known to cross the placenta; thus,
penpulimab may be transmitted from the mother to the fetus. Based on its mechanism of
action and findings from murine models of pregnancy (Guleria et al. 2005), administration of
penpulimab is likely to disrupt the maintenance of normal pregnancy. Potential risks associated
with administration of penpulimab during pregnancy include increased rates of abortion and
stillbirth. In addition, as PD-1 knockout mice develop late onset autoimmune phenotypes
(Okazaki and Honjo 2007), fetal exposure to penpulimab may alter the normal immune
response or increase the risk of developing immune-related disorders. As inhibition of the PD1/PD-L1 pathway can lead to increased risk of immune-mediated rejection of the developing
fetus, resulting in fetal death, a warning for embryofetal toxicity is recommended for
PENPULIMAB-KCQX. Based on a half-life of approximately 24 days, females of reproductive

5.5.5. Other Toxicology Studies

Literature Based Assessment of Potential for Effects of Infection
(Previously reviewed by FDA)
While loss of PD-1 function enhances clearance of some tumors and viral infections, it increases
susceptibility to certain other pathogens such as tuberculosis in some animal models. PD-1deficient mice (C57BL/6) infected with Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) exhibited a decrease
in survival, which correlated with uncontrolled bacterial proliferation and a larger inflammatory
response in the lungs of PD-1-deficient mice compared with wild-type controls. Thus, PD-1
appears to be required to control infection and the inflammatory responses in the lungs of mice
infected with Mtb (Lazar-Molnar, et al. 2010); however, the pathogenesis of this observation
has not been clearly defined. In particular, it is unclear whether the decreased survival reflects
rampant bacterial growth resulting from an inability to mount appropriate antibacterial
responses and/or whether it is a failure to downregulate the immune reaction that leads to
massive tissue destruction and organ failure.
58
Version date: January 2020 (ALL NDA/ BLA reviews)
Disclaimer: In this document, the sections labeled as “Data” and “The Applicant’s Position” are
completed by the Applicant and do not necessarily reflect the positions of the FDA.
Reference ID: 5577575

NDA/BLA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation- BLA 761258
Penpulimab
In a recent publication, Kauffman et al. (2021) evaluated the role of PD-1 during Mtb infection
of rhesus macaques. Monkeys (~2 years old; males) were infected with 30-50 colony forming
units of fluorescently labeled Mtb into the right lower lung lobe. Tissue from Mtb-infected
monkeys was harvested 15–16 weeks post-infection and assessed for PD-1 expression using
flow cytometry. Additional Mtb-infected monkeys were intravenously infused with 10 mg/kg of
isotype control (DSPR4) or a primatized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody (n=6/group) at 2, 4, 6, 8,
10, and 13 weeks post-infection to determine the role of PD-1 during an Mtb infection. PET
scans and 18FDG (18F-fluoro-2-deoxy-D-glucose) uptake, granuloma size and number, and
colony forming units per granuloma were used to evaluate infection. Monkeys in both studies
were necropsied at 15–16 weeks post-infection. Treatment of Mtb-infected monkeys with an
anti-PD-1 antibody led to early euthanasia in one monkey due to severe pulmonary stress and
another monkey developed cachexia and showed elevated 18FDG uptake in the lungs but
survived until study termination. PD-1 expression in Mtb-infected monkeys occurred more
frequently on antigen specific CD4 and CD8 T cells in lung granulomas compared to other
tissues. Mtb-infected monkeys treated with an anti-PD-1 showed similar numbers of
granulomas compared to controls, but these were characterized as larger granulomas, with
increased 18FDG uptake and a higher bacterial load. The increased bacterial loads noted with
PD-1 blockade occurred primarily within the site of infection (pulmonary lymph nodes and
granulomas), suggesting it did not result in disseminated infection. The mechanism underlying
the increased bacterial loads after PD-1 blockade in Mtb infection are not clear, but IFN-γ and
TNF have been previously implicated. Evaluation of cytokines in granulomas of isotype and antiPD-1-treated monkeys indicated that IFN-γ, TNF, and IL-18 were the most dysregulated
cytokines and positively correlated with bacterial loads after PD-1 blockade. Data from
Kauffman et al. (2021) indicate that blockade of PD-1 with an anti-PD-1 antibody can
exacerbate Mtb infection in monkeys, consistent with previous findings noted in PD-1 knockout
mice infected with Mtb (Lazar-Molnar et al. 2010).

6. Clinical Pharmacology
6.1. Executive Summary
The FDA’s Assessment:
The Applicant seeks approval of penpulimab for the treatment of the following indications at
the following proposed recommended dosages:
•

In combination with either cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine for the first-line
treatment of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). The recommended dosage is penpulimab
200 mg administered via intravenous (IV) infusion every three weeks (Q3W).

•

As a single agent for the treatment of non-keratinizing NPC with diseases progression on or
after platinum-based chemotherapy and at least one prior line of therapy. The
recommended dosage is penpulimab 200 mg administered via IV infusion every two weeks
(Q2W).

The recommended dosage of penpulimab 200 mg IV Q2W as a single agent was selected from
the pivotal Study AK105-202, which was previously reviewed during the initial BLA review cycle.
The proposed dosage 200 mg Q2W was supported by the clinical benefit and safety profile from
Study AK105-202. The clinical pharmacology review found the proposed dosage acceptable
based on population PK (PPK), exposure response (E-R) and immunogenicity analyses.
(Reference ID: 5313694).
The recommended dosage of 200 mg IV Q3W in combination with chemotherapy (either
cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine) was reviewed in this submission. The primary
evidence of efficacy and safety was obtained from the pivotal study AK105-304, in which
patients were randomized (1:1) to receive either penpulimab 200 mg Q3W by IV infusion in
combination with chemotherapy or placebo in combination with chemotherapy.
The clinical pharmacology review addressed the following two key review issues:
ISSUE #1 – Is the proposed dosage acceptable?: The proposed dosage of penpulimab 200 mg
Q3W is acceptable for patients with NPC given the following considerations from Study
AK105-304:
•

The dosages of penpulimab 200 mg Q2W as a single agent and penpulimab 200 mg Q3W in
combination with chemotherapy showed comparable exposures based on PPK analysis. No
dosage adjustment is recommended for patients based on age, sex, race, body weight,
serum albumin, baseline LDH, baseline C-reactive protein, baseline ECOG score,

•

The E-R analysis for efficacy showed a flat relationship but is considered exploratory due to

•

immune-related adverse events (irAEs) and specific adverse events (AEs) including
decreased white blood cells, hypothyroidism, rash, and upper respiratory tract infections.
These AEs are not clinically significant due to comparable dose interruptions and
discontinuations between treatment arms in Study AK105-304.

ISSUE #2 – Is the observed immunogenicity acceptable?: The incidence of treatment emergent
anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) and neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) against penpulimab were 8.8%
(12/137) and 33% (4/12), respectively in the penpulimab arm of Study AK105-304. Although
observed trough concentrations (Ctrough) decreased by 47% in ADA positive patients enrolled in
Study AK105-304, ADAs or NAbs did not have a clinically significant effect on penpulimab
pharmacokinetics (PK). The PPK analysis showed <20% differences in the Geometric Mean
Ratios (GMRs) for clearance (CL), area under the curve at steady-state (AUCss), maximum
concentration at steady state (Cmax,ss) and minimum concentration at steady state (Cmin,ss).
The observed 47% decrease in Ctrough in Study AK105-304 is attributable to patient factors such
as weight and albumin, as the patients who tested positive and negative for ADA are not
randomized. The effect of ADAs on safety and efficacy cannot be determined due to low
numbers of ADA positive patients in Study AK105-304.

The proposed recommended dosage is 200 mg IV Q3W in combination with either

6.2. Summary of Clinical Pharmacology Assessment
6.2.1. Pharmacology and Clinical Pharmacokinetics
Data:
Penpulimab is a humanized immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) monoclonal antibody targeting
programmed cell death-1 (PD-1). Penpulimab binds specifically to human PD-1 with high affinity
62
Version date: January 2020 (ALL NDA/ BLA reviews)
Disclaimer: In this document, the sections labeled as “Data” and “The Applicant’s Position” are
completed by the Applicant and do not necessarily reflect the positions of the FDA.
Reference ID: 5577575

NDA/BLA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation- BLA 761258
Penpulimab
and competitively blocks the binding of PD-1 to its ligand programmed cell death-1 (PD-L1) and
programmed cell death ligand-2 (PD-L2), thereby relieving immunosuppression of T
lymphocytes, promoting the proliferation of lymphocytes and the secretion of related
cytokines, and ultimately recovering cytotoxic activities of T cells to block tumor growth.
Pharmacokinetic (PK) data of penpulimab were derived from 8 clinical studies. A total of 771
patients were included in the population PK analysis (PopPK), and 31 patients who underwent
intensive sampling were included in the non-compartmental PK analysis. The patients received
penpulimab at 1.0, 3.0 or 10.0 mg/kg Q2W, 200 mg Q2W or 200 mg Q3W. According to the
non-compartmental analysis (NCA), the Cmax and AUC0-14d increased relatively proportional
within the dose range of 1.0 mg/kg to 10.0 mg/kg.
Penpulimab is administered via IV infusion. Based on population PK (PopPK) model (n=771),
after single dose IV infusion of 200 mg, the terminal elimination half-life (t1/2) of penpulimab is
32.4 days. The mean (CV%) of volume of distribution was 10.2 L (43.5%). The mean (CV%) of CL
was 0.229 L/day (32.7%).
Steady state concentrations of penpulimab were reached by week 15 following 200 mg Q3W,
with accumulation ratios for Cmax and AUC of 1.53 and 2.10, respectively. The mode-predicted
means of Cmax,ss, Cavg,ss and Cmin,ss are 87.6 μg/mL, 45.5 μg/mL and 30.1 μg/mL, respectively. The
effective half-lives (t1/2eff) calculated based on Cmax and AUC were 13.6 days and 22.4 days,
respectively.
Receptor occupancy (RO) is an important measure of the in vivo biological activity of
penpulimab and also an important parameter underlying the determination of the
recommended dose in clinical studies. In the Phase Ia clinical study conducted in Australia
(AK105-101 study), patients with advanced solid tumors received penpulimab therapy (1, 3 and
10 mg/kg Q2W). PD-1 RO reached 80% to 100% starting from two days post-dose for all these
cohorts. No apparent correlation between RO value and dose level was noted.

The Applicant’s Position:
Penpulimab exhibited linear PK characteristics in patients who received penpulimab by IV
administration within the dose range of 1.0 mg/kg to 10.0 mg/kg. PopPK analysis indicated that
distribution of penpulimab was limited to the central vascular compartment, and with an
effective half-life of 22.4 days and mild accumulation upon repeat dosing.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position that the exposure to penpulimab increased dose
proportionally over the range of 1 mg/kg to 10 mg/kg after a single dose.

6.2.2. General Dosing and Therapeutic Individualization
6.2.2.1. General Dosing
Data:
In the Phase Ia dose-escalation trial, no DLT occurred at the highest dose cohort of 10.0 mg/kg
Q2W and no maximum tolerated dose (MTD) was explored, therefore the maximum
administered dose (MAD) for this study was 10.0 mg/kg Q2W. Phase Ia PK data showed a linear
relationship between exposure of penpulimab and dose over the dose range of 1.0 mg/kg Q2W
to 10.0 mg/kg Q2W. Receptor occupancy analysis showed 80% to 100% PD-1 receptor
occupancy starting on day 2 after administration. There was no significant difference in
receptor occupancy between 1.0, 3.0 and 10.0 mg/kg doses level. The efficacy results showed
anti-tumor activities at doses ranging from 1.0 mg/kg to 10.0 mg/kg Q2W. Since higher drug
concentrations can be obtained with the 3 mg/kg dosing regimen than with the 1 mg/kg dosing
regimen, this may ensure to achieve more stable blood concentrations after multiple doses for
better sustained receptor occupancy.
Results of study AK105-101 showed that, following IV administration of penpulimab 1.0, 3.0
and 10.0 mg/kg, Cmax and AUC(0-14d) increased proportionally with dose; the 90% confidence
interval (CI) of β values of AUC(0-14d) and Cmax was 0.676-1.15 and 0.844-1.13, respectively.
Based on population PK (PopPK) model (n=771), the PK parameters following single-dose IV
infusion of penpulimab 200 mg are as follows: the mean Cmax (CV%) was 57.6 μg/mL(19.5%), the
mean AUC(0-inf) (CV%) was 955 μg*day/mL(29.6%), the mean CL (CV%) was 0.229 L/day(32.7%),
the mean Vz (CV%) was 10.2 L(43.5%), and the mean terminal elimination half-life (t1/2) (CV%)
was 32.4 days(43.5%).
Following multi-dose administration of penpulimab 200 mg Q3W, the steady state was reached
by Week 15; the mode-predicted mean of Cmax,ss, Cavg,ss and Cmin,ss (CV%) are 87.6 μg/mL(21.1%),
45.5 μg/mL (29.1%) and 30.1 μg/mL(38.1%), respectively; the mean (CV%) accumulation ratios
for Cmax and AUC were 1.53 (12.6%) and 2.10 (19.4%), respectively. The effective halflives(t1/2eff) calculated based on Cmax and AUC were 13.6 days and 22.4 days, respectively.
The steady-state drug concentrations following administration of penpulimab 200 mg Q3W in
771 patients are simulated. In vitro studies indicated 0.5 µg/mL penpulimab was associated
with a receptor occupancy close to 90%. PopPK analysis showed that, with a penpulimab dose
of 200 mg Q3W, the steady-state trough concentration in more than 95% of patients was >10
μg/mL, which is 100-fold higher than those at which 80% of the receptors (0.1 µg/mL) could be
occupied or 20-fold higher than those at which 90%~100% of the receptors (0.5 µg/mL) could
be occupied.

A logistic regression analysis was performed to explore the exposure-efficacy (E-E) and

The Applicant’s Position:
The recommended dosage of penpulimab was 200 mg Q3W administered with intravenous
infusion (IV). Dose selection is based on the following considerations:
Safety:
●

In phase 1 dose-escalation phase, Penpulimab was well tolerated up to 10 mg/kg Q2W, no
DLT was observed.

●

In NPC population, Penpulimab (200 mg Q3W) in combination with chemotherapy, was safe
and tolerable.

●

E-R safety analysis indicated that no apparent correlation between exposure and incidence
of TEAE/TRAE (Grade 3+) in the wide dose range (1 - 10 mg/kg Q2W) with either
monotherapy or in combination therapy.

Efficacy:
●

Penpulimab 200 mg Q3W demonstrated notable clinical benefits in NPC population: the
median PFS was 9.6 months (95% CI:7.1, 12.5), compared to placebo of 7.0 months (95% CI:
6.9, 7.3).

●

E-R analysis suggested a relative flat exposure-response (ORR/DCR) curve and no apparent
difference in exposure between responders and non-responders.

PK/PD:
●

Penpulimab exhibited linear PK characteristics over large dose range (1-10 mg/kg Q2W) with
terminal half-life of 32.4 day.

●

No intrinsic/extrinsic factor had clinically meaningful effect on PK and exposures were similar
between Caucasian and Asian patients.

The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA generally agrees that the proposed recommended dosage of 200 mg IV Q3W is supported
by the observed clinical safety, efficacy, and PK/PD data from Study AK105-304.
FDA disagrees that the E-R analysis for efficacy is relatively flat and concludes that the E-R
analysis for efficacy is inconclusive given that the analysis only included one dose level.
FDA generally agrees that there appears to be no apparent correlation between the incidence
of most TEAEs and penpulimab exposure, but there is a positive correlation between exposure
and immune-related adverse events (irAEs) and some specific adverse events (AEs) including
decrease in white blood cells (WBC), hypothyroidism, rash, and upper respiratory tract
infections (Refer to Section 19.4.3.3). However, there were comparable dose interruptions
(77% penpulimab arm vs 71% placebo arm) and discontinuations (12% penpulimab arm vs 9%
placebo arm), and the relationship between exposure and irAEs and other AEs is likely not
clinically significant.
6.2.2.2. Therapeutic Individualization
Data:
Intrinsic factors that might have an impact on penpulimab PK were subjected to covariate
analysis by the PopPK model to identify main contributors to the PK variability.
Covariates investigated for their potential to influence penpulimab PK included age, body
weight (WT), creatinine clearance (CLcr), creatinine concentration (CR), total bilirubin (TBIL),
aspartate transaminase (AST), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), alanine aminotransferase (ALT),
lactic dehydrogenase (LDH), albumin (ALB), tumor size (TSIZEB), Eastern Cooperative Oncology
Group (BECOG) score, C-reactive protein (CRP) at baseline, tumor type (DIAG), sex, race, coadministration (COMBO) and total anti-drug antibody (TADA).
A two-compartment model with zero-order IV infusion and first-order elimination adequately
described penpulimab PK. The typical subject is a male Asian patient with NPC and negative
TADA, WT of 62.0 kg, ALB of 41.9 g/L, CRP of 9.55 mg/L, LDH of 214 IU/L, age of 55 years old,
and receiving penpulimab plus chemotherapy.
The final model included the effects of (i) WT, age, ALB, LDH, race, sex, and TADA on clearance
(CL); (ii) WT, ALB, SEX, COMBO and DIAG on volume of the central compartment (V1); (iii) CRP,
COMBO and DIAG on volume of the peripheral compartment (V2). None of the other covariates

Age:
Among the 771 patients included in the PopPK analysis, the median age was 55 years (range:
18-91 years). The results of the stepwise covariate model (SCM) indicated that age had a
statistically significant effect on CL of penpulimab. CL of penpulimab increased with age. This
increase in penpulimab CL ranged from -8.82% to +4.74% of the median CL estimate when age
increased from the 10% (34.0 years) to the 90% (70.0 years). However, comparison of modelpredicted steady state exposures (Cmax,ss, Cmin,ss, AUCss) indicated exposure ratios of less than
30%, suggesting that age has no clinically meaningful impact on penpulimab exposures.
Sex:
Females accounted for 25.6% (n=197), and males accounted for 74.4% (n=574). The CL and
apparent volume of distribution of central compartment V1 of penpulimab were 11.1% and
12.8% lower in females than in males with the same weight and conditions, indicating sex had a
statistically significant impact on CL and V1. However, comparison of model-predicted steadystate exposures (Cmax,ss, Cmin,ss, AUCss) indicated exposure ratios of less than 30%. Overall, the
impact of sex on PK exposure was not clinically significant.

Body weight:
The median weight was 62.0 kg (range: 32.0-113 kg). The SCM results showed that penpulimab
Volume of distribution of central compartment (V1 ) increased with CL and body weight. In a
patient with an extremely low weight (48.0 kg, 10% quantile) comparing to the patient with
median weight (62 kg), V1 and CL was 11.5% and 9.85% lower, respectively; In a patient with an
extremely high weight (79.4 kg ,90% quantile) comparing to the patient with median weight (62
kg), V1 and CL was 12.6% and 10.5% higher, respectively. Weight had a statistically significant
impact on CL and V1. However, comparison of model-predicted steady state exposures (Cmax,ss,
Cmin,ss, AUCss) indicated exposure ratios of less than 30%. Hence, it is considered that the impact
of weight on AUCSS, Cmax,SS and Cmin,SS was not clinically significant.
Renal impairment:
In accordance with the Guidance on Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal Function
released by FDA in 2024, renal impairment in the 771 patients included into the population PK
analysis set was graded by creatinine clearance (CLcr). The grading criteria and included
patients are summarized as follows. Normal renal function, CLcr ≥ 90 mL/min (n=405); mild
renal impairment: CLcr < 90 mL/min and CLcr ≥ 60 mL/min (n=301); moderate renal
impairment: CLcr < 60 mL/min and CLcr ≥ 30 mL/min (n=64); 1 patient with severe renal
impairment (CLcr < 30 mL/min) has been included.
Through PopPK covariate screening, it was found that the renal function related factor (CLcr)
did not have a statistically significant impact on population PK parameters of penpulimab.The
results showed that there was no significant difference in clearance between patients with mild
or moderate renal impairment and patients with normal renal function.
Data of penpulimab in patients with severe renal impairment are not adequate.
Hepatic impairment:
Hepatic impairment of the 771 patients included in PopPK analysis was graded by TBIL and AST.
Grading criteria and included patients are summarized as follows. Normal hepatic function:
TBIL<upper limit of normal (ULN) and AST<ULN(n=652); mild hepatic impairment: TBIL≤ULN and
AST>ULN or TBIL=1.0 to 1.5×ULN, regardless of AST (n=113); moderate hepatic impairment:
TBIL=1.5 to 3.0×ULN, regardless of AST(n=6); no patient with severe hepatic impairment
(TBIL>3.0×ULN, regardless of AST) has been included.
Through PopPK analysis covariate screening, it was found that the hepatic function related
factors (TBIL, AST) did not have a statistically significant impact on population PK parameters of
penpulimab. The results showed that there was no significant difference in clearance between

Tumor type:
Among the 771 patients included in PopPK analysis, there were 302 (39.2%) patients with

Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score:
Among the 771 patients included in PopPK analysis, there were 243 (31.5%) patients with a
baseline Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 0 and 528 (68.5%) patients with
an ECOG score of 1. Population PK covariate screening results showed that ECOG score did not
have a statistically significant impact on PK parameters of penpulimab.
Serum albumin (ALB):
Among the 771 patients included in PopPK analysis, the median albumin (ALB) was 41.9 g/L
(range: 22.0 - 67.7 g/L). Population PK covariate screening results showed that penpulimab CL
and V1 decreased with increase of ALB; Clearance (CL) of the patient with ALB at the 10%
quantile level (34.7 g/L) was 13.9% higher than CL of the patient with ALB at the median level;
CL of the patient with ALB at the 90% quantile (47.4 g/L) was 8.16% lower than CL of the patient
with ALB at the median level. the central compartment (V1) of the patient with ALB at the 10%
quantile level (34.7 g/L) was 5.92% higher than V1 of the patient with ALB at the median level;
V1 of the patient with ALB at the 90% quantile (47.4 g/L) was 3.69% lower than V1 of the patient
with ALB at the median level. Therefore, ALB had a statistically significant impact on CL and V1.
The geometric mean ratios of PK parameters (AUCSS, Cmax,SS, Cmin,SS) in patients with ALB at 10%
or 90% quantile levels versus the typical patient were between 0.8 and 1.1; namely, the
differences were less than 30%. Hence, the impact of ALB on AUCSS, Cmax,SS and Cmin,SS was not
clinically significant.

Impacts of extrinsic factors on PK:
Impacts of extrinsic factors (e.g., food, alcohol or smoking) on penpulimab PK have not been
assessed in this study.
Impacts of immunogenicity on PK:
If ADA to penpulimab were detected at any visit, the patient was classified as TADA-positive
immune response, otherwise as a TADA-negative immune response. Impacts of TADA on PK
parameters were analyzed by a PopPK analysis.
Among the 771 patients included in PopPK analysis, 235 patients (30.5%) were TADA positive,
and 536 patients (69.5%) were TADA negative. The SCM results indicated that TADA had a
statistically significant effect on CL of penpulimab.
Compared to TADA-negative patients, the CL of TADA-positive patients was 16.8% higher.
However, comparison of model-predicted steady state exposures (Cmax,ss, Cmin,ss, AUCss)
indicated exposure ratios of less than 30%, suggesting that TADA has no clinically meaningful
impact on penpulimab exposures .

6.3. Comprehensive Clinical Pharmacology Review
6.3.1. General Pharmacology and Pharmacokinetic Characteristics
Data:
The clinical pharmacology of Penpulimab has been studied in patients with malignant solid
tumors such as NPC or non-solid tumours such as cHL who received penpulimab by intravenous
infusion administration at dose range of 1 - 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks, or 200 mg every 2 or 3
weeks. Levels of serum penpulimab were measured using validated methods and the results
were used to evaluate PK parameters.
PK data of penpulimab were derived from 8 clinical studies. A total of 771 patients were
included into population PK analysis, and 31 patients who underwent intensive sampling into
non-compartmental PK analysis. The PK profile is outlined as follows:
Absorption
Penpulimab is administered via IV infusion, and the drug directly enters blood circulation.
Distribution
According to PopPK analysis, following administration of penpulimab 200 mg as a single IV
infusion, the mean (CV%) of volume of distribution was 10.2 L (43.5%).
Elimination
According to PopPK analysis, the mean (CV%) of CL was 0.229 L/day (32.7%). The effective half75

life (t1/2eff) was 22.4 days (27.4%), following IV infusion of 200 mg every 3 weeks.
Linearity/non-linearity
The exposure of penpulimab increase dose proportionally in the dose range of 1 to 10 mg/kg.
Steady state
According to PopPK analysis, the penpulimab concentration was approximate to the steady
state at Week 15 following IV infusion of penpulimab 200 mg Q3W, and the accumulation ratios
for Cmax and AUC were 1.53 and 2.10, respectively. The mean steady-state trough
concentration (CV%) was 30.1 μg/mL (38.1%).
Other PopPK analysis Results
A two-compartment model with zero-order IV infusion and first-order elimination adequately
described penpulimab PK. The typical subject is a male Asian patient with NPC and negative
TADA, WT of 62.0 kg, ALB of 41.9 g/L, CRP of 9.55 mg/L, LDH of 214 IU/L, age of 55 years old,
and receiving penpulimab plus chemotherapy.
According to PopPK analysis, body weight (32.0 to 113 kg), age (18 to 91 years), sex, race (White
and Asian), ADA, albumin (22.0 to 67.7g/L), C-reactive protein (0 to 328 mg/L), lactate
dehydrogenase (111 to 4450 IU/L), tumor types (NPC vs. other tumors) and co-administration

Penpulimab. However, these covariates did not have clinically meaningful effects on the steadystate exposures, thus no dose adjustment is required. Mild to moderate hepatic impairment or
mild to moderate renal impairment did not have significant impact on the CL and steady-state
exposures of Penpulimab, therefore no dose adjustment is required. There's no sufficient data
on patients with severe hepatic impairment or severe renal impairment.

Total of 720 patients included in the immunogenicity evaluation were treated with penpulimab
of 1, 3 and 10 mg/kg Q2W, or 200mg Q2W/Q3W (either monotherapy or combination therapy).
26.8% of patients developed treatment-emergent ADA (TEADA), and 7.9% of patients had
positive neutralizing antibody (Nab).

The Applicant’s Position:
The information from clinical studies contributing to the clinical pharmacology evaluation of
penpulimab was included in the submitted reports (Module 2.7.2 Summary of Clinical
Pharmacology, Module 5.3.3.5 Penpulimab PopPK and ER report). Penpulimab exhibited linear
PK(from dose 1.0 mg/kg to 10.0 mg/kg) with an effective half-life (t1/2eff) of 22.4 days and the
mean of CL was 0.229 L/day.
No dedicated clinical drug-drug interaction studies have been conducted in humans.
Penpulimab is a humanized monoclonal antibody, PK interactions with other drugs have not
been studied. As monoclonal antibodies are not metabolized by cytochrome P450 (CYP) or
other drug metabolizing enzymes, inhibition or induction of these enzymes by co-administered
medicinal products is not anticipated to affect the pharmacokinetics of penpulimab.
Overall, penpulimab administered by intravenous infusion at fixed 200mg Q3W regimen,
demonstrated a favorable benefit-risk profile for patients in the target population of recurrent
or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA agrees with the Applicant’s summary of the PK characteristics of penpulimab. Of the 137
evaluable patients in Study AK 105-304 with NPC who received penpulimab 200 mg IV Q3W,
8.8% (12/137) of patients tested positive for treatment emergent ADAs and 33% (4/12) of
patients for treatment emergent NAbs. The PPK analysis indicates that treatment emergent
ADA had no significant impact on penpulimab PK, with <20% differences in the GMRs for CL,
AUCss, Cmax,ss, and Cmin,ss. Although observed PK data showed a 47% decrease in Ctrough in ADA
positive patients, this is attributable to patient factors such as weight and albumin, as the
patients who tested positive and negative for ADA are not randomized.

6.3.2. Clinical Pharmacology Questions
6.3.2.1. Does the clinical pharmacology program provide supportive evidence of
effectiveness?
Yes, the clinical pharmacology program provides supportive evidence of penpulimab
effectiveness in patients in the target population of recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal
carcinoma.
Data:
For AK105-304 study, patients with recurrent or metastatic NPC were enrolled in the study.
Among the 286 patients included in the primary efficacy population, per the primary analysis of
BICR-assessed PFS based on RECIST v1.1, 80 (55.6%) subjects in AK105 group and 109 (74.1%)
subjects in placebo group had PD or died, median PFS of the two groups was 9.6 (95% CI: 7.1,
12.5) and 7.0 (95% CI: 6.9, 7.3) months, respectively. Compared with placebo group, median
PFS in AK105 group was 2.6 months longer, the risk of PD or death was reduced by 55%,
HR=0.45 (95% CI: 0.33, 0.62; P<0.0001). Per BICR’s assessment, the confirmed ORR or DCR for
AK105 group was 68.1% (95% CI: 59.8%, 75.6%) and 91.0% (95% CI: 85.1%, 95.1%), respectively.
To support the clinical efficacy observed with penpulimab dosed at 200mg Q3W regimen,
exposure-efficacy relationship was evaluated in NPC population (AK105-304 study), see
[Module 2.7.2, Section 3.3.1 and 3.3.2]. Univariate logistic regression analysis was conducted to
assess the relationship between penpulimab PK exposures and model-predicted ORR response
(CR/PR) or DOR response (CR/PR/SD). Results of E-R analysis suggested a relative flat exposureresponse (ORR/DCR) curve and no apparent difference in exposure between responders and
non-responders.
A total of 380 patients received penpulimab monotherapy at 1, 3, 10 mg/kg Q2W, or 200 mg
Q2W. There’s no significant dose or exposure-dependent increase in the incidence of TEAEs,
TRAEs or CTCAE Grade3+ AEs, and drug-related SAEs. A total of 391 patients received
penpulimab 200 mg Q3W in combination therapy. Similar to monotherapy, there was no
significant increase in TEAE/TRAE (Grade 3+) with increasing of PK exposure, while association
with irAE was found to be statistically significant. For AEs with incidence rate of 10% or higher,
white blood cell count decrease, hypothyroidism, rash and upper respiratory tract infection
were associated with higher exposure, consistent with common adverse events observed in this
population.
Overall, E-R safety analysis suggested a flat exposure-response relationships between
penpulimab exposure and most AEs in both monotherapy and combination therapy groups.
However, higher exposure levels may be associated with a slightly increased risk of irAEs and
some specific AEs.

The Applicant’s Position:
Penpulimab 200 mg Q3W showed notable clinical benefits in patients with NPC, and E-R
analysis suggested a relative flat exposure-response (ORR/DCR) curve and no apparent
difference in exposure between responders and non-responders. In NPC population,
Penpulimab (200 mg Q3W) in combination with chemotherapy was safe and tolerable. E-R
safety analysis indicated that no apparent correlation between exposure and incidence of
TEAE/TRAE (Grade 3+) in the wide dose range (1-10 mg/kg Q2W) with either monotherapy or in
combination therapy.
In conclusion, the interim analysis results of AK105-304 showed that the Phase 3 trial of
penpulimab combined with gemcitabine and cisplatin/carboplatin as the first-line treatment for
R/M NPC patients, met the preset primary endpoint of BICR-assessed PFS, and there was no
evidence of a detrimental effect on the long survival follow up. Compared with the current
standard chemotherapy regimen, penpulimab combined with gemcitabine and
cisplatin/carboplatin did not increase the toxicity of chemotherapy. Compared with similar
studies of other PD-1 inhibitors combined with chemotherapy as first-line treatment for R/M
NPC, the efficacy and safety were generally consistent, no new safety signal was identified.
Therefore, penpulimab combined with gemcitabine and cisplatin/carboplatin has a relatively
significant benefit-risk ratio in R/M NPC patients globally.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA does not agree that there is a flat E-R relationship for efficacy. FDA notes that as in the
penpulimab monotherapy analysis during the original BLA submission, the E-R analysis for
efficacy of penpulimab in combination with chemotherapy is inconclusive due to the limited
exposure range of penpulimab at one dose level.
6.3.2.2. Is the proposed dosing regimen appropriate for the general patient
population for which the indication is being sought?
Yes, penpulimab administered by intravenous infusion at 200mg Q3W regimen is appropriate
for the first-line treatment for R/M NPC patients when combined with gemcitabine and
cisplatin/carboplatin. The proposed dosing regimen is supported by the observed efficacy,
safety, and PK/PD data.
Data:
In the Phase Ia dose-escalation trial, no DLT occurred at the highest dose cohort of 10.0 mg/kg
Q2W and no MTD was explored, therefore the maximum administered dose(MAD) for this
study was 10.0 mg/kg Q2W. Phase Ia PK data showed a linear relationship between exposure of
penpulimab and dose over the dose range of 1.0 mg/kg Q2W to 10.0 mg/kg Q2W; receptor

Based on the final population PK model, serum penpulimab concentrations at each time point
within 42 weeks following multi-dose (200 mg Q3W) IV infusion in 771 patients were simulated.
Following multi-dose administration of penpulimab 200 mg Q3W, the steady state was reached
at about Week 15; the mode-predicted mean of Cmax,ss, Cavg,ss and Cmin,ss (CV%) are 87.6
μg/mL(21.1%), 45.5 μg/mL (29.1%) and 30.1 μg/mL(38.1%), respectively; the mean
accumulation ratios for Cmax and AUC (CV%) were 1.53 (12.6%) and 2.10 (19.4%), respectively.
The effective half-lives(t1/2eff) calculated based on Cmax and AUC were 13.6 days and 22.4 days,
respectively.

Data:
The population PK profile of penpulimab could be described using a two-compartment model
with zero-order IV infusion and first-order elimination. Covariate analysis showed that the
impacts of age, body weight, ALB, LDH, race, TADA and sex on CL and impacts of body weight,
ALB, combination therapy, tumor type and sex on V1 were statistically significant, impacts of
CRP, combination therapy and tumor type on V2 were statistically significant, but these factors
were not clinically significant.

and Asian), ADA, albumin (22.0 to 67.7g/L), C-reactive protein (0 to 328 mg/L), lactate

(monotherapy vs. combination therapy) were identified as significant covariates affecting PK of
Penpulimab. However, these covariates did not have clinically meaningful effects on the steadystate exposures, thus no dose adjustment is required. Mild to moderate hepatic impairment or
mild to moderate renal impairment did not have significant impact on the CL and steady-state
exposures of Penpulimab, therefore no dose adjustment is required. There's no sufficient data
on patients with severe hepatic impairment or severe renal impairment.

6.3.2.4. Are there clinically relevant food-drug or drug-drug interactions, and what is
the appropriate management strategy?
No, penpulimab is intended for intravenous infusion administration; therefore, food-drug
interactions are not expected.
The Applicant’s Position:
Penpulimab is intended for intravenous infusion administration; therefore, food-drug
interactions are not expected.
Penpulimab is a humanized monoclonal antibody, and PK interactions with other drugs have
not been studied. As monoclonal antibodies are not metabolized by cytochrome P450 (CYP) or
other drug metabolizing enzymes, inhibition or induction of these enzymes by co-administered
medicinal products is not anticipated to affect the pharmacokinetics of penpulimab.
Penpulimab belongs to a class of drugs called immune checkpoint inhibitors. Because the
mechanism of action of this class of drugs is to block inhibitory signal that prevents activation of
T cells there is a potential that these drugs may cause immune mediated adverse drug reaction.
Withhold or permanently discontinue penpulimab depending on severity. In general, if
penpulimab requires interruption or discontinuation, administer systemic corticosteroid
therapy (1 mg to 2 mg/kg/day prednisone or equivalent) until improvement to Grade 1 or less.
Upon improvement to Grade 1 or less, initiate corticosteroid taper and continue to taper over
at least 1 month. Consider administration of other systemic immunosuppressants in patients
whose immune-mediated adverse reactions are not controlled by corticosteroid therapy.

8. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation
8.1. Review of Relevant Individual Trials Used to Support Efficacy
8.1.1. Study AK105-304
Trial Design
The Applicant’s Description:
AK105-304 is a randomized, double-blind, multi-center phase III clinical study to compare the
efficacy and safety of penpulimab combined with chemotherapy and placebo combined with
chemotherapy in the first-line treatment of R/M NPC.
Approximately 278 subjects were planned to be enrolled in this study. The subjects were
randomized in a 1:1 ratio to the 2 treatment groups, stratified by stages of disease (primary
metastases vs. recurrent), ECOG (0 vs. 1), and liver metastasis (present vs. absent):
Arm A (experimental arm): Penpulimab+ gemcitabine + cisplatin/carboplatin, every 3 weeks
(Q3W) for up to 6 cycles, followed by penpulimab monotherapy Q3W.
Arm B (control arm): Placebo+ gemcitabine + cisplatin/carboplatin, Q3W for up to 6 cycles,
followed by placebo monotherapy Q3W.
In each arm, carboplatin was selected as a replacement of cisplatin at the discretion of
investigator prior to randomization. After randomization, change of chemotherapy regimen was
not allowed during the treatment period. Subjects received up to 6 cycles of penpulimab or
placebo combined with chemotherapy, followed by penpulimab or placebo monotherapy Q3W
as maintenance treatment until lack of clinical benefit as judged by the investigator
(comprehensive judgment by the investigator based on RECIST v1.1 imaging assessment and
clinical condition), intolerable toxicity, completion of 24 months of treatment, or other criteria
for discontinuation outlined in the protocol, whichever occurred first.
The study consisted of a screening period (up to 28 days from the signing of the informed
consent form to the first dose of study treatment), a treatment period (including on-treatment
visits and an end-of-treatment visit), and a follow-up period (including a safety follow-up visit, a
disease progression follow-up visit, and survival follow-up visits). Subjects underwent a
screening evaluation within 28 days before the first dose to confirm eligibility. Tumor specimens
(tumor tissue samples either archived or freshly obtained) were collected from subjects during
the screening period.
Regular tumor response assessments were performed for all subjects, with PFS evaluated by
BICR based on RECIST v1.1 as the primary response variable. Subjects underwent a tumor
assessment every 6 weeks (±7 days) for the first 54 weeks after the first dose of study
