treatment, and every 9 weeks (±7 days) thereafter until radiographic progression or loss of
clinical benefit (whichever occurs later), or the start of new antitumor therapy, or lost to followup, or death, or withdrawal of consent, or study closure, whichever occurred first.
If any radiographic disease progression was confirmed by BICR (based on RECIST v1.1), the
treatment assignment was unblinded for the subject. The subjects could receive open-label
penpulimab monotherapy (200 mg, administered on Day 1 of each cycle, Q3W) until intolerable
toxicity, lack of clinical benefit as judged by the investigator, or completion of 24 months of
treatment, or study termination by the sponsor, whichever occurred first.
Subjects in Arm A were allowed to continue open-label treatment with penpulimab
monotherapy beyond radiographic disease progression if, in the opinion of the investigator, the
subject would benefit from continued treatment and if other criteria are met as outlined in the
protocol.
Subjects in Arm B had the opportunity to crossover to open-label treatment with penlulimab
monotherapy after radiographic disease progression (confirmed by BICR) if, in the opinion of the
investigator, the subject would benefit from treatment with penpulimab and if other criteria
were met as outlined in the protocol.
Adverse events (AEs) of each subject were recorded until 30 days after the last dose of study
treatment (either penpulimab/placebo or chemotherapy) or the initiation of other antitumor
therapy, whichever occurred first. Serious adverse events (SAEs) were recorded until 90 days
after the last dose of study treatment (including chemotherapy) or the initiation of other
antitumor therapy, whichever occurred first. Immune-related AEs (irAEs) were recorded until 90
days after the last dose of penpulimab (regardless of initiation of other antitumor therapy).
Survival assessment was performed every 3 months (±7 days) after the last dose to collect
survival and subsequent antitumor therapy information.

particular application by the FDA review team and was communicated to the Applicant during

email communications on April 17, 2024, and April 19, 2024. See FDA’s assessment under

Study Endpoints
The Applicant’s Description:
•
•
•

Primary Efficacy Endpoint: progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded
independent center review (BICR) based on Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumor,
version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1).
Key Secondary Efficacy Endpoints: overall survival (OS)
Other Secondary Endpoints:
1) BICR-assessed ORR, DoR, and DCR based on RECIST v1.1.
2) Investigator-assessed PFS, ORR, DoR, and DCR based on RECIST v1.1.
3) Safety assessment: incidence and severity of adverse events (AEs) and serious
adverse events (SAEs), and clinically significant laboratory abnormalities.
4) PK profile: serum drug concentrations of penpulimab in individual subjects at
different time points after penpulimab administration.
5) Immunogenicity: number and percentage of subjects with detectable anti-drug
antibody (ADA).
6) Health-related quality of life (HRQoL): the European Organization for Research and
Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Core 30 (EORTC QLQ-C30) and
EORTC QLQ-H&N43.
7) PD-L1 expression in tumor samples, and the correlation between PD-L1 expression
and efficacy.
8) Blood EBV level at baseline and changes from baseline after administration of study
drugs, and correlation between blood EBV level and efficacy.

The FDA’s Assessment:
In general, FDA agrees with the Applicant’s description of the study endpoints with the
exception that DCR was considered to be an exploratory endpoint.

Definition of Key Analysis Sets
•
Intention-to-treat (ITT) set:
ITT set included all randomized subjects. Subjects were analyzed according to the treatment to
which they were randomized. The ITT set was used for the disposition of subjects,
demographics, baseline characteristics and primary efficacy analysis.
•
Safety Set (SS)
SS included all randomized subjects who received at least one dose of the study drug. Subjects
were analyzed according to the treatment that they actually received. The SS was used for drug
exposure and safety analysis.
•
Pharmacokinetics Set (PKS)
PKS included all randomized subjects who received at least one dose of penpulimab and had at
least one valid post-dose serum concentration data.
•

Immunogenicity Set (IMS)

For the penpulimab plus chemotherapy group, IMS included all randomized subjects who
received at least one dose of the penpulimab and had at least one pre-dose immunogenicity
assessment and one post-dose immunogenicity assessment.For the placebo plus chemotherapy
group, it included all subjects who entered the crossover treatment phase and received at least
one dose of penpulimab, and had at least one pre-dose immunogenicity assessment before the
crossover treatment and one post-dose immunogenicity assessment.
•
Crossover Treatment Set (CTS)
CTS included subjects of the control group who received AK105 at least once during the
crossover treatment phase.
The FDA’s Assessment:
The proposed sample size of 278 for Study AK105-304 was based on PFS. As of protocol version
2.1, dated August 31, 2022, the Applicant had proposed to enroll 218 (78%) patients in China
and 60 (22%) from outside of Asia. As of the data cut-off date of April 29, 2024, the study had
enrolled 291 patients of whom only 11 (3.8%) patients were enrolled outside of Asia. Based on
version 2.1 of the statistical analysis plan, dated June 17, 2024, assuming a median PFS of 7
months in the placebo arm and 10.8 months in the penpulimab arm, 222 events would provide
89% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.65 at a 2-sided level of significance of 0.05. The accrual
duration for the study was 28 months with a follow-up of an additional 6 months. The annual
dropout rate was assumed to be 5%. The primary analysis was a stratified log-rank test based
on the ITT population.
In protocol version 2.2 and in statistical analysis plan version 1.1, submitted to the FDA on
September 16, 2022, one interim analysis for PFS was proposed at 155 (70%) events for
efficacy, which was considered reasonable at that time by the review team. However, in the
91
Version date: January 2020 (ALL NDA/ BLA reviews)
Disclaimer: In this document, the sections labeled as “Data” and “The Applicant’s Position” are
completed by the Applicant and do not necessarily reflect the positions of the FDA.

NDA/BLA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation- BLA 761258

briefing document for the pre-BLA meeting, the Applicant stated that according to a data
transfer from an imaging vendor, 172 PFS events had been observed at that time across the
treatment and placebo arms and that the Applicant projected an immediate data cutoff date
would result in 190 (86%) PFS events for the interim analysis. In an email communication dated
April 17, 2024, the Applicant clarified that the study had enrolled 280 patients in China to
adhere to Chinese regulatory requirements and that the Applicant had planned to include the
first 218 patients from China in the efficacy population for the marketing application in the US
and that the projected 155 PFS events would be based on those 218 patients from China, along
with 60 patients from outside of Asia. The Applicant stated that substantial challenges were
experienced during patient enrollment outside of Asia due to the approval of toripalimab, the
conduct of the trial during the COVID-19 epidemic period, and the rarity of NPC outside of Asia.
The Applicant also stated that patients with NPC in the U.S in the first-line setting could be
prescribed immunotherapies, which would make patients less willing to participate in a
randomized clinical trial with a 50% chance of receiving chemotherapy only in the first line
treatment setting. Hence, the Applicant proposed to include all 280 patients from China in the
efficacy population for the marketing application in the US. The Applicant further stated that
this proposed change in the efficacy population required FDA's concurrence prior to the
conduct of a formal analysis and therefore, the Applicant did not conduct the PFS interim
analysis based on 155 events and the number of events had overrun the prespecified number
of events at the time of the pre-BLA meeting. The Applicant also stated that the 222 events
prespecified for the final analysis of PFS was expected to be reached on January 10, 2025. The
review team informed the Applicant that a PFS interim analysis based on 190 events could be
acceptable for a marketing application in the US. Consequently, the statistical analysis plan for
Study AK105-304 was updated and version 2.1 dated June 17, 2024, reflected these proposed
changes to the PFS interim analysis at 190 (86%) events. In this version, the Applicant stated
that the efficacy boundaries at the interim and final analysis of PFS would be calculated based
on the O’Brien-Fleming boundaries using the observed information fraction. The actual PFS
interim analysis, based on the data cut-off date of April 29, 2024, was conducted based on 189
(85%) events. Based on O’Brien-Fleming boundaries, the 2-sided p-value boundary at the
interim analysis of PFS was 0.030.
The study was also designed to test OS. Assuming a median OS of 29 months in the placebo arm
and 44.6 months in the penpulimab arm, 172 deaths would provide 80% power to detect a
hazard ratio of 0.65 at a 2-sided level of significance of 0.05. Two formal interim analyses were
proposed, at 103 (60%) deaths and at 138 (80%) deaths. Additionally, if PFS was statistically
significant at the interim analysis, the Applicant proposed to spend a 2-sided nominal alpha of
0.0001 for a descriptive analysis of OS at the time of the primary PFS analysis. Efficacy
boundaries would be calculated based on the observed information fraction using the O’BrienFleming boundary method. The Applicant proposed a hierarchical testing strategy where PFS
would be tested first at a 2-sided alpha of 0.05, and OS would be tested only if PFS was
statistically significant.

Patient Disposition
Data:
The study was conducted from August 16, 2021 (the first subject signed the ICF) to April 29,
2024 (data cutoff) across 36 sites in China and 10 sites in ex-Asia countries, including 2 in U.S., 1
in Canada and 7 in Brazil.
As shown in Applicant – Table 8, a total of 410 subjects were screened, and 291 subjects were
randomized, including 144 in AK105 group and 147 in placebo group. Of these, 11 were ex-Asia
patients from U.S., Canada, and Brazil. All except 3 subjects received study drugs.
Among all the subjects enrolled in the study, by the data cutoff date, 259 (89.0%) subjects
discontinued from the assigned treatment, with 124 (86.1%) in AK105 group and 135 (91.8%) in
placebo group. In placebo group, 68 (46.3%) subjects crossed over to receive AK105
monotherapy after progressed on the initially assigned treatment. One hundred and four
(35.7%) subjects had completed the study (49 [34.0%] in AK105 group, 55 [37.4%] in placebo
group).

The Applicant’s Position:
AK105-304 was first initiated in China in August 2021. To reflect the global distribution of NPC,
especially to represent the NPC population in the U.S. in line with FDA’s recommendation,
Akeso originally planned to enroll 60 patients outside of China. However, despite tremendous
efforts Akeso has made to complete enrollment outside of China, we have been experiencing
extreme challenges during the enrollment period. Among the three-year arduous efforts, we
contacted a total of 234 ex-Asia sites and only initiated 19 sites in the US, Canada, Brazil and
Australia. Up until September 18, 2024, we have enrolled a total of 16 patients outside of
China, including 3 in the US, 6 in Canada, and 7 in Brazil. 11 subjects from ex-Asia countries
were included in this analysis (as of Aprial 29, 2024).
As of 29 April 2024, compared with AK105 group, more subjects in placebo group had
completed the study treatment assigned at randomization (86.1% vs 91.8%). The most common
reason for discontinuation of study treatment in both groups was PD. 68 (34.5%) in placebo
group crossed over to receive AK105 monotherapy after BICR confirmed radiographic PD.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA agrees with the Applicant’s description of patient disposition for Study AK105-304.
Substantially more patients in the placebo arm (71%) discontinued treatment due to
radiographic disease progression, as compared to the penpulimab arm (43%).

The Applicant’s Position:
The baseline demographic characteristics were well-balanced between AK105 group and
placebo group. The racial distribution in AK105-304 is similar to that in the KEYNOTE-122 study
and probably represents a reasonable racial characteristic of a global trial in NPC. On the other
hand, JUPITER-02, the study used for FDA approval of toripalimab, exclusively enrolled patients
from Asia countries.
The FDA’s Assessment:
In general, FDA agrees with the Applicant’s description of patient demographics for Study
AK105-304. In the penpulimab arm, 10% of patients were 65 years or older, as compared to
3.4% of patients in the placebo arm. Otherwise, the demographics were well-balanced between
the treatment arms. As of the data cut-off date of April 29, 2024, the study had enrolled 291
patients of whom only 11 (3.8%) patients were enrolled outside of Asia, specifically in the US,
Canada, and Brazil. Otherwise, the demographics appear to be comparable between the
treatment arms.
Since Study AK105-304 was conducted primarily in China, with 96% of the patients enrolled in
China, the patient population may not be representative of the US population of patients with
NPC. A postmarketing commitment (PMC) will be issued to better characterize the safety and
efficacy of penpulimab plus chemotherapy in a patient population whose demographic and
disease characteristics are more representative of the population of U.S. patients with NPC. See
Section 13 on Postmarketing Commitments for additional details.

The Applicant’s Position:
The population treated in AK105-304 were managed according to the standard of care for
patients with NPC in the US. In ITT population, the majority of patients had metastatic disease
(80.1%); 45.6% had liver metastases. The histological type was mostly non-keratinizing
undifferentiated squamous cell carcinoma (76.6%), followed by non-keratinizing differentiated
squamous cell carcinoma (19.2%). Of the 11 subjects enrolled from ex-Asia countries, the
disease stage at enrollment was mainly recurrent NPC (72.7%), and 27.3% was primary
metastasis. The majority of subjects had distant metastases (63.6%), of which lung metastases
was most common (45.5%). The histological type was mostly non-keratinizing differentiated
squamous cell carcinoma (54.5%), followed by non-keratinizing undifferentiated squamous cell
carcinoma (45.5%). Prior to study entry, radiotherapy or concurrent chemoradiation was
administered to all of those with recurrent disease.
The FDA’s Assessment:

whereas the correct ECOG score for that patient was 0 per electronic data capture (EDC).

Treatment Compliance, Concomitant Medications, and Rescue Medication Use
Data:
Treatment Compliance
Penpulimab was adminstered intravenously, and each infusion was documented. Subjects who
had AK105 interruption or permanently discontinued due to AEs were disscussed in Section
8.2.4.3 and 8.2.4.4.
Concomitant Medications
A total of 144 (100.0%) subjects in AK105 group and 144 (98.0%) subjects in placebo group had
at least one concomitant medication. The most commonly used (≥50%) drug types were
antiemetics and antinauseants, immunostimulants, drugs for acid related disorders, blood
substitutes and perfusion solutions, corticosteroids for systemic use, antianemic preparations,
bile and liver therapy, vitamins, and diuretics. Those frequently used concomitant medications
were mainly used for pre-treatment of chemotherapy, as well as for the management of
common chemotherapy complications such as nausea, vomiting, and hematological toxicity.

The use of concomitant medications did not affect the efficacy or safety of penpulimab.

FDA agrees with Applicant’s position.

To assess the robustness of the primary endpoint of this study, the following sensitivity
analyses were conducted for BICR-assessed PFS:
Sensitivity analysis 1: The unstratified log-rank test and unstratified Cox proportional hazards
regression model was performed to compare PFS time between two groups, HR=0.53 (95% CI:
0.40, 0.71), P<0.0001. The results were consistent with the primary analysis.
Sensitivity analysis 2: For the stratified analysis, the stratification factors were stage of disease
at study entry (primary metastases vs. recurrent), ECOG score (0 vs. 1), liver metastases
(present vs. absent) and investigator’s choice of chemotherapy regimens (carboplatin vs.
cisplatin) all obtained from the EDC instead of randomization system (IWRS). The results
(HR=0.45; 95% CI: 0.33, 0.63; P<0.0001) were consistent with the primary analysis.
Sensitivity analysis 3: Subject who has experienced radiological PD or death right after missing
two or more consecutive tumor assessments were considered as progressed at the time of PD
or death, whichever occurs first. The results of this analysis (HR=0.47; 95% CI: 0.34, 0.64;
P<0.0001) were similar to those of the primary analysis.
Sensitivity analysis 4: Subject who had initiated a new anticancer therapy before radiological PD
or death were considered as progression at the time of starting the new anticancer therapy.

inhibitors (with the caveats of cross-study comparison). The PFS results assessed by BICR and
investigator were consistent. In the subgroup analysis, PFS benefits of AK105 were observed

across all subgroups (Age,

The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA’s stratified analysis of PFS did not include the stratification factor of investigator’s choice of
chemotherapy (cisplatin vs. carboplatin) as it was not a stratification factor originally
considered at the time of randomization. Additionally, only 2.4% of all randomized patients
received carboplatin which in turn resulted in sparse strata. FDA’s analysis based on the data
cut-off date of April 29, 2024, without using the above-mentioned stratification factor yielded
results that were numerically identical to that of the Applicant’s. This also indicated that the
stratification factor of investigator’s choice of chemotherapy had minimal effect on the primary
analysis of PFS. FDA’s sensitivity analyses that excluded the stratification factor of investigator’s
choice of chemotherapy also yielded results that were numerically identical to the Applicant’s
analysis.

68 (46.3%) subjects in placebo group had crossed over to receive AK105 monotherapy after PD,
which was explicitly allowed by design. An analysis based on the ITT principle will lead to a
biased estimate of the true treatment effect and will likely underestimate the AK105 group's
true survival benefit. Therefore, to investigate the impact of the existence of such a high
percentage of crossover and to correct for the potential bias in the primary analysis, three
commonly used statistical methods for correcting treatment-switching are considered as
sensitivity analyses: Rank Preserving Structural Failure Time (RPSFT) model, Inverse Probability
of Censoring Weighting (IPCW) method and two-stage Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) model.
After adjusting for potential bias in OS caused by the crossovers, the trend of OS benefit
became more evident, with an HR of 0.62 (0.41, 0.94) by RPSFT model, 0.75 (0.43, 1.30) by
IPCW method, and 0.78 (0.52, 1.17) by two-stage AFT model (Applicant – Table 14).

Other secondary endpoints
Investigator-assessed PFS
Per investigator assessment, 78 (54.2%) subjects in AK105 group and 112 (76.2%) subjects in
placebo group had PD or died, the median PFS was 12.3 (95% CI: 9.7, 14.6) and 7.2 (95% CI: 7.0,
8.3) months in the two groups, respectively. Compared with placebo group, AK105 group
reduced the risk of progression or death by 56% (HR=0.44, 95% CI: 0.32, 0.60; P<0.0001) based
on the stratified log-rank test. These results were consistent with those of BICR-assessed PFS.
BICR-assessed ORR/DCR
Per BICR assessment, 26 (18.1%) subjects in AK105 group and 13 (8.8%) subjects in placebo
group had confirmed CR; 72 (50.0%) subjects in AK105 group and 81 (55.1%) in placebo group
had confirmed PR. The ORR for the two groups was 68.1% (95% CI: 59.8%, 75.6%) and 63.9%
(95% CI: 55.6%, 71.7%), respectively. The DCR for the two groups was 91.0% (95% CI: 85.1%,
95.1%) and 91.8% (95% CI: 86.2%, 95.7%), respectively.
Investigator-assessed ORR/DCR
Per investigator assessment, 11 (7.6%) subjects in AK105 group and 4 (2.7%) subjects in placebo
group had confirmed CR, and 84 (58.3%) subjects in AK105 group and 80 (54.4%) subjects in
placebo group had confirmed PR. The ORRs for the two groups were 66.0% (95% CI: 57.6%,
73.7%) and 57.1% (95% CI: 48.7%, 65.3%), respectively. The DCR for the two groups was 91.0%
(95% CI: 85.1%, 95.1%) and 91.2% (95% CI: 85.4%, 95.2%), respectively.

The Applicant’s Position:
Median OS has not yet been reached for either group, and the OS data is immature. Since this
study began on August 25, 2021, the therapeutic landscape for advanced NPC has changed
considerably, especially with the approval of immune checkpoint inhibitors. To maximize
patients' clinical benefits, by design, this study allows patients in placebo group to receive
AK105 treatment after PD. 73 (50.7%) subjects in AK105 group and 107 (72.8%) subjects in
placebo group received subsequent anti-tumor therapies. Specifically, 68 (46.3%) subjects
in placebo group crossed over to receive the same treatment as AK105 group after PD, and
42 (28.6%) subjects received other anti-PD-1 therapies. Furthermore, more subjects in
placebo group (60 [40.8%]) received two or more types of systemic anti-tumor treatment
sequences or combinations (e.g., targeted therapy, chemotherapy, and other
immunotherapy) compared to AK105 group (39 [27.1%]). After adjusting for potential bias
in OS caused by the crossovers, the sensitivity analyses showed that the HR adjusted for
crossover effects ranged from 0.62 to 0.78. The lowest corrected HR, 0.62, was comparable to
the HR observed for toripalimab in the JUPITER-02 study.
The FDA’s Assessment:
At the time of the BLA submission, the Applicant provided an analysis of OS based on the data
cut-off date of April 29, 2024, when 97 (56%) deaths were observed in 291 enrolled patients.
This was a descriptive analysis of OS conducted at the time of the PFS interim analysis.
According to the SAP, the first formal interim analysis for OS (OS IA1) was expected to be
conducted at 103 deaths (60% information fraction of pre-specified OS events for the final
analysis). On January 23, 2025, FDA requested that the Applicant provide the results of OS IA1,
and the results was submitted to the FDA based on a data cut-off date of January 24, 2025. At
the time of the first OS interim analysis, the study had enrolled 296 patients, with the additional
five patients being enrolled outside of China. Of these five additional patients, three were
already under screening at the time of the pre-BLA meeting. The first interim analysis was
conducted at 121 (70%) events, instead of the prespecified 103 (60%) events. Based on the preBLA meeting documents, the Applicant had projected that 103 deaths would be observed by
January 10, 2025. It appears that deaths accrued faster than the Applicant’s projection.
Additionally, the Applicant also stated that an analysis at 60% information fraction would not
be very informative, given that a descriptive OS analysis was conducted at 56% information
fraction. FDA’s analysis of OS did not include investigator’s choice of chemotherapy as a
stratification factor for analysis. The following table provides FDA’s analysis of OS at 70%
information fraction, based on the data cut-off date of January 24, 2025. OS was not statistically
significant at the first interim analysis.

8.1.5. Integrated Assessment of Effectiveness
Data:
As of data cutoff date for this interim analysis, the median follow-up time was 19.1 months (range:
0.0, 31.5), penpulimab combined with gemcitabine and cisplatin/carboplatin significantly
improved PFS in the first-line treatment of R/M NPC, as compared to gemcitabine and
cisplatin/carboplatin alone. The key efficacy outcomes are summarized as follows:
Primary Endpoint BICR-assessed PFS:



o

Primary analysis: 80 (55.6%) subjects in AK105 group and 109 (74.1%) subjects in placebo
group had PD or died, and the median PFS was 9.6 (95% CI: 7.1, 12.5) and 7.0 (95% CI:
6.9, 7.3) months, respectively. Compared with placebo group, AK105 group reduced the
risk of PD or death by 55% (HR=0.45, 95% CI: 0.33, 0.62; P<0.0001). The study crossed
the O'Brien-Fleming boundary for this PFS interim analysis (2-sided P-value boundary is
0.030 based on 189 PFS events).

o

Sensitivity analysis per FDA request: Included only the first 218 Asian subjects and all 11
ex-Asia subjects, 65 (56.5%) subjects in AK105 group and 83 (72.8%) subjects in placebo
group had PD or died, and the median PFS was 8.4 (95% CI: 7.0, 12.5) and 7.0 (95% CI:
6.9, 7.2) months, respectively. Compared with placebo group, AK105 group reduced the
risk of PD or death by 52%, HR=0.48 (95% CI: 0.33, 0.68; P<0.0001). The results of this
sensitivity analysis and the primary analysis were consistent.

Key Secondary Endpoint OS:



o

Since PFS reached statistical significance, as planned in the SAP, a descriptive analysis
of OS was conducted with a nominal α of 0.0001. A total of 97 OS events were
observed, with 48 from AK105 group and 49 from placebo group with an HR of 0.94
(95% CI: 0.63, 1.40). 24-month survival rate was 66.3% in AK105 group and 61.9% in
placebo group. Median OS has not yet been reached for either group, and the OS data
is immature.

o

68 (46.3%) subjects in placebo group had crossed over to receive AK105 monotherapy
after PD, which was explicitly allowed by design. Three sensitivity analyses were
conducted via the commonly used methods for correcting crossover effects: Rank
Preserving Structural Failure Time (RPSFT) model, Inverse Probability of Censoring
Weighting (IPCW) method and two-stage Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) model. After

Penpulimab
adjusting for potential bias in OS caused by the crossovers, the trend of OS benefit
became more evident, with an HR of 0.62 (0.41, 0.94) by RPSFT model, 0.75 (0.43, 1.30)
by IPCW method, and 0.78 (0.52, 1.17) by two-stage AFT model.
Other Secondary Endpoints:



o

Investigator-assessed PFS: 78 (54.2%) subjects in AK105 group and 112 (76.2%) subjects
in placebo group had PD or died, and the median PFS was 12.3 (95% CI: 9.7, 14.6) and
7.2 (95% CI: 7.0, 8.3) months, respectively. Compared with placebo group, AK105 group
reduced the risk of progression or death by 56% (HR=0.44, 95% CI: 0.32, 0.60; P<0.0001).

o

BICR-assessed response: the confirmed ORR for AK105 group and placebo group was
68.1% (95% CI: 59.8%, 75.6%) and 63.9% (95% CI: 55.6%, 71.7%), respectively. The
median DoR for the two groups was 9.8 (95% CI: 7.0, 17.5) and 5.7 (95% CI: 5.5, 6.7)
months, respectively, with AK105 group showing a longer DoR than placebo group with
an HR of 0.4 (95%CI: 0.27, 0.59).

o

Investigator-assessed response: the confirmed ORR for AK105 group and placebo group
was 66.0% (95% CI: 57.6%, 73.7%) and 57.1% (95% CI: 48.7%, 65.3%), respectively. The
median DoR was also longer in AK105 group (12.1 months, 95% CI: 8.5, 17.5) compared
to placebo group (5.7 months, 95% CI: 5.5, 6.7) with an HR of 0.35 (95%CI: 0.23, 0.52).

The Applicant’s Position:
The interim analysis results of AK105-304 showed that the Phase 3 trial of penpulimab combined
with gemcitabine and cisplatin/carboplatin as the first-line treatment for R/M NPC patients,
demonstrated large and robust treatment effect in terms of both BICR-assessed PFS (the primary
endpoint) and investigator-assessed PFS. However, the study design allowing crossover after PD
substantially affects the OS results. After correcting the confounding effect of crossovers via
common statistical methods, the OS effect becomes evident and similar to those shown in other
phase 3 studies on other anti-PD-1 agents. Compared with similar studies of other PD-1 inhibitors
combined with chemotherapy as first-line treatment for R/M NPC, the efficacy was generally
comparable. Furthermore, the sensitivity analysis of PFS including 218 Asian and 11 ex-Asia
subjects showed similar efficacy. Therefore, penpulimab combined with gemcitabine and
cisplatin/carboplatin has a favorable efficacy and provides a new beneficial treatment option for
R/M NPC patients globally.
The FDA’s Assessment:
Based on the results from Studies AK105-304 and AK105-202, the review team concluded that
the Applicant provided substantial evidence of effectiveness for penpulimab in combination
with cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine, for the first-line treatment of adult patients with
metastatic or recurrent, locally advanced nonkeratinizing NPC and for penpulimab as
monotherapy, in adult patients with recurrent unresectable or metastatic NPC of

Study AK105-304 demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in BICR-assessed PFS
favoring the penpulimab arm, with a HR of 0.45 (95% CI 0.33, 0.62; p<0.0001), corresponding to
a median PFS of 9.6 months (95% CI: 7.1, 12.5) in the penpulimab arm and 7.0 months (95% CI:
6.3, 7.3) in the placebo arm. The proportions of patients with observed PFS of at least 12
months was 31% in the penpulimab arm and 11% in the control arm. The PFS HR of 0.45 and a
2.6-month improvement in median PFS, along with a 20 percent-point difference in observed
PFS rate at 12 months are considered clinically meaningful in this disease setting. In Study
AK105-304, while the numerical difference in median PFS between the two arms was less than
3 months (median PFS was 9.6 months (95% CI: 7.1, 12.5) in the penpulimab-kcqx arm and 7.0
months (95% CI: 6.9, 7.3) in the placebo arm), the substantial reduction in the risk of disease
progression or death in the penpulimab plus chemotherapy arm as compared to chemotherapy
alone, as indicated by the hazard ratio, underscores a clinically meaningful benefit. The KaplanMeier curves begin to separate at approximately around 7 months, which suggests that some
patients may derive prolonged PFS benefit, or that there may be a potential late treatment
effect, which was not captured by median PFS alone. The ORR was 68% in the penpulimab arm
and 64% in the placebo arm. The secondary endpoint of DOR demonstrated that penpulimab
with cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine had a longer median DOR at 9.8 months (95% CI:
7.0, 17.4) compared to cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine alone at 5.7 months (95% CI:
5.5, 6.7).
These results provide substantial evidence of effectiveness for penpulimab in combination with
cisplatin (or carboplatin) and gemcitabine, for the first-line treatment of adults with metastatic
or with recurrent, locally advanced nonkeratinizing NPC. OS was not statistically significant at
the first formal interim analysis, conducted at 70% information fraction. The HR was 0.91 (95%
CI: 0.64, 1.31, p = 0.615). Median OS was not reached in the penpulimab arm (95% CI: 27.4, NE),
while the median OS in the placebo arm was 31.3 months (95% CI: 27.2, NE). However, the
interpretation of these results is challenging due to several reasons. Notably, a high rate of
crossover from the placebo arm to the penpulimab arm (49%) may have impacted any potential
OS difference between the treatment arms. Additionally, a substantial proportion of patients
(31%) in the placebo arm received another anti-PD-(L)1 antibody upon disease progression. In
total 80% of patients in the placebo arm received either penpulimab or another anti-PD-(L)1
antibody as subsequent treatment. This may have influenced survival outcomes and further
complicated the assessment of treatment effect. Consequently, while no apparent OS
detriment was observed at the time of the first formal OS analysis (DCO date: January 24,
2025), the impact of these post-progression treatments will be considered in future analyses
when mature OS data are available.

A major limitation of the data is that Study AK105-304 enrolled 96% of the patients in China
(based on a data cut-off date of April 29, 2024), and Study AK105-202 was conducted
exclusively in China. While both Studies AK105-304 and AK105-202 were conducted
predominantly in China, a flexible regulatory approach is warranted given the high unmet need
for treatment options for patients with NPC. These trials were initiated prior to the approval of
regimens with toripalimab, the only other FDA-approved anti-PD-(L)1 antibody for U.S. patients
with NPC. Cisplatin or carboplatin plus gemcitabine was considered an appropriate control arm
in Study AK105-304 when the trial was designed, making the study results relevant to U.S.
medical practice. Cisplatin plus gemcitabine was considered standard of care for the first-line
treatment of recurrent or metastatic NPC in the U.S., and carboplatin plus gemcitabine was
considered an appropriate option for patients who may be unable to tolerate or who have
contraindications to cisplatin. The incidence of NPC is much higher in East Asia relative to the
U.S., where NPC is a relatively rare disease, making enrollment to clinical trials more feasible in
that region of the world. Clinical site inspections were conducted by FDA to validate the data
supporting this application. To further address the issue of applicability to the U.S. population,
the Applicant will be collecting additional clinical data to further characterize the safety and
efficacy of penpulimab in combination with either cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine for
the treatment of non-keratinizing NPC in a study population whose demographic and disease
characteristics are more representative of the population of U.S. patients with NPC (see
Postmarketing Commitments later in this review for details).

AK105-304

patients were treated for more than 3 months, 68.8% for more than 6 months, 41.0% of patients

AK105-301

In Study AK105-304, the median number of penpulimab treatment cycles (13 vs. 12) and
treatment duration in days (259 vs. 236) were comparable between the experimental and
control arms.
In AK105-304, 71% of patients were exposed to penpulimab in combination with either cisplatin
or carboplatin and gemcitabine for 6 months or more and 38% were exposed 12 months or
more.
In AK105-202, 45% of patients were exposed to penpulimab for 6 months or more and 30%
were exposed 12 months or more. In the pooled safety monotherapy dataset, 49% of patients
received treatment for at least six months, and 34% for at least 12 months.
The FDA notes that drug exposure data from AK105-304 suggest that the addition of
penpulimab did not impact the administration of cisplatin and gemcitabine. However, in AK105202 and the pooled safety dataset, penpulimab exposure was relatively short, with a median
duration of 140 days (4.7 months) and 169 days (5.6 months), respectively.

FDA agrees that regarding male predominance, this is consistent with what is expected in the
US patient population with NPC. However, the median age of patients in AK105-304 (51 years)
and AK105-202 (50 years) is slightly younger than the median age for US patients with NPC (53
or 54 years). Furthermore, given that nearly all patients in the efficacy populations for both
studies were of Chinese ethnicity, the efficacy populations do not reflect the racial and ethnic
diversity of the US patient population with NPC. Patients with keratinizing histology were
permitted to enroll to Study AK105-304; however, only very few patients with keratinizing
histology were included in this trial and were therefore greatly underrepresented relative to
the incidence of this histology in the US population with NPC. In total, only 0.7% of patients in
each arm of AK105-304 had keratinizing histology compared to 35% of patients in the US with
NPC expected to have keratinizing histology. Only patients with non-keratinizing histology were
eligible for enrollment into Study AK105-202. There were no additional patients with nonkeratinizing NPC in the pooled dataset.
Despite the differences noted above, FDA agrees that the safety data from AK105-304, AK105202, and the pooled safety dataset provide sufficient data for evaluations of the safety profile
of penpulimab in combination with cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine and as a single
agent.
Adequacy of the safety database:
Data:
Integrated penpulimab Monotherapy Part includes pooled safety data from 558 patients with a
variety of tumor types across 6 studies who have been exposed to penpulimab monotherapy at
any dose levels. Of those patients, 372 patients with penpulimab 200mg Q2W were included for
overall safety evaluation.
Integrated penpulimab Combination Therapy Part includes 393 patients who have been exposed
to penpulimab 200mg Q3W in combination with chemotherapy or other regimens. Of those
patients, 146 patients with NPC treated with penpulimab in combination with cisplatin and
gemcitabine were included for overall safety evaluation.
The Applicant’s Position:
The safety database was considered adequate to support the characterization of the safety
profile of penpulimab in the proposed patient population.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA did not independently verify data from the AK105-302 or AK105-301 trials because these
patients received chemotherapy regimens other than cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine.

basis for assessing the safety profile of penpulimab both in combination with cisplatin or
carboplatin and gemcitabine, and as a single agent.
8.2.3. Adequacy of Applicant’s Clinical Safety Assessments
Issues Regarding Data Integrity and Submission Quality
Data:
All clinical trials in this package were conducted according to Good Clinial Practice. Monitors were
responsible for ensuring adherence to the protocol; compliance with GCP. The study team and
site personnel collaborated closely to ensure the completeness, accuracy, and consistency of the
study data. Direct access to medical and laboratory records of all subjects was permitted to verify
entries on the study-specific eCRFs.
Central laboratories were preferred in the studies. Where local laboratories were used, their
qualification was strictly evaluated by the study monitors.
All safety evaluation procedures including monitoring for AEs, reporting SAEs, physical
examinations, vital sign measurements, clinical laboratory tests, and ECGs were standard (i.e.,
widely used and generally recognized as reliable, accurate, and relevant).
The Applicant’s Position:
Although there were several cases of untimely reporting of SAEs as described in critical protocol
deviation, no issues were identified that could affect the quality and integrity of the submitted
datasets and individual case narratives.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position.

The Applicant’s Position:
Most death cases in the clinical studies were related to disease progression. This is consistent
with patients’ underlying medical conditions, and possibly concomitant medications. SAE
Narratives are available for all patients and include all TEAEs leading to death.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA reviewed all fatal adverse events in patients from the primary safety population in Studies
AK105-304 and AK105-202. Based on this review, one patient (0.7%) in the investigational arm
of Study AK105-304 experienced a Grade 5 adverse event that could be at least potentially
related to penpulimab (due to syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion).
Additionally, in the AK105-202 trial of penpulimab monotherapy, four patients (1%) had Grade
5 adverse events that were at least potentially related to penpulimab. Fatal adverse reactions
included a case each of pneumonitis, septic shock, colitis, and hepatitis.
A summary of FDA’s review of fatal adverse events in Study AK105-304 and Study AK105-202 is
provided in the tables below.

8.2.4.2. Serious Adverse Events
Data:
Monotherapy Part
NPC 200mg Q2W population
31 patients (23.8%) experienced at least one SAE. Excluding death and disease progression, the
most commonly (the incidence of PT ≥ 1%) reported SAEs included pneumonia, lung infection,
respiratory failure, pneumonitis, hepatic function abnormal, and rash.
10 patients (7.7%) had SAEs that were deemed to be drug-related by the investigator. Excluding
death and disease progression, pneumonitis and rash occurred in 2 patients each, while other
PTs were reported in one patient each, including pneumonia, abdominal infection, herpes zoster
disseminated, transaminases increased, pleural effusion, hepatic function abnormal and
pemphigoid.
Penpulimab 200mg Q2W population
100 patients (26.9%) experienced at least one SAE. Excluding death and disease progression, the
most commonly (the incidence of PT ≥ 1%) reported SAEs included pneumonia, lung infection
and diarrhoea.
28 patients (7.5%) had SAEs that were deemed to be drug-related by the investigator. Excluding
death and disease progression, pneumonia, alanine aminotransferase increased, transaminases
increased, immune-mediated pneumonitis, pneumonitis, hepatic function abnormal and rash
occurred in 2 patients each; other PTs were reported in one patient each, including lung infection,
abdominal infection, herpes zoster, herpes zoster disseminated, aspartate aminotransferase
increased, blood bilirubin increased, pleural effusion, pain, gastrointestinal haemorrhage,
intestinal obstruction, pemphigoid, hypersensitivity, infusion related reaction,
mesangioproliferative glomerulonephritis, renal injury and hypertension.

Combination Therapy Part
AK105-304
In patients treated with penpulimab 200mg Q3W in combination with cisplatin/carboplatin and
gemcitabine in AK105-304, 74 patients (50.7%) experienced at least one SAE. Excluding disease
progression, 73 patients (50.0%) experienced at least one SAE. The most commonly (the
incidence of PT ≥ 1%) reported SAEs (excluding disease progression) included platelet count
decreased, white blood cell count decreased, neutrophil count decreased, blood creatinine
increased, anaemia, febrile neutropenia, myelosuppression, pneumonia, upper respiratory tract
infection, COVID-19 pneumonia, urinary tract infection, asthenia, epistaxis, hyponatraemia,
diabetic ketoacidosis, arrhythmia and nausea.
43 patients (29.5%) had SAEs that were deemed to be drug-related by the investigator, included:

The Applicant’s Position:
The frequency and nature of SAEs were generally similar between the NPC penpulimab 200mg
Q2W population, penpulimab 200mg Q2W population and the overall monotherapy population,
and there were no clinically meaningful differences between these three monotherapy
populations for any SAEs.
In the pivotal AK105-304 study, the incidence of SAEs in the penpulimab group was generally
similar to that in the placebo group. No serious unexpected AEs were observed.
The FDA’s Assessment:
When reviewing SAEs, FDA’s process for grouping preferred terms resulted in slightly different
percentages. In addition, the FDA included laboratory abnormalities in the review of SAEs.
In Study AK105-304, 51% of patients experienced an SAE. The most frequent serious adverse
reactions (≥2%) were thrombocytopenia (19%), decreased neutrophils (14%), decreased white
blood cells (12%), anemia (8%), myelosuppression (3.4%), decreased sodium (2.7%), pneumonia
(2.1%), and nausea (2.1%).
In Study AK105-202, 22% of patients in the NPC population and 27% of patients in the pooled
safety dataset had one or more SAEs. The most frequent SAEs (≥1%) included pneumonia,
pneumonitis, respiratory failure, and rash.

The Applicant’s Position:
The incidence of AEs resulting in permanent discontinuation of penpulimab was low and similar
between the NPC penpulimab 200mg Q2W population, penpulimab 200mg Q2W population and
the overall monotherapy population. There were no appreciable differences between the three
populations for any of the SOCs or PTs.
In the pivotal AK105-304 study, the incidence of AEs resulting in permanent discontinuation of
penpulimab/placebo in the penpulimab group was slightly higher than that in the placebo group.
AEs resulting in discontinuation of penpulimab were distributed across a broad range of PTs, with
no specific SOC or PT accounting for most of the events (occurred in ≤1% of patients).
The FDA’s Assessment:
In Study AK105-304, 3.4% of patients discontinued penpulimab due to AEs. Rates of
discontinuation were similar between the penpulimab and placebo arms.
In Study AK105-202, 3.8% of patients discontinued penpulimab due to AEs. The FDA estimates
of penpulimab discontinuation due to AEs generally aligned with Applicant’s estimates.
In the pooled safety dataset, 6% of patients discontinued penpulimab due to AEs.
AEs leading to permanent discontinuation of penpulimab are listed in FDA – Table 16 and FDA –
Table 17 below.

The overall incidence of AEs resulting in drug interruption were generally similar between the
NPC penpulimab 200mg Q2W population, penpulimab 200mg Q2W population and the overall
monotherapy population. There were no marked differences between the three populations for
any of the SOCs or PTs.
In the pivotal AK105-304 study, the incidence of AEs resulting in drug interruption of
penpulimab/placebo in the penpulimab group was similar to that in the placebo group.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA included laboratory abnormalities in the analysis of AEs leading to dose interruptions,
resulting in the report of additional AEs leading to penpulimab dose interruption compared
with Applicant’s report.

8.2.4.6. Treatment Emergent Adverse Events and Adverse Reactions
Data:
Monotherapy Part
NPC 200mg Q2W population
Excluding disease progression, 123 out of 130 (94.6%) patients had at least one TEAE. Most
patients had Grade 1 or 2 AEs; 38 (29.2%) patients had at least one ≥ Grade 3 TEAE. The incidence
of drug-related TEAEs was 71.5% (93/130), and the incidence of ≥ Grade 3 drug-related TEAEs
was 8.5% (11/130).
The most commonly (the incidence of PT ≥ 20%) reported TEAEs included anemia and
hypothyroidism. Common ≥ Grade 3 TEAEs (with an incidence of ≥ 1%) were anaemia, hepatic
function abnormal, liver injury, lung infection, aspartate aminotransferase increased, blood
alkaline phosphatase increased, blood magnesium increased, gamma-glutamyltransferase
increased,weight decreased, hyperuricaemia, hyponatraemia, respiratory failure, rash, disease
progression and death.
Penpulimab 200mg Q2W population
Excluding disease progression, 355 out of 372 (95.4%) patients had at least one TEAE. Most
patients had Grade 1 or 2 AEs; 127 (34.1%) patients had at least one ≥ Grade 3 TEAE. The
incidence of drug-related TEAEs was 71.8% (267/372), and the incidence of ≥ Grade 3 drugrelated TEAEs was 9.7% (36/372).
The most commonly (the incidence of PT ≥ 20%) reported TEAEs included anemia and
hypothyroidism. Common ≥ Grade 3 TEAEs (with an incidence of ≥ 1%) were anaemia, Diarrhoea,
Vomiting, Lower respiratory tract infection, lung infection, pneumonia, Urinary tract infection,
alanine aminotransferase increased, aspartate aminotransferase increased, gammaglutamyltransferase increased, platelet count decreased, hyperuricaemia, hyponatraemia,
hypertension and disease progression.
Overall Monotherapy Population
Excluding disease progression, 512 out of 558 (91.8%) patients had at least one TEAE. Most
patients had Grade 1 or 2 AEs; 172 (30.8%) patients had at least one ≥ Grade 3 TEAE. The
incidence of drug-related TEAEs was 69.7% (389/558), and the incidence of ≥ Grade 3 drugrelated TEAEs was 10.8% (60/558).
The most commonly (the incidence of PT ≥ 20%) reported TEAEs included anemia. Common ≥
Grade 3 TEAEs (with an incidence of ≥ 1%) were anaemia, lung infection, pneumonia, urinary
tract infection, aspartate aminotransferase increased, gamma-glutamyltransferase increased,
hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia, hypertension, disease progression and death.

Combination Therapy Part
AK105-304
In patients treated with penpulimab 200mg Q3W in combination with cisplatin/carboplatin and
gemcitabine in AK105-304, 146 (100.0%) patients had at least one TEAE. 132 (90.4%) patients
had at least one ≥ Grade 3 TEAE. The most commonly (the incidence of PT ≥ 20%) reported TEAEs
with a marginally higher incidence in the penpulimab group included aspartate aminotransferase
increased, weight decreased, blood creatinine increased, anaemia, vomiting, hyponatraemia,
hypoalbuminaemia, hypokalaemia, hypochloraemia, pyrexia, COVID-19, cough and
hypothyroidism. Common ≥ Grade 3 TEAEs (with an incidence of ≥ 2%) with a marginally higher
incidence in the penpulimab group included lymphocyte count decreased, alanine
aminotransferase increased, blood creatine phosphokinase increased, anaemia, pneumonia,
COVID-19 pneumonia, hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia, hypocalcaemia, hypomagnesaemia,
nausea, hypertension and disease progression.
The incidence of drug-related TEAEs was 89.7% (131/146), and the incidence of ≥ Grade 3 drugrelated TEAEs was 57.5% (84/146). The most commonly (the incidence of PT ≥ 10%) reported
drug-relates TEAEs with a marginally higher incidence in the penpulimab group included
aspartate aminotransferase increased, platelet count decreased, blood creatinine increased,
anaemia, hyponatraemia, hypoalbuminaemia, hypokalaemia, hypertriglyceridaemia,
hypochloraemia, hypomagnesaemia, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, rash and
hypothyroidism. Common ≥ Grade 3 drug-relates TEAEs (with an incidence of ≥ 1%) with a
marginally higher incidence in the penpulimab group included white blood cell count decreased,
lymphocyte count decreased, anaemia, hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia, hypertriglyceridaemia,

The Applicant’s Position:
The most common AEs (regardless of severity and causality) in monotherapy observed in NPC
penpulimab 200mg Q2W population were comparable to penpulimab 200mg Q2W population
and the overall monotherapy population. Most of the AEs were Grade 1 or 2, indicating a
tolerable safety profile of penpulimab.
In the pivotal AK105-304 study, only a few of TEAEs occurred at a slightly higher rate in the
penpulimab group, such as abnormal transaminases, anemia, metabolic and nutritional disorders,
electrolyte abnormalities, COVID-19, hypothyroidism, cough, and headache. Except for COVID19, these are common AEs in cancer patients, and most of the AEs were grades 1 or 2, without
affecting the function of important organs or systems.

8.2.4.9. Electrocardiograms (ECGs)
Data:
Electrocardiogram (ECG) assessments are part of routine safety monitoring.
Shift table for ECGs of clinical significance from baseline to worst post-baseline was summarized
in Module5.3.5.3, ISS, Appendix 3.5, Table 7.1.1 and Table 7.1.2.
NPC 200mg Q2W population
No patients had a QTcF value > 500 msec or an increase from baseline > 90 msec. No patients
had a QTcF value > 480 msec, 3 (2.5%) patients had an increase from baseline > 60 msec.
Penpulimab 200mg Q2W population
2 (0.6%) patients had a QTcF value > 500 msec and 4 (1.1%) patients had an increase from
baseline > 90 msec. 6 (1.7%) patients had a QTcF value > 480 msec and 14 (3.9%) patients had an
increase from baseline > 60 msec.
Overall Monotherapy population
6 (1.1%) patients had a QTcF value > 500 msec and 7 (1.3%) patients had an increase from
baseline > 90 msec. 11 (2.1%) patients had a QTcF value > 480 msec and 21 (4.0%) patients had
an increase from baseline > 60 msec.
Conclusions
Individuals with clinically meaningful QTcF values and changes from baseline were found to have
had either cardiac medical history or were receiving potentially cardioactive concomitant
medications at the time of abnormality or had single occurrences above the defined threshold.
There was no evidence of clinically meaningful cardiac effects associated with penpulimab
exposure.
Combination Therapy Part
AK105-304
No patients had a QTcF value > 500 msec, 1 (0.7%) patient had an increase from baseline > 90
msec. No patients had a QTcF value > 480 msec, 11 (8.0%) patients had an increase from baseline
> 60 msec.

8.2.4.10.

Immunogenicity

Data:
NPC 200mg Q2W population
The proportion of patients with ADA positive at baseline and post-baseline was 5.9% and
30.3%, respectively. 27.7% of patients developed treatment-emergent ADA (TEADA), and 6.7 %
TEADA patients had positive neutralizing antibody (Nab). Among patients with negative
baselines, the incidence of TEADA was 25.2%, and the incidence of positive Nab was 6.7%. Only
3 (2.5%) TEADA patients had positive baselines and none of them had positive Nab.
The incidence rates of TEADA and Nab in NPC population who received Penpulimab
monotherapy were comparable to other tumor types.
Penpulimab 200mg Q2W population
349 patients were treated with penpulimab monotherapy at 1mg/kg, 3mg/kg, 10mg/kg, 200mg
Q2W.
The proportion of patients with ADA positive at baseline and post-baseline was 3.4% and
31.2%, respectively. 30.1% of patients developed treatment-emergent ADA (TEADA), and 5.2 %
of patients with TEADA had positive neutralizing antibody (Nab). Among patients with negative
baselines, the incidence of TEADA was 28.4%, and the incidence of positive Nab was 5.2%. Only
5 (1.4%) patients with TEADA had positive baselines and none of them had positive Nab.
Among the patients treated with penpulimab monotherapy (1~10mg/kg Q2W, or 200mg
Q2W/Q3W), the incidence of AEs such as TEAE, TRAE (CTCAE Grade 3+), serious TEAEs, serious
drug-related TEAEs, TEAEs leading to death, drug-related TEAEs leading to death, drug-related
TEAEs leading to drug discontinuation in the patients with TEADA were similar to those from
ADA-negative patients, and no special type of AE occurred in patients with TEADA.
For drug-related TEAEs leading to dose interruption, the incidence in patients with TEADA was
slightly higher than that in the ADA-negative patients (20.0% vs. 13.8%).

In ex-Asia patients who received penpulimab monotherapy (200mg Q2W), AE events in the

In NPC monotherapy population, the incidence of AEs in patients with TEADA was similar to

interruption in patients with TEADA was higher than ADA-negative patients (11.4% vs. 6.3%).
The Applicant’s Position:
In TEADA patients, the incidence and types of AEs were generally similar to those of all patients.
Treatment emergent ADA had no significant impact on safety.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position.

Penpulimab
Endocrine Toxicity
Hypothyroidism
In patients treated with penpulimab 200mg Q3W in combination with cisplatin/carboplatin and
gemcitabine in AK105-304, hypothyroidism occurred in 26 (17.8%) of patients, including 7 (4.8%)
Grade 1 and 19 (13.0%) Grade 2 irAEs. No patient experienced a serious irAE. 1 (0.7%) patient
experienced irAEs leading to drug interruption. No patient experienced irAEs leading to drug
discontinuation.
Hyperthyroidism
In patients treated with penpulimab 200mg Q3W in combination with cisplatin/carboplatin and
gemcitabine in AK105-304, hyperthyroidism occurred in 3 (2.1%) of patients, including 2 (1.4%)
Grade 1 and 1 (0.7%) Grade 2 irAEs. There was no serious irAE. No irAE leading to interruption or
permanent discontinuation of penpulimab.
Hyperglycaemia/Type 1 diabetes mellitus
In patients treated with penpulimab 200mg Q3W in combination with cisplatin/carboplatin and
gemcitabine in AK105-304, hyperglycaemia/type 1 diabetes mellitus occurred in 4 (2.7%) of
patients, including 1 (0.7%) Grade 1, 1 (0.7%) Grade 2, 1 (0.7%) Grade 3 and 1 (0.7%) Grade 4
irAEs. 2 (1.4%) patients experienced a serious irAE. 1 (0.7%) patient experienced irAEs leading to
drug interruption. 1 (0.7%) patient experienced irAEs leading to drug discontinuation.
Dermatologic Toxicity
In patients treated with penpulimab 200mg Q3W in combination with cisplatin/carboplatin and
gemcitabine in AK105-304, dermatologic toxicity occurred in 14 (9.6%) of patients, including 6
(4.1%) Grade 1, 7 (4.8%) Grade 2 and 1 (0.7%) Grade 3 irAEs. 1 (0.7%) patient experienced a
serious irAE. 2 (1.4%) patients experienced irAEs leading to drug interruption. No patient
experienced irAEs leading to drug discontinuation.
Pulmonary Toxicity
In patients treated with penpulimab 200mg Q3W in combination with cisplatin/carboplatin and
gemcitabine in AK105-304, only one patient (0.7%) developed pulmonary toxicity, which was
CTCAE grade 2 and a serious irAE. The irAE led to interruption of penpulimab but didn’t lead to
permanent discontinuation of penpulimab.
Hepatotoxicity
In patients treated with penpulimab 200mg Q3W in combination with cisplatin/carboplatin and
gemcitabine in AK105-304, only one patient (0.6%) developed hepatotoxicity, Grade 2. The event
was not a serious irAE. The event led to interruption of penpulimab but didn’t lead to permanent
discontinuation of penpulimab.

Penpulimab
Musculoskeletal Toxicity
In patients treated with penpulimab 200mg Q3W in combination with cisplatin/carboplatin and
gemcitabine in AK105-304, only one patient (0.7%) developed musculoskeletal toxicity, which
was CTCAE grade 3 and was a serious irAE. The irAE led to interruption of penpulimab but didn’t
lead to permanent discontinuation of penpulimab.
Hematological Toxicity
In patients treated with penpulimab 200mg Q3W in combination with cisplatin/carboplatin and
gemcitabine in AK105-304, only one patient (0.7%) developed thrombocytopenia, which was
CTCAE grade 4 and was a serious irAE. The irAE led to interruption of penpulimab but didn’t lead
to permanent discontinuation of penpulimab.
Pancreatic Toxicity
In patients treated with penpulimab 200mg Q3W in combination with cisplatin/carboplatin and
gemcitabine in AK105-304, pancreatic toxicity occurred in 2 (1.4%) of patients, including 1 (0.7%)
Grade 2 and 1 (0.7%) Grade 3 irAEs. 2 (1.4%) patients experienced a serious irAE. No patient
experienced irAEs leading to drug interruption. 1 (0.7%) patient experienced irAEs leading to drug
discontinuation.
The Applicant’s Position:
In the overall monotherapy population, the most commonly (the incidence of PT ≥ 1%) reported
irAEs included hypothyroidism, blood thyroid stimulating hormone increased, thyroxine free
decreased, hyperthyroidism, blood thyroid stimulating hormone decreased, rash, pruritus, rash
generalised, alanine aminotransferase increased and aspartate aminotransferase increased.
Compared with monotherapy with penpulimab, the combination of penpulimab and
chemotherapy did not increase the incidence of irAEs, and the incidence of irAEs in various organs
was low. The incidence of hypothyroidism was relatively high, which may also be related to a
history of previous radiotherapy. 67.5% of the enrolled patients had recurrent nasopharyngeal
carcinoma and had previously received neck radiotherapy, so thyroid damage may have already
existed at baseline. Moreover, immune-related endocrine toxicity can be controlled with
hormone replacement therapy, and there was no significant safety risk.
The development of irAEs was expected based on the mechanism of action of the drug. The
pattern, incidence and severity of irAEs was consistent with other PD-1 inhibitors and was
manageable with the use of appropriate dose interruption and immunosuppressants.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA reviewed the Applicant adjudicated immune-related AEs (irAEs) in AK105-304, AK105-202,
and in the pooled safety dataset. Given the potential delayed onset of irAEs, FDA’s review
includes adverse events that occurred up to 90 days after the last dose of treatment with
penpulimab or placebo.

FDA’s analysis of irAEs agrees with the Applicant’s position. Overall, the most common irAEs

8.2.5.2. Infusion-Related Reactions
NPC 200mg Q2W population
5 patients (3.8%) experienced infusion-related reactions, including Grade 1 in 4 patients, Grade
2 in 1 patient. No patient occurred Grade 3-4 infusion-related reactions. No patient experienced
serious infusion-related reaction, infusion-related reactions leading to interruption of
penpulimab or infusion-related reaction leading to permanent discontinuation of penpulimab.
No patient received systemic corticosteroid therapies. All these 5 patients had
recovered/resolved.
Penpulimab 200mg Q2W population
38 patients (10.2%) experienced infusion-related reactions, including Grade 1 in 14 patients,
Grade 2 in 22 patients. 2 patients occurred Grade 3-4 infusion-related reactions. 3 patients (0.8%)
experienced serious infusion-related reaction. Infusion-related reaction led to interruption of
penpulimab in 3 patients (0.8%) and 1 patients (0.3%) occurred infusion-related reaction resulted
in permanent discontinuation of penpulimab. 8 patients (2.2%) received systemic corticosteroid
therapies. All these 38 patients had recovered/resolved.
Overall Monotherapy population
41 patients (7.3%) experienced infusion-related reactions, including Grade 1 in 15 patients,
Grade 2 in 23 patients. 3 patients had Grade 3-4 infusion-related reactions. 4 patients (0.7%)
experienced serious infusion-related reaction. Infusion-related reaction led to interruption of
penpulimab occurred in 3 patienst (0.5%) and 2 patients (0.4%) had infusion-related reaction
resulted in permanent discontinuation of penpulimab. 9 patients (1.6%) received systemic
corticosteroid therapies. All these 41 patients had recovered/resolved.

The Applicant’s Position:
In the overall monotherapy population, The most commonly (the incidence of PT ≥ 1%) reported
irAEs included hypothyroidism, blood thyroid stimulating hormone increased, thyroxine free
decreased, hyperthyroidism, blood thyroid stimulating hormone decreased, rash, pruritus, rash
generalised, alanine aminotransferase increased and aspartate aminotransferase increased.
Compared with monotherapy with penpulimab, the combination of penpulimab and
chemotherapy did not increase the incidence of irAEs, and the incidence of irAEs in various organs
was low. The incidence of hypothyroidism was relatively high, which may also be related to a
history of previous radiotherapy. 67.5% of the enrolled patients had recurrent nasopharyngeal
carcinoma and had previously received neck radiotherapy, so thyroid damage may have already
existed at baseline. Moreover, immune-related endocrine toxicity can be controlled with
hormone replacement therapy, and there was no significant safety risk.

FDA generally agrees with the Applicant’s position. In AK105-304, no patients experienced an
infusion-related reaction in the penpulimab arm. Infusion-related reactions occurred in 3.4%
and 10% of patients in AK105-202 and the pooled safety dataset, respectively.

ECOG performance status
In overall penpulimab monotherapy population, the incidence of events was similar in patients
with a baseline ECOG performance status of 0 and 1 for most AE categories. However, notable
differences were observed for Grade 3 or higher TEAEs (29.9% vs 38.3%) and SAEs (20.4% vs
28.8%), all of which occurred at a higher rate in patients with an ECOG performance status of 1
compared with ECOG performance status of 0.
Among patients in AK105-304 study, the incidence of events was similar in patients with a
baseline ECOG performance status of 0 and 1. Among patients in AK105-302 study, TEAEs of
CTCAE grade 3 or higher, serious TEAEs, and TEAEs leading to drug interruption occurred at a
higher rate in patients with an ECOG performance status of 1 compared with ECOG performance
status of 0.
The differences between ECOG subgroups in other studies of penpulimab combination therapy
cannot be assessed due to the small sample size.
Race
For penpulimab monotherapy, the safety subgroup analysis revealed no clinically relevant
differences in the incidence, nature, or severity of AEs between Asian and non-Asian patients.
The differences between race subgroups in penpulimab combination therapy cannot be assessed
due to only 6 non-Asian patients enrolled.
The Applicant’s Position:
The AE profile for penpulimab monotherapy population and combination therapy was generally
similar across subgroups based on age and sex.
The incidence of AEs of any grade was generally similar between ECOG subgroup, and lower
incidence rate of grade 3 or higher TEAEs, SAEs, and TEAEs leading to drug interruption in patients
with ECOG performance status of 0 were observed.
The similarity in the safety profiles across ethnic groups suggests that the pharmacological
activity and safety profile of penpulimab are not significantly influenced by ethnicity.

191
Version date: January 2020 (ALL NDA/ BLA reviews)
Disclaimer: In this document, the sections labeled as “Data” and “The Applicant’s Position” are
completed by the Applicant and do not necessarily reflect the positions of the FDA.
Reference ID: 5577575

NDA/BLA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation- BLA 761258
Penpulimab
The Applicant’s Position:
Penpulimab has not been studied in pregnant or breastfeeding women. As of the DCO dates for
studies on dosing regimen of penpulimab 200 mg Q2W, there were no reports of pregnancies or
pregnancy-related events in either study. Based on its mechanism of action, penpulimab has the
potential to impact maintenance of pregnancy and may cause fetal harm when administered to
a pregnant woman. Human IgG1 is known to cross the placental barrier; therefore, penpulimab
has the potential to be transmitted from the mother to the developing fetus. penpulimab is not
recommended during pregnancy and in women of childbearing potential not using effective
contraception during treatment and for at least 3 months after the last dose.
There is no information regarding the presence of penpulimab in human milk, the absorption and
effects on the breastfed infant, or the effects on milk production. Human IgG is excreted in
human milk. Because of the potential for adverse reactions in breastfed infants from penpulimab,
advise a lactating women not to breastfeed during treatment and for at least 5 months after the
last dose.
The FDA’s Assessment:
See FDA’s Assessment in Section 5.5.4 (Reproductive and Developmental Toxicity) of this
review.

Penpulimab
Overdose, Drug Abuse Potential, Withdrawal, and Rebound
Data:
There are no available safety data for penpulimab overdose.
The Applicant’s Position:
There is no specific treatment in the event of penpulimab overdose and possible symptoms have
not been established.
As a result of its use, mode of action, physiological and pharmacological activity, and lack of
stimulant properties, penpulimab monotherapy is unlikely to be abused. Because penpulimab
has no known potential for dependence and is not continuously dosed, withdrawal or rebound
events are not relevant to penpulimab dosing.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position.
8.2.10. Safety in the Postmarket Setting
Safety Concerns Identified Through Postmarket Experience
Data:
Cumulatively, 866 post-marketing adverse events were received from IBD by 29 Apr 2024,
including 430 serious adverse events and 436 non-serious adverse events. Serious adverse events
with the highest number of reports (≥8 events) included white blood cell count decreased,
neutrophil count decreased, platelet count decreased, myelosuppression, rash, immunemediated lung disease, dyspnoea, chest discomfort, drug-induced liver injury, hepatic function
abnormal, hypothyroidism, immune-mediated myocarditis, anaphylactic shock.
The Applicant’s Position:
The first indication of penpulimab (Approval Number: GYZZ S20210033) was conditionally
approved for marketing in China on 3 Aug 2021 (International Birth Date, IBD). Penpulimab is
indicated, as a single agent, for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory
classical Hodgkin lymphoma who have failed at least two lines of systemic chemotherapy. For
classical Hodgkin lymphoma, the recommended dosage is administered by intravenous infusion
at a recommended dose of 200mg every 2 weeks until disease progression or unacceptable

Based on the analysis of the post-marketing safety data, mechanism of action of the drug or
adverse reaction profile of same class drugs, Marketing Authorization Holder applied to Center
for Drug Evaluation, NMPA for revising the package insert of penpulimab to add the adverse

information on concomitant diseases, concomitant medication, diagnosis evidence of adverse
events or medical history and limited follow-up information are prevalent in post marketing
reports. Confounding factors such as different medication populations, different combined antitumor treatment regimens and differences in the patients' own conditions also existed during
the assessment of adverse events.
Overall, the analysis of the post-marketing safety data supports the good tolerability of
penpulimab and adequacy of the risk management plan. Benefit-risk profile continues to support
further development of penpulimab.

In monotherapy part, the safety profile of penpulimab 200mg Q2W in NPC population is

manageable, and consistent with other marketed PD-1 inbibitors.
The demographic and disease characteristics of patients in the NPC 200mg Q2W monotherapy

in clinical practice.

FDA conducted the safety review of penpulimab in combination with cisplatin or carboplatin
and gemcitabine in 146 patients with locally recurrent, unresectable or metastatic NPC who
received penpulimab 200 mg Q3W in combination with cisplatin or carboplatin and
gemcitabine in the AK105-304 trial. For penpulimab monotherapy, FDA conducted the safety
review in 130 patients with locally recurrent or metastatic NPC whose disease progressed on or
after platinum-containing chemotherapy and an additional line of therapy who received
penpulimab 200 mg Q2W as a single agent in the AK105-202 trial and in a pooled dataset of 372
patients with various solid tumors or cHL who received penpulimab 200 mg Q2W as a single
agent. FDA’s review of deaths due to AEs in AK105-304, AK105-202, and the pooled safety
dataset did not identify unexpected safety signals relative to other anti-PD-(L)1 antibodies.

Discontinuation of penpulimab due to AEs occurred in 3.4% of patients in AK105-304, and in
3.8% and 5.9% of patients in the AK105-202 trial and the safety pooled dataset, respectively. In
AK105-304, AK105-202, and the safety pooled dataset there were no AEs leading to
discontinuation that were ≥1%. In AK105-304 one patient each discontinued penpulimab as a
result of Grade 3-4 acute myocardial infarction, AKI, brain edema, DKA, lipase increased, and
platelet count decreased. In AK105-202 one patient each discontinued penpulimab due to
Grade3-4 herpes zoster disseminated, pleural effusion, rash, spinal cord compression, and
transaminases increased. For the pooled safety population 3 patients discontinued for any
grade pneumonitis, 2 for pleural effusion, 2 for GI hemorrhage, and one each for herpes zoster
disseminated, rash, spinal cord compression, transaminases increased, ascites, colitis, pelvic
infection, septic shock, cholangitis, hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, hypersensitivity,
cerebral infarction, epilepsy, mesangioproliferative glomerulonephritis, and renal injury.
Adverse events leading to penpulimab dose interruptions occurred in 64%, 25%, and 26% of
patients in AK105-304, AK105-202, and the pooled safety dataset, respectively. In AK105-304,
the most frequent AEs leading to dose interruptions (≥2%) were Covid19, anemia,
thrombocytopenia, white blood cell count decreased, neutrophil count decreased, COVID 19
pneumonia, pneumonia, ALT increased, hyponatremia, AST increased, asymptomatic COVID 19,
creatinine increased, pyrexia, and URI. In AK105-202, the most frequent AEs leading to dose
interruptions (≥1%) were pneumonia, anemia, hypothyroidism, hepatic function abnormal,
pneumonitis, rash, and ALT increased. Amongst the pooled safety set these plus AST increased,
lung infection, and diarrhea occurred in ≥1%.
Serious adverse reactions events (SAEs) occurred in 51%, 22%, and 27% of patients in AK105304, AK105-202, and the pooled safety dataset, respectively. In AK105-304, the most frequent
SAEs (≥2%) were platelet count decreased, neutrophil count decreased, wbc count decreased,
anemia, myelosuppression, COVID19 pneumonia, pneumonia, hyponatremia, and nausea. In
AK105-202, the most frequent SAEs (≥2%) was only pneumonia while in the pooled safety set
no SAE was ≥2%.
In AK105-304, the most frequent irAEs (≥2%) were hypothyroidism, TSH increased,
hyperthyroidism, and rash. For AK105-202 and the pooled safety set the most frequent irAEs
(≥2%) were hypothyroidism, rash, hyperthyroidism, and TSH increased. On FDA review one
patient in AK105-304 may have died from SIADH while on AK105-202 one patient may have
died from pneumonitis, one from hepatitis, one from colitis, and one from septic shock.
Infusion-related reactions (IRRs) occurred in 3.4% and 10.2% of patients in AK105-304 and the
pooled safety dataset, respectively. All IRRs were Grades 1 or 2, except for 2 grade 3-4 IRR in
the pooled safety dataset. In AK105-304, the most frequent AEs (≥20%) were nausea, vomiting,
constipation, hypothyroidism, decreased appetite, weight decreased, cough, Covid19, fatigue,
pyrexia, and rash. In AK105-202 the most frequent AEs (≥20%) were hypothyroidism and
musculoskeletal pain.

The safety profile of penpulimab was similar to other PD-(L)1 blocking antibodies when

addressed by the information in the Warnings and Precautions section included in product
labeling. There were no significant safety concerns identified during BLA review requiring risk
management beyond labeling or warranting consideration for Risk Evaluation and Mitigation
Strategy (REMS). Penpulimab, in combination with cisplatin or gemcitabine or as a
monotherapy, appears to have an acceptable safety profile when assessed in the context of a
life-threatening disease with unmet medical need.

8.3. Statistical Issues
The FDA’s Assessment:
There were no major statistical issues identified during review of the application. The marketing
application was based on results from two studies, Study AK105-304 and Study AK105-202.
Study AK105-202 was conducted entirely in China, while 96% of patients enrolled in Study
AK105-304 were from China. FDA was not able to examine the consistency of the treatment
benefit by geographical location, race and ethnicity, or in a patient population that are more
representative of the population of U.S. patients with NPC. As described in Section 1 and
Section 8.1.5, given the high unmet need and the fact that only one other FDA-approved
immunotherapy exists for NPC in the U.S., a flexible regulatory approach is applied in this case.
For Study AK105-304, as of the data cut-off date of April 29, 2024, the primary endpoint of PFS
per BICR was statistically significant at the PFS interim analysis based on 85% information
fraction. Of note, as the interim analysis of PFS was originally proposed at 70% information
fraction, this interim analysis at 85% information fraction was based on an additional 34 PFS
events. The review team considered the overrun of PFS events and the lower-than-expected
patient accrual outside of Asia to be acceptable for this particular marketing application as the
overrun is mainly due to the difficulties of enrollment outside of Asia. See FDA’s assessment
under Section 1.3 and 8.1 for “Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments” for additional details.
Similar to PFS, the first interim analysis of OS was conducted at 70% information fraction,
199
Version date: January 2020 (ALL NDA/ BLA reviews)
Disclaimer: In this document, the sections labeled as “Data” and “The Applicant’s Position” are
completed by the Applicant and do not necessarily reflect the positions of the FDA.
Reference ID: 5577575

NDA/BLA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation- BLA 761258
Penpulimab
instead of the prespecified 60% information fraction, resulting in an additional 18 OS events. OS
was not statistically significant at the first interim analysis, and thus OS will be formally tested
at the second interim analysis at 80% information fraction and, if necessary, at the final analysis
when 172 deaths are observed.
There were no major statistical issues identified during the review of Study Ak105-202. Due to
the single arm design, no statistical inferential procedures were applied, and the efficacy
decision was based on the lower limit of a 95% confidence interval of the response rate in the
trial to exceed a clinically relevant response rate with adequate duration of response. The ORR
in this pre-treated patient population was clinically relevant, and the responses were durable.
In general, the treatment benefit appeared to be consistent across all relevant subgroups. For
this study, the time-to-event endpoints of PFS and OS were considered to be descriptive due to
a lack of comparator, while the endpoint of DCR was considered to be exploratory in nature.

8.4. Conclusions and Recommendations
The FDA’s Assessment:
The demonstration of a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in PFS
favoring the penpulimab plus chemotherapy arm in AK105-304, along with a longer median
DOR in the penpulimab plus chemotherapy arm vs the placebo plus chemotherapy arm and no
evidence of a detrimental effect on OS, provides substantial evidence of effectiveness for
penpulimab, at 200 mg IV Q3W in combination with cisplatin or carboplatin and gemcitabine,
for the first-line treatment of adults with metastatic or with recurrent, locally advanced
nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). The indication for the treatment of adult patients with
metastatic NPC of nonkeratinizing histology with disease progression on or after platinum
containing chemotherapy and at least one other line of therapy is supported by Study AK105202. The ORR was 28% (95% CI: 20, 37) and median DOR was not reached. The proportion of
patients with observed DOR of at least 12 months was 46%. The results of AK105-202 are
considered clinically meaningful for the intended patient population, and the results of the
AK105-304 study provide further confidence in the benefit of penpulimab for the treatment of
advanced NPC.
The overall safety profile of penpulimab was similar to that observed with other PD-(L)1
blocking antibodies. Safety issues identified as significant and serious during the BLA review
were immune-related adverse events and infusion-related reactions, which are adequately
addressed by the information in the Warnings and Precautions section included in product
labeling. There were no significant safety concerns identified during BLA review requiring risk
management beyond labeling or warranting consideration for Risk Evaluation and Mitigation
Strategy (REMS). Penpulimab appears to have an acceptable safety profile when assessed in the
context of a life-threatening disease with unmet medical need.
