Section 21 CFR 314.106(b) outlines three requirements to establish the acceptability of foreign
data as the sole basis for marketing approval:
1. The foreign data are applicable to the U.S. population and U.S. medical
practice.
2. The studies have been performed by clinical investigators of recognized
competence.
3.
FDA is able to validate the data through an onsite inspection or other
appropriate means.
FDA will apply this policy in a flexible manner according to the nature of the drug and
data being considered.
While both AK105-304 and AK105-202 were conducted nearly or entirely exclusively in
Asia, a flexible regulatory approach is warranted given the high unmet need and lack of
available therapies for US patients with NPC. The comparator arm of cisplatin or
carboplatin plus gemcitabine used in the AK105-304 study is considered standard of
care for the first-line treatment of NPC in the US and is therefore applicable to US
medical practice. The incidence of NPC is much higher in Southeast Asia relative to the
United States, where NPC is a relatively rare disease, making enrollment to clinical trials
more feasible in that region of the world. While a higher proportion of patients with
NPC in the US have keratinizing histology compared to patients in China (25% vs 2%),
the majority of patients with NPC even in the US have non-keratinizing histology. The
company attempted to enroll patients in the US but with little success and thus had only
2 cases in AK105-304 (one on the interventional and one on the placebo arm). Due to
this very limited number of patients evaluated with keratinizing histology, and an
absence of data for penpulimab as a single agent for patients with keratinizing NPC, the
FDA narrowed the indication to locally advanced, unresectable or metastatic nonkeratinizing NPC. AK105-202 enrolled only patients with non-keratinizing NPC.
To further address the issue of applicability to the US population, the Applicant should
collect additional clinical data to further characterize the safety and efficacy of
penpulimab in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine for the treatment of NPC in a
study population whose demographic and disease characteristics are more
representative of the population of U.S. patients with NPC (refer to Section 13).
In addition, clinical site inspections were completed and Study AK105-304 appears to
have been conducted adequately and the data generated by the inspected clinical
investigators and the imaging CRO and submitted by the Applicant appear acceptable in
support of the proposed indication.
The clinical data supports a positive risk-benefit assessment and is supportive of regular
approval to penpulimab for the following indications:

12. Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS)
The Applicant’s Position:
The risks of penulimab could be managed by routine pharmacovigilance activities and labeling.
REMS is not necessary to ensure that the benefits outweigh the risk for penpulimab for the
following reasons:
204
Version date: January 2020 (ALL NDA/ BLA reviews)






The benefit of penpulimab in the treatment of NPC was demonstrated in the pivotal study
of AK105-202 and AK105-304.
The risks observed with penpulimab will be communicated through labeling. The risks
associated with penpulimab are in part due to its inhibitory effects of PD-1. If approved,
penpulimab will belong to a class with many other drugs (nivolumab, pembrolizumab,
atezolizumab, durvalumab and avelumab, etc.) in which irAEs are labeled in Warnings and
Precautions. The prescribers are likely aware of the risks of irAEs and the management with
other drugs in this class.
Sponsor has robust pharmacovigilance system, which includes data intake, case
management, regulatory reporting, literature monitoring, signal management and aggregate
reporting.
In the postmarket setting, Akeso continually conducts routine surveillance of the safety
profile of penpulimab including all reports of adverse drug experiences and product
compliant reports, and revises RMP, RSI, and package insert if an evaluation of the safety
data yields significant new information.

The FDA’s Assessment:
The clinical review team determined that a risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS) was
not required to ensure safe and effective use of penpulimab for the indicated populations.
Recommendations for the safe and effective use of penpulimab are made in labeling and a
patient package insert. There are no additional risk management strategies required beyond
the recommended labeling. Although penpulimab can cause severe/serious toxicity, there are
multiple other approved agents in the same class, and it will be prescribed by oncologists who,
by training and experience, understand how to monitor and manage such toxicities.

19.4.2.

Population PK Analysis

19.4.2.1.

Executive Summary

The FDA’s Assessment:
The PK of penpulimab in the adult population was characterized by a 2-compartment model
with first-order elimination. The population PK model described the observed data reasonably
well.
The proposed dosages of 200 mg Q2W for monotherapy and 300 mg Q3W for combination
therapy is considered acceptable for the respective proposed patient populations.
19.4.2.2.

PPK Assessment Summary

The Applicant’s Position:
Penpulimab PPK model was based on pooled data from 8 clinical studies in patients with
nasopharyngeal carcinoma, NSCLC, and other tumors. Potential covariates that may influence
Penpulimab PK and its variability were also evaluated. A total of 5,849 PK concentrations from
771 patients were included in the PPK analysis.
215
Version date: January 2020 (ALL NDA/ BLA reviews)
Disclaimer: In this document, the sections labeled as “Data” and “The Applicant’s Position” are
completed by the Applicant and do not necessarily reflect the positions of the FDA.
Reference ID: 5577575

NDA/BLA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation- BLA 761258
Penpulimab
The final PPK model was a two-compartment with zero-order IV infusion and first-order
elimination. The model indicated that baseline characteristics (body weight, C-reactive protein,
albumin, lactate dehydrogenase), ADA, tumor type, co-administration, age, sex and race had
statistically significant effects on PK parameters. However, these covariates did not have
clinically meaningful effects on the steady-state exposure (≤30%). Also, mild to moderate
hepatic impairment or mild to moderate renal impairment didn not have significant effect on
PK of Penpulimab.
Although Race was found to be correlated with clearance, the overall exposures (Cmax,ss, Cavg,ss
and Cmin,ss) were essentially the same between Caucasian and Asian populations after taking
into consideration of body weight.
According to PPK analysis, the mean (CV%) of volume of distribution was 10.2 L (43.5%),
following administration of penpulimab 200 mg as a single IV infusion. The effective half-life
and steady-state trough concentration were 22.4 days (27.4%) and 30.1 μg/mL(38.1%),
respectively, following IV infusion of 200 mg Q3W.

19.4.3.1.

E-R (Efficacy) Executive Summary

The FDA’s Assessment:
Positive E-R trends for ORR and PFS were observed across steady-state exposure with a fixed

19.4.3.2.

E-R (Efficacy) Assessment Summary

The Applicant’s Position:
Target indication: first-line treatment for recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma
(NPC). The E-R analysis included patients from the AK105-304 who received Penpulimab 200 mg
Q3W in combination with chemotherapy (n=144). the univariate logistic regression analysis
between Penpulimab Cavg,ss and ORR/DCR were explored. And Kaplan-Meier survival curve,
stratified by quartiles of exposures, was applied to explore the association between exposure
and progression-free survival (PFS). E-R analysis suggested a relative flat exposure-response
(ORR/DCR) curve and no apparent difference in exposure between responders and nonresponders.
[Highlight the key findings in the white cells.]
General Information
Goal of ER analysis

Characterize the relationships between Penpulimab serum
exposures and key efficacy endpoints, including objective
response rate (ORR) disease control rate (DCR), progression
free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), duration of response
(DOR), and time to response (TTR)

19.4.3.3.

ER (Safety) Executive Summary

The FDA’s Assessment:
Across steady-state exposure over the dosing range from 1 to 10 mg/kg Q2W including 200 mg
Q2W and 200 mg Q3W, the risk for Gr≥3 TEAEs exhibits a flat trend, whereas the risk for
immune related AEs (irAEs) exhibits a positive trend. The positive E-R trend does not appear
clinically significant given the low incidences of interruptions (5.7%) and discontinuation (1.8%)
due to irAEs.
19.4.3.4.

ER (Safety) Assessment Summary

The Applicant’s Position:
The exposure-safety response was evaluated by a univariate logistic regression model. AE
responses were used as the dependent variable, and model-predicted Penpulimab exposure
such as Cmax,ss, Cavg,ss were used as independent variables to estimate the significance levels.
In NPC population, Penpulimab (200 mg Q3W) in combination with chemotherapy, was safe
and tolerable. E-R safety analysis indicated that no apparent correlation between exposure and
incidence of TEAE/TRAE (Grade 3+) in the wide dose range (1 - 10 mg/kg Q2W) with either
monotherapy or in combination therapy.
[Highlight the key findings in the white cells.]

19.4.3.7.

Overall Benefit-Risk Evaluation Based on E-R Analyses

The Applicant’s Position:
Penpulimab 200 mg Q3W demonstrated notable clinical benefits and tolerable safety profiles in
NPC patients: the median PFS was 9.6 months (95% CI:7.1, 12.5), compared to placebo of 7.0
months (95% CI: 6.9, 7.3). E-R analysis suggested a relative flat E-R (ORR/DCR) curve and no
apparent difference in exposure between responders and non-responders. In NPC patients,
Penpulimab (200 mg Q3W) in combination with chemotherapy was safe and tolerable. E-R
safety analysis indicated that no apparent correlation between exposure and incidence of
TEAE/TRAE (Grade 3+) in the wide dose range (1 - 10 mg/kg Q2W) with either monotherapy or
in combination therapy.

Penpulimab

1. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation
1.1.

Review of Relevant Individual Trials Used to Support Efficacy

1.1.1.

Studies

1.1.1.1. Study AK105-202
Trial Design
The Applicant’s Description:
Study AK105-202 is a single-arm, open-label, multicenter phase II clinical study to evaluate the
efficacy and safety of penpulimab in patients with metastatic nonkeratinizing NPC with disease
progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and at least one other prior line of
therapy. Patients were excluded from the study based on history of autoimmune disease,
medical conditions requiring systemic immunosuppression, prior organ or allogeneic stem cell
transplantation, prior treatment with anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1 or CTLA-4 antibodies, active central
nervous system (CNS) metastases, or ECOG performance score > 2.
Patients received penpulimab 200 mg intravenously every 2 weeks until disease progression as
determined by the investigator, or unacceptable toxicity, or a maximum of 24 months,
whichever occurred first. Administration of penpulimab was permitted beyond RECIST-defined
disease progression if the patients were assessed as clinically beneficial and tolerated to the
study drug by the investigator. Tumor measurements were performed every 8 weeks in first
year and every 12 weeks thereafter, to determine response by RECIST v1.1 criteria.
The primary objective of the study was to evaluate the objective response rate (ORR) assessed
by blinded independent radiology review committee (IRRC) per RECIST v1.1. Secondary
objectives included duration of response (DoR), progression-free survival (PFS) and overall
survival (OS).
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA agrees with the Applicant’s description of the trial design for Study AK105-202. FDA
clarifies that the study was conducted at multiple sites in China. Since Study AK105-202 is a
single arm trial, FDA does not use any inferential procedures to evaluate the trial results. The
efficacy decision is based on the lower limit of a 95% confidence interval of the response rate in
the trial to exceed a clinically relevant response rate with adequate duration of response.
Additionally, time-to-event endpoints such as PFS and OS are not interpretable in a single arm
trial due to a lack of comparator and their corresponding analyses are considered as descriptive.

Study Endpoints
The Applicant’s Description:
• Primary Efficacy Endpoint: ORR assessed by IRRC per RECIST v1.1 in the Full Analysis Set
(FAS).
ORR is defined as the proportion of patients whose best overall response (BOR) is
confirmed CR or PR. The confirmation of CR or PR by repeated imaging assessments is
performed not less than 28 days (4 weeks) after the first observation of a CR or PR, and
there is no evidence of PD between the follow-up of the first observed CR or PR and the
follow-up for confirmation of CR or PR.
• Key Secondary Efficacy Endpoints: duration of response (DoR)
• Other Secondary Endpoints:
1) Efficacy: ORR assessed by investigator, Disease control rate (DCR), time to response
(TTR), PFS assessed by IRRC and investigator per RECIST v1.1 and OS
2) Pharmacokinetic (PK) and immunogenicity assessment
3) Safety: incidence and severity of adverse events, abnormal laboratory findings with
clinical significance.
4) Correlation analysis between the expression of EBV-DNA in blood and the anti-tumor
activity of penpulimab.
The FDA’s Assessment:
In general, FDA agrees with the Applicant’s description of the study endpoints. As noted in the
previous section, time-to-event endpoints such as PFS and OS are not interpretable in a single
arm study, and their corresponding analyses are considered descriptive.
Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments
The Applicant’s Description:
The sample size calculation was based on the primary endpoint of ORR. A total of 110 patients
were needed for an ORR of 15% to be excluded using the lower limit of a two-sided 95% CI. If
an ORR of 26% is assumed for penpulimab, there is 82% chance of observing at least 25
responses (an ORR of 22.7%), with the lower limit of the 95% CI excluding a historical response
rate of 15%. Considering an attrition rate of 15%, a total sample size of 130 was needed to
ensure at least 110 evaluable patiesnts. In this study, an interim analysis was originally planned
after at least 110 patients were enrolled and completed at least 16 weeks of follow-up (an
interval between the data cutoff date and the date of first dose ≥ 16 weeks), and the results of
the interim analysis was planned to be used for communicating with the regulatory agencies.
There were no plans to stop the trial based on either of these analyses and no formal statistical
tests were planned.
An interim analysis of efficacy was conducted after 110 patients treated with penpulimab had
an opportunity to be followed for at least 8 months prior to data cutoff date (to allow at least 6

Definition of Key Analysis Sets
•
Enrollment Analysis Set [ENR]
The ENR includes all patients who have signed the ICF and been enrolled into the study.
•
Primary Efficacy Population
The Primary Efficacy Population includes all patients in the ENR who have received at least one
dose of penpulimab and meet the following inclusion criteria:
Patients diagnosed with disease stage of IVb in accordance with Chinese
Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Staging 2017 (2008 Expert Consensus on Nasopharyngeal
Cancer Staging Revision) at enrollment.

Patients who had disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and
at least one other prior line of therapy. Prior neoadjuvant chemotherapy, concurrent
chemoradiotherapy, or adjuvant chemotherapy would be considered as the first line of
therapy if recurrence/metastasis occurs within 6 months since the last dose of
chemotherapy. Switching treatment regimen due to intolerability were not counted as
additional lines of therapy.

Patients with at least one measurable lesion at baseline per RECIST v1.1 as assessed
by IRRC if efficacy summary based on IRRC assessment, or at least one measurable
lesion at baseline per RECIST v1.1 as assessed by the investigator if efficacy summary
based on investigator assessment.

Patients who had an opportunity to be followed for at least 8 months prior to data
cutoff date (to allow at least 6 months follow-up past onset of response assuming the
response occurs at the first follow-up scan).


•
Safety Analysis Set
The Safety Analysis Set includes all enrolled patients who have received at least one dose of
penpulimab.
•
Pharmacokinetics Set [PKS]
The PKS includes all enrolled patients in the safety analysis set who have at least one
quantifiable concentration data at the scheduled time point and no major and critical protocol
violations affecting the concentration data.
•

Immunogenicity Set [IMMS]

The IMMS includes all enrolled patients for safety analysis who have received at least one
immunogenicity assessment at baseline and post-baseline, respectively.

The FDA’s Assessment:
In general, FDA agrees with the Applicant’s description of the primary efficacy analysis of the

considered to be an exploratory endpoint and hence, the corresponding analysis was not
verified by the FDA. There is a substantial numerical difference in ORR between the TPS ≥ 50%
(43%, (95% CI: 29, 59)) and the TPS < 50% (20%, (95% CI: 11, 30)) subgroups. Given the
exploratory nature of the subgroup analyses, the corresponding results should be interpreted
with caution.
Additionally, in “Applicant – Figure 1 Forest Plot of Objective Response Rate (ORR) Based on
RECIST 1.1 per IRRC by Subgroup Factors -- Primary Efficacy Population” the Applicant has
mislabeled the subgroup analysis by prior lines of therapy, and instead had provided analysis by
“Number of location of metastasis” twice. Among the 79 patients who received two prior lines
of systemic therapy, ORR per IRRC was 30% (95% CI: 21, 42), whereas among the 46 patients
who received at least three prior lines of therapy the ORR per IRRC was 24% (95% CI: 13, 39).

DoR and TTR
The median TTR in the primary efficacy population was 1.84 months (range: 1.6 to 7.4months).

The Applicant’s Position:
Results based on the final analysis of additional secondary efficacy variables including DoR, PFS
and OS demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness of penpulimab monotherapy in
patients with metastatic nonkeratinizing NPC with disease progression on or after at least two
prior lines of therapy, a serious disease where there is a clear unmet medical need.
The responses were durable. After a median follow-up time of 22.1 months, median DoR has
not yet been reached at the time of DCO, and 20 (57.1%) of 35 responders had an ongoing
response. The OS results were encouraging in this heavily pretreated NPC population. The
median OS was 22.74 months and the 12-month OS rate was 66.4% (95% CI: 57.2%, 74.0%). The
percentage of DoR ≥ 6 months, median OS, and the 12-month OS rate compare favorably
against those seen with chemotherapy agents.
The FDA’s Assessment:
FDA’s analysis of DOR assessed by IRRC is provided in the table below. The median DOR was not
reached. The proportion of patients with observed DOR of at least 6 months was 83%. In
addition to the landmark DOR rates provided by the Applicant, that were estimated using the
Kaplan-Meier method, FDA calculated the landmark DOR rates based on observed response
duration.

Note that, in a single arm study such as AK105-202, time-to-event endpoints such as PFS and OS
are considered descriptive only due to the absence of a comparator arm. Hence, FDA considers
PFS and OS as descriptive enponts for Study AK105-202. Additionally, the Applicant provided
analysis of OS in “Applicant – Table 9” is based on 130 enrolled patients, which is not the
efficacy population under consideration.

N/A.
The Applicant’s Position:
All patients with NPC in the primary efficacy population received penpulimab 200 mg every two
weeks. Therefore, dose response relationships for efficacy could not be evaluated. Univariate
logistic regression analyses showed a flat relationship between penpulimab PK exposures and
model-predicted ORR (CR/PR).

The FDA agrees that a dose-response relationship is not evaluable given that all patients

The FDA’s Assessment:
Please refer to the section titled “Efficacy Results – Secondary and other relevant endpoints”
for FDA’s assessment of durability of response.
Persistence of Effect
The Applicant’s Position:
The observed effect of ORR in the primary efficacy population is consistent accross prespecified subgroups as illustrated in Applicant – Table 7. Notably, patients with positive PD-L1
status exhibited substantially higher response rates compared to the overall average. Secondly,
as highlighted in the previous section, the responses are durable, with more than half of
responders (20 out of 35) maintaining an ongoing response at a median follow-up of 22.1
(b) (4)
months.
In summary, patients experienced sustained clinical benefits
with penpulimab monotherapy, demonstrating persistent efficacy across key measures.
The FDA’s Assessment:
The FDA agrees that there may potentially be persistence of effect based on the DOR data and
that higher response rates was observed in the PDL1 ≥50% population. However, as above, the
(b) (4)
secondary endpoints of PFS and
OS as this is a single arm study and these results are considered descriptive only.

Penpulimab

1. Executive Summary
1.1. Product Introduction
Penpulimab is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody targeting PD-1, thereby blocking the
immunosuppressive interaction between PD-1 and PD-L1 and PD-L2. It is not approved for any
indication in the U.S.
The recommended dosage regimen for the proposed indication is penpulimab 200 mg
intravenously (IV) every two weeks until disease recurrence or unacceptable toxicity.

1.2. Conclusions on the Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness
Data from Study AK105-202, a single arm, open label study of penpulimab in patients with
metastatic non-keratinizing NPC who had received prior therapy, conducted entirely in China,
was provided as the primary evidence in support of the proposed indication. A total of 130
patients with metastatic non-keratinizing NPC, who had progressed on platinum-based
chemotherapy and at least one other line of therapy, were enrolled and received penpulimab
200 mg every 2 weeks (Q2W). The primary efficacy outcome measure was overall response rate
(ORR) by Independent Radiologic Review Committee (IRRC) per RECIST v1.1. The key secondary
endpoint was duration of response (DOR).
Amongst the 111 patients in the primary efficacy population, the ORR was 30% (95% CI 21, 39)
(data cutoff date of February 3, 2021). The median DOR was not reached (range 3.8, 17.1+); a
total of 39% of the 33 responding patients had a DOR ≥ 9 months.
During FDA’s review of this BLA, FDA toripalimab-tpzi, an anti-PD-1 antibody, in combination
with cisplatin and gemcitabine was granted traditional approval for the first-line treatment of
adult patients with metastatic or recurrent, locally advanced NPC based on a randomized trial
which demonstrated a 3.7-month improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) with the
addition of toripalimab-tpzi to cisplatin and gemcitabine. This approval changed the standard of
care for patients with metastatic or recurrent, locally advanced NPC with the inclusion of antiPD-1-based therapy in the first-line treatment setting. At the time of this approval, toripalimabtpzi was also approved as a single agent for patients with unresectable or metastatic NPC with
disease progression on or after a platinum-containing chemotherapy based on ORR and DOR
results from a single arm study of patients with metastatic NPC (ORR 21% (95% CI 15, 28);
median DOR 14.9 months (95% CI 10.3, not estimable).
Given the approvals of toripalimab-tpzi for patients with NPC, the efficacy of penpulimab,
based on the results of Study AK105-202, does not demonstrate a clear advantage over
currently available therapeutic options for patients with metastatic, non-keratinizing NPC.
According to the U.S. Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), Section 21 314.500, new drug products
that have been studied for their safety and effectiveness in treating serious or life-threatening

is well-controlled and will lead to a product that is pure and potent.

1.3. Benefit-Risk Assessment (BRA)
Benefit-Risk Summary and Assessment
NPC is a rare, life-threatening disease with distinct geographical distribution and histologies. In 2018, approximately
129,000 new cases of NPC were diagnosed globally (0.7% of all cancers diagnosed in 2018) (Chen Lancet 2019).
There are three pathological subtypes of NPC: keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma (type 1), non-keratinizing
differentiated carcinoma (type 2), and non-keratinizing undifferentiated carcinoma (type 3). Types 2 and 3 are
typically associated with Epstein Barr virus (EBV), and account for 97% of NPC cases diagnosed in China. In North
America, Type 1 and Type 3 NPC account for 25% and 63% of cases respectively.
The prognosis for patients with recurrent, unresectable, or metastatic NPC is poor. On October 27, 2023, FDA
approved toripalimab-tpzi with cisplatin and gemcitabine for the first-line treatment of adults with metastatic or
recurrent, locally advanced NPC. In the randomized, double-blind JUPITER-02 trial, toripalimab-tpzi with cisplatin and
gemcitabine demonstrated a median progression-free survival (PFS) of 11.7 months and a median overall survival
(OS) not yet reached. Patients who received placebo with cisplatin and gemcitabine had a median PFS of 8.0 months
and median OS of 33.7 months (LOQTORZI [toripalimab-tpzi] USPI). On October 27, 2023, FDA also approved
toripalimab-tpzi as a single agent for adult patients with recurrent unresectable or metastatic NPC with disease
progression on or after a platinum-containing therapy based on results of POLARIS-02, an open-label, multicohort
trial, which demonstrated an overall response rate (ORR) as assessed by a Blinded Independent Review Committee
(BIRC) of 21% and median duration of response (DOR) of 14.9 months.
Penpulimab is a monoclonal antibody targeting programmed death-1 (PD-1), an immune checkpoint inhibitor with
an established pharmacological class of PD-1 blocking antibody. The proposed dosing regimen is 200 mg
intravenously (IV) every two weeks (Q2W) until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.
The primary efficacy data providing evidence in support of the proposed indication is derived from Study AK105-202,
a single arm, multicenter, open label study conducted in China that enrolled 130 patients with metastatic NPC who
had disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and at least one other prior line of therapy. All
patients received penpulimab 200 mg IV Q2W until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

The primary efficacy population from Study AK105-202 is comprised of 111 patients with non-keratinizing
undifferentiated NPC (64%); 32% of patients had non-keratinizing differentiated NPC, and 3.6% of patients had had
non-keratinizing NPC of unknown differentiation. In the primary efficacy population, the ORR by IRRC was 30% (95%
CI 21, 39) (data cut off February 3, 2021). Median duration of response (DOR) was not reached (range 3.8, 17.1+);
Among the 33 patients with an objective response, 39% had a DOR ≥ 9 months.
The evaluation of safety for penpulimab was primarily based upon safety data from 130 patients enrolled in Study
AK105-202 supported by a pooled population of 372 patients with advanced solid tumors or classical Hodgkin
lymphoma treated with penpulimab 200 mg Q2W. Among the 372 patients in the pooled safety population, the
most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were hepatitis (27%), hypothyroidism (24%), rash (20%), upper respiratory
tract infection (18%), pyrexia (15%), fatigue (13%), musculoskeletal pain (11%), weight increased (11%), weight
decreased (11%), colitis (11%), and cough (11%). Among the 130 patients with NPC treated with penpulimab in Study
AK105-202, the most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were hypothyroidism (32%), hepatitis (28%),
musculoskeletal pain (22%), weight decreased (17%) pyrexia (15%), rash (12%), upper respiratory tract infection
(12%), and cough (10%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 19% of the patients in the primary safety population;
the most common serious adverse reactions (≥ 1%) were pneumonia, death, hepatitis, respiratory failure,
pneumonitis, and rash.
Adverse reactions leading to permanent discontinuation of penpulimab occurred in five patients (3.8%) in the
primary safety population including one event (0.8%) each of pleural effusion, herpes zoster disseminated infection,
spinal cord compression, hepatitis, and pemphigoid. A total of four patients (3.1%) in the primary safety population
had a fatal adverse reaction; these included one event of respiratory failure and three events of death due to
unknown cause.
Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) occurred in 22% of patients, including Grade 3 to 4 irAEs in 2% of patients in
the primary safety population. The most common irAE (≥ 10%) was hypothyroidism (15%). There were no fatal irAEs
observed in the pooled or primary safety population.
The overall safety profile of penpulimab was similar to that observed with other PD-1 blocking antibodies.
A major limitation of the data is that the primary trial supporting the marketing application was conducted
exclusively in China. Therefore, the patient population is not reflective of the racial and ethnic diversity of U.S.

unmet need, penpulimab no longer addresses an unmet need for patients with NPC given the recent approvals of
toripalimab-tpzi for patients with NPC. Based on the approvals of toripalimab-tpzi, the Study AK105-202 results do

advantage for penpulimab over toripalimab-tpzi.

manufactured by Akeso Biopharma Co., Ltd. The data submitted in this application are not sufficient to support a
conclusion that the manufacture of penpulimab-kcqx is well-controlled and will lead to a product that is pure and
potent.
Given the efficacy results that do not demonstrate a clear advantage over currently available therapy and the
substantial identified manufacturing deficiencies, FDA does not consider the current data supportive of a favorable
risk-benefit assessment for penpulimab and recommends a Complete Response action.

2. Therapeutic Context
2.1. Analysis of Condition
Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a kind of malignancy arising in the top or lateral wall of
nasopharyngeal cavity. Although NPC, comprised of keratinizing, non-keratinizing
differentiated, and nonkeratinizing undifferentiated subtypes, is endemic in Southeast Asia, it is
rare in the US population (1-2 cases per 100,000). The keratinizing squamous cell subtype is
more common in the US (25% vs. 2% of NPC cases) and has a poorer prognosis, while the nonkeratinizing undifferentiated subtype is more common in Southeast Asia (95% vs. 63% of NPC
cases). Based on high-level evidence, radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy has become the
mainstay of treatment for patients with early or locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma,
and the 5-year survival rate is approximately 85%. However, tumor metastasis remains the
leading cause of treatment failure in these patients. Moreover, approximately 15% of NPC
patients develop distant metastases at initial diagnosis, and patients with recurrent/metastatic
NPC have a very poor prognosis, with a median overall survival of approximately 20 months.
The FDA’s Assessment
There were approximately 133,354 cases of NPC diagnosed worldwide in 2020 with the
majority of cases (>75%) in South and East Asia and 1.6% in Northern America, and
approximately 80,000 people died from NPC in 2020 (Globocan, 2020). NPC is rare in the United
States, with <1 case per 100,000 people each year (Cancer.Net, 2022).
The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position but notes that the Applicant provided little
information specific to the demographics or disease characteristics for patients with NPC in the
U.S. A review of data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) registry
reported by Sun et al (2017) identified 3919 patients with histologically confirmed NPC
between 2004 and 2013. Among the 3919 patients, median age was 54 years (range 44, 63) and
71% of patients were male. Information on race was included for 3672 patients with 49%
White, 12% Black, and 39% Asian (including 18% Chinese ethnicity). Information on histology
was included for 1087 patients; of these, 83% were non-keratinizing and 17% were keratinizing.

2.2. Analysis of Current Treatment Options
The Applicant’s Position
Platinum-containing chemotherapy is generally considered the standard of care for patients
with recurrent/metastatic for all types of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Currently, cisplatin in
combination with continuous intravenous infusion of fluorouracil is the global standard

progression-free survival of 7 to 11 months. However, adverse reactions, common mucosal
complications, and requirements for deep venous catheterization remain major limitations to
the fluorouracil plus cisplatin regimen. A Phase III randomized controlled study demonstrated
that gemcitabine plus cisplatin significantly improved the objective tumor response rate from
42% to 64% and the median progression-free survival from 5.6 months to 7.0 months compared
to fluorouracil plus cisplatin.
For patients who have failed platinum-containing first-line chemotherapy, the subsequent
second-line therapy depends on patient performance status, toxicity, and the time interval to
relapse after a platinum-containing regimen. For patients who have failed platinum-containing
first-line chemotherapy but have no disease progression for more than 1 year, the re-treatment
of platinum-containing combination chemotherapy may be considered. For patients who have
failed first-line platinum-containing chemotherapy and whose disease has relapsed within one
year after the chemotherapy regimen, the second-line chemotherapy includes gemcitabine,
capecitabine, or paclitaxel, monotherapy. However, after relapse on 2nd line treatment there is
no recognized standard third-line systemic therapy. Increasing evidence suggests that further
use of chemotherapy after second- or third-line chemotherapy may not prolong survival in
most patients.
It has been reported that NPC is closely associated with EB virus infection, and there is high PDL1 expression in the tumor, suggesting that PD-1 blockade may be an ideal treatment option for
NPC.
The FDA’s Assessment
The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position regarding the standard of care first and second
line therapies for advanced NPC at the time of submission of this BLA (July 2021). However, on
October 27, 2023, FDA granted traditional approval to toripalimab-tpzi in combination with
cisplatin and gemcitabine for the first-line treatment of adults with metastatic or recurrent,
locally advanced NPC based on the results of the JUPITER-02 trial. The median PFS was 11.7
months for patients treated with toripalimab-tpzi with cisplatin and gemcitabine versus 8.0
months for patients treated with placebo with cisplatin and gemcitabine (PFS HR 0.52; 95% CI
0.36, 0.74; p=0.0003). A statistically significant OS improvement was also observed with median
OS not reached (95% CI: 38.7 months, not estimable) for the toripalimab-tpzi-containing
regimen and 33.7 months (95% CI: 27.0, 44.2) for the placebo-containing regimen (HR 0.63
[95% CI: 0.45, 0.89], p-value=0.0083). On October 27, 2023, FDA also granted traditional
approval to toripalimab-tpzi as a single agent for the treatment of adults with recurrent
unresectable or metastatic NPC with disease progression on or after a platinum-containing
chemotherapy based on results of the POLARIS-02 trial. In 172 patients, the ORR by BICR was
21% (95% CI: 15, 28) and median DOR was 14.9 months (95% CI: 10.3, not estimable).

4. Nonclinical Pharmacology/Toxicology
4.1. Executive Summary
Penpulimab is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that targets programmed cell death protein
1 (PD-1); its established pharmacologic class is PD-1 blocking antibody. PD-1 is expressed on
activated T and B cells, natural killer cells, and myeloid lineage cells. Binding of PD-1 to its
ligands, programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) and PD-L2, inhibits T-cell activity, T-cell
proliferation, and cytokine production. In the tumor microenvironment, PD-1 signaling
contributes to the inhibition of T cell-mediated immune surveillance of tumors. Thus, blockade
of PD-1 signaling in the tumor microenvironment is intended to enhance tumor
immunosurveillance and anti-tumor immune responses.
In in vitro studies, penpulimab bound to human and cynomolgus monkey PD-1 but did not bind
rodent PD-1, supporting the use of cynomolgus monkeys as the single pharmacologically
relevant species for toxicity assessment. In cellular assays, penpulimab blocked the binding of
human PD-1 to human PD-L1 and PD-L2 and also competitively bound to PD-1 expressed on the
surface of human PD-1-transfected 293T cells. Additionally, penpulimab induced the secretion
of interleukin-2 (IL-2) and interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) in a mixed culture of peripheral blood
mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and dendritic cells (DCs) and in a mixed culture of PBMCs, DCs, and
Raji Burkitt lymphoma cells. Penpulimab also enhanced IFN-γ secretion by cytomegalovirus
(CMV)-responsive human PBMCs during the recall response to CMV antigen.
Given that penpulimab does not bind mouse PD-1, the Applicant investigated the in vivo antitumor activity of penpulimab in a human PD-1 knock-in genetically engineered mouse model
(HuGEMM) implanted subcutaneously with MC38 mouse colon adenocarcinoma cells.
Intraperitoneal administration of penpulimab at doses of 0.8 and 8 mg/kg twice a week for a
total of 5 doses resulted in tumor growth inhibition (TGI) compared to the isotype control. The
Applicant also evaluated the antitumor activity of penpulimab in immunodeficient mice
implanted subcutaneously with Raji cells expressing PD-L1 or a Raji-PD-L1/PBMC mixture.
Intravenous (IV) administration of penpulimab (10 mg/kg) on Days 7, 13, and 21 resulted in
greater TGI compared to the isotype control.
The Applicant evaluated the safety of penpulimab in cynomolgus monkeys in GLP-compliant
repeat-dose toxicology studies of up to 13 weeks duration. In the 6- and 13-week studies,
monkeys received IV infusion of penpulimab at doses up to 60 mg/kg once every 2 weeks.
There were no mortalities or penpulimab-related findings of toxicological significance. Target
organs of toxicity in the 6-week study were the kidney (increased cortical tubular pigment or
pigmented interstitial macrophages), spleen (increased cellularity), adrenal gland (cortical
hypertrophy), parotid salivary gland (acinar cell atrophy), thymus (increased weight); and in the
13-week study was lymph nodes (erythrophagocytosis and increased cellularity). The incidence
of anti-drug antibody formation was 63.33% in the 6-week study and 93.33% in the 13-week

study, which may explain the limited findings noted in the 13-week study. In clinical trials done
to support the approval of penpulimab in the proposed patient population, toxicities associated
with penpulimab were primarily immune-mediated adverse reactions that are predicted by its
mechanism of action. At the recommended clinical dose of 200 mg, the human AUC0-336 was
26200 µg*h/mL.
Based on its mechanism of action and data from the literature, there is potential for enhanced
immune responses to infection following treatment with penpulimab. Mycobacterium
tuberculosis (Mtb)-infected PD-1 knockout mice exhibited decreased survival compared to wildtype mice, which correlated with increased bacterial proliferation and inflammatory responses
in these animals. It is unclear whether decreased survival resulted from an inability to mount an
appropriate antibacterial response or a failure to control the immune response leading to
normal tissue destruction and organ failure (Lazar-Molnar, et al. 2010). Furthermore, in mouse
models of lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) infection, the absence of PD-1 pathway
signaling led to fatal CD8+ T cell-mediated killing of virally infected vascular endothelial cells,
systemic vascular leakage, and ultimately cardiovascular collapse (Frebel et al. 2012; Mueller et
al. 2010). Similarly, PD-L1 deficient mice died early after chronic systemic LCMV infection
(Barber et al. 2006). In addition, blockade of PD-1 with an anti-PD-1 antibody in Mtb infection in
monkeys can exacerbate the infection and lead to death and severe pulmonary stress in
infected monkeys (Kauffman et al. 2021). A brief description of these data was included in
Section 13.2 of the label to convey these potential risks to prescribers.
No reproductive or embryo-fetal developmental toxicology studies were conducted with
penpulimab. Rather, the Applicant provided a literature-based assessment of the potential
reproductive toxicity of penpulimab, consistent with the alternative approach described in the
FDA Guidance for Industry Oncology Pharmaceuticals: Reproductive Toxicity Testing and
Labeling Recommendations. Data from the literature demonstrate that the PD-1/PD-L1
pathway plays a critical role in maintaining maternal immunological tolerance to the fetus
during pregnancy. Blockade of PD-1/PD-L1 signaling in murine models of pregnancy resulted in
an increased incidence of fetal loss but no fetal malformations; however, late onset
autoimmunity can occur in PD-1-deficient mice. Based on these findings, the potential risks of
administering penpulimab during pregnancy include increased rates of abortion or stillbirth and
an increased risk in offspring of developing immune-related disorders or altering the normal
immune response. As a result, the pharmacology/toxicology team recommends a warning for
embryo-fetal toxicity in the prescribing information. Based on a half-life of penpulimab of 23.9
days, females of reproductive potential are advised to use effective contraception during
treatment with penpulimab and for 4 months after the last dose. The Applicant did not
evaluate transfer of penpulimab to the fetus or milk, but IgG antibodies can be present in milk.
Because of the potential adverse effects of penpulimab on a breastfeeding child, the review
team included recommendations in the label not to breastfeed during treatment with
penpulimab and for 4 months after the last dose. Neither genetic toxicology or carcinogenicity

4.3. Pharmacology
4.3.1. Primary Pharmacology
The FDA’s Assessment (all data presented by FDA):
Primary pharmacology studies NCS105-0001 through NCS105-00010 were reviewed under the
original IND by Dr. Wimolnut Manheng. All other pharmacology studies were reviewed under
the current BLA by Dr. Kelie Reece.
In Vitro Studies
The Applicant determined the binding affinities of penpulimab for human (Study NCS105-0001),
cynomolgus monkey (Study NCS105-0005), mouse (Study NCS105-0006), and rat PD-1 (Study
NCS105-0007) using the enzyme-linked immunoassay (ELISA). Penpulimab (0.0014–1 µg/mL)
bound to human PD-1-mFc fusion protein (human PD-1 extracellular domain fused to murine
IgG Fc domain) and monkey PD-1-hFc fusion protein (monkey PD-1 extracellular domain fused
to human IgG1 Fc domain) with EC50 values of 0.053 and 0.215 nM, respectively, but did not
bind to mouse or rat PD-1, supporting the use of cynomolgus monkeys as a pharmacologically
relevant species for toxicity assessment.
The Applicant determined the binding activity of penpulimab to PD-1 expressed on the surface
of human PD-1-transfected 293T cells (293T-PD-1 cells) by fluorescence activated cell sorting
(FACS) analysis (Study NCS105-0008). Penpulimab (0.1–20 nM) bound to human PD-1 in a dosedependent manner, with an EC50 of 2.53 nM. As assessed by surface plasmon resonance,
penpulimab (1.56–50 nM) exhibited high binding affinity for human PD-1, with a KD of 0.588 nM
(Study NCS105-0002), which was similar to the KD of the anti-PD-1 comparator antibody
nivolumab.

In Vivo Studies
Because penpulimab does not bind to mouse PD-1, male C57BL/6 mice were genetically
engineered to express a chimeric human/mouse PD-1 gene; these mice have a functional
human PD-1 with expression regulated by the mouse PD-1 promoter. The Applicant
investigated the in vivo antitumor activity of penpulimab in this human PD-1 knock-in
genetically engineered mouse model (HuGEMM) implanted subcutaneously with MC38 mouse
colon adenocarcinoma cells (Study E3174-B1701). Nivolumab (manufactured by Bristol-Myers)
was used as a comparator control. Intraperitoneal administration of 0.8 and 8 mg/kg
penpulimab twice a week for a total of 5 doses resulted in 74.1% and 54.5% TGI, respectively,
compared to the isotype control (Figure 7). Penpulimab exhibited similar in vivo antitumor
activity as nivolumab. There were no mortalities, and body weights remained stable during
treatment.

The Applicant’s Position
In the Fc domain of penpulimab, point mutations were introduced to eliminate a series of Fc
receptor mediated effects, including antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC),
antibody dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP), complement dependent cytotoxicity (CDC)
and Fc receptor mediated cytokine release. The affinity of penpulimab to Fc-receptor FcγRIIIa,
FcγRI and C1q were evaluated by Fortebio Octet molecular interaction assay and confirmed lack
of binding. Cellular assays were further conducted to evaluate the ADCC, ADCP, CDC and

4.3.3. Safety Pharmacology
The Applicant’s Position
Safety pharmacology studies were conducted during cynomolgus monkey toxicity studies, and
effect of penpulimab on vital functions in cardiovascular system, central nervous system (CNS)
and respiratory system were investigated. The evaluation of safety pharmacology endpoints
including body temperature, respiratory rate, blood oxygen saturation, electrocardiograms, and
blood pressure upon treatment with penpulimab was incorporated into the repeat-does
toxicology study in cynomolgus monkey conducted under GLP condition. There were no
treatment-related effects on body temperature, respiratory rate, blood oxygen saturation,
electrocardiograms, or blood pressure found in the repeat dose toxicology study. Thus, no
specific concerns were observed on vital functions in cardiovascular system, CNS, and
respiratory system.
The FDA’s Assessment
The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s conclusions. In vivo, cardiovascular parameters were
assessed pre-treatment; 2 to 5 hours after dosing on Days 1, 15, 29, and 43; and 1 day prior to
recovery necropsy (Day 84) in the 13-week repeat-dose monkey study. Findings were reviewed
under the General Toxicology below (Section 5.5.1). There were no toxicologically significant
changes observed at doses up to 60 mg/kg/day.

4.5. Toxicology
4.5.1. General Toxicology
The Applicant’s Position
In 6-week repeat-dose toxicity study, no apparent toxicity was observed in cynomolgus
monkeys following intravenous infusion of penpulimab at 4, 15, or 60 mg/kg once every two
weeks for 6 weeks. Treatment-related histopathological change of kidneys (increased cortical
tubular pigment or pigmented interstitial macrophages) was noted in some animals but no
impact on kidney functions. Pigment in the cortical tubular epithelium of the kidneys is not
reported as a common background finding in cynomolgus monkeys. In this study, there were no
apparent changes in clinical chemistry, urinalysis, or organ weights which would indicate an
impact of treatment on kidney function. There were also no other histopathological changes
associated with the pigment which were indicative of damage to the kidneys. These changes
were therefore considered not to be adverse. The no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL)
was considered to be 60 mg/kg.
In 13-week repeat-dose toxicity study, no apparent toxicity and histopathological change of
kidney was observed in cynomolgus monkeys following intravenous infusion of penpulimab at
4, 15, or 60 mg/kg once every two weeks for 13 weeks, the NOAEL was considered to be 60
mg/kg.
The FDA’s Assessment
In general, the FDA agrees with the Applicant’s assessment of the toxicology data. In the 6week repeat-dose toxicology study, clinical chemistry findings included a dose-dependent
decrease in total bilirubin and increase in creatine kinase levels at all dose levels in males, which
were present at the end of the recovery period. In addition to the kidney, as noted by the
Applicant, other target organs of toxicity in the 6-week study were the spleen (increased
cellularity of the red and white pulp), adrenal gland (cortical hypertrophy), parotid salivary
gland (acinar cell atrophy), and thymus (increased weight). Changes in the adrenal gland,
spleen, and thymus (females) were present at the end of the recovery period. Of the 30
monkey serum samples tested, 19 were ADA-positive with an incidence of 63.33%.
In the 13-week toxicity study, histological findings included erythrophagocytosis and increased
cellularity in the lymph nodes (inguinal, mandibular, mesenteric), which were present at the
end of the recovery period. Limited findings may be reflective of ADA formation. Of the 30
monkey serum samples tested, 28 were ADA-positive with an incidence of 93.33%.

4.5.4. Reproductive and Developmental Toxicology
The Applicant’s Position
Fertility, embryonic fetal development, or pre- and postnatal developmental toxicity studies
were not conducted with penpulimab. As described in ICH Guidance S9, fertility and early
embryonic developmental toxicity study is not warranted for marketing of pharmaceuticals for
the treatment of patients with advanced cancer. Information available from general toxicology
studies on the pharmaceutical’s effect on reproductive organs were used as the basis of the
assessment of impairment of fertility. In the 6-week and 13-week repeat-dose toxicity studies,
there were no notable effects in the male and female reproductive organs.
Embryo-fetal development toxicity studies were not conducted with penpulimab. Literature
data shows that a central function of the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway is to preserve pregnancy by
maintaining maternal immune tolerance to the fetus. Blockade of PD-L1 signaling has been
shown in murine models of pregnancy to disrupt tolerance to the fetus and to increase fetal
loss. There are potential reproductive risks when giving penpulimab during pregnancy,
including increased rates of miscarriage or stillbirth. Penpulimab is an IgG1 antibody drug with
high affinity to human FcRn, thus it is expected to cross the placenta during third-trimester
pregnancy in human, though the exposure of penpulimab in fetus under treatment dose level is
undetermined. Based on its mechanism of action, fetal exposure to penpulimab may increase
the risk of developing immune-mediated disorders or altering the normal immune response
and immune-mediated disorders have been reported in PD-1 knockout mice.
Pre- and postnatal toxicity studies were not conducted with penpulimab. As described in ICH
Guidance S9, pre- and postnatal toxicity study is not warranted for marketing of
pharmaceuticals for the treatment of patients with advanced cancer.
The FDA’s Assessment
The FDA agrees that dedicated reproductive and developmental toxicity studies are not needed
to support this BLA submission. To address the potential effects of penpulimab on embryo-fetal
development, the Applicant submitted an assessment of the potential reproductive toxicity of
penpulimab using a weight-of-evidence approach. The FDA agrees that this approach is
reasonable.

Reference ID: 5313694

NDA/BLA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation- BLA 761258
Penpulimab
The PD-1/PD-L1 pathway plays a critical role in maintaining maternal immunological tolerance
to the fetus during pregnancy (Guleria et al. 2005). PD-L1 is expressed in the human placenta
throughout pregnancy and at the maternal-fetal interface in fetal villous syncytiotrophoblasts
and extravillous cytotrophoblasts (Petroff et al. 2003). Blockade of PD-L1 signaling in murine
models of pregnancy disrupts tolerance to the fetus, resulting in increased fetal loss (Guleria et
al. 2005).
Penpulimab is a humanized IgG1 antibody, and human IgG is known to cross the placenta; thus,
penpulimab may be transmitted from the mother to the fetus. Based on its mechanism of
action and findings from murine models of pregnancy (Guleria et al. 2005), administration of
penpulimab is likely to disrupt the maintenance of normal pregnancy. Potential risks associated
with administration of penpulimab during pregnancy include increased rates of abortion and
stillbirth. In addition, as PD-1 knockout mice develop late onset autoimmune phenotypes
(Okazaki and Honjo 2007), fetal exposure to penpulimab may alter the normal immune
response or increase the risk of developing immune-related disorders. As inhibition of the PD1/PD-L1 pathway can lead to increased risk of immune-mediated rejection of the developing
fetus, resulting in fetal death, a warning for embryofetal toxicity is recommended for
penpulimab. Based on a half-life of approximately 24 days, females of reproductive potential
are advised to use effective contraception during treatment with penpulimab and for 4 months
after the last dose of penpulimab.
Fertility studies have not been conducted with penpulimab and are not needed to support a
BLA for the proposed indication. In 6- and 13-week repeat-dose toxicity studies in monkeys,
there were no notable effects on male and female reproductive organs up to the highest dose
tested of 60 mg/kg (approximately ≥4.7 times the human exposure based on AUC at the 200 mg
clinical dose); however, most animals in these studies were not sexually mature.
4.5.5. Other Toxicology Studies
The Applicant’s Position
The investigation of tissue cross-reactivity of penpulimab with normal human and normal
cynomolgus monkey frozen tissues revealed that penpulimab reacted with normal human
spleen and lymph nodes and normal cynomolgus monkey spleen, mesenteric lymph node,
thymus, jejunum, and colon. PD-1 is expressed on the surface of activated T cells, B cells, and
macrophages, and as the results of penpulimab tissue cross-reactivity (TCR) studies showed no
unexpected binding of penpulimab to human or cynomolgus monkey tissues was found. In
hemolysis study, penpulimab at the concentration of 10 mg/mL had no hemolytic or
aggregation effect on human red blood cells.

Literature-Based Assessment of Potential for Effects of Infection
Reviewed by Drs. Shawna Weis and Stephanie Aungst.
While loss of PD-1 function enhances clearance of some tumors and viral infections, it increases
susceptibility to certain other pathogens such as tuberculosis in some animal models.
PD-1-deficient mice (C57BL/6) infected with M. tuberculosis exhibited a decrease in survival,
which correlated with uncontrolled bacterial proliferation and a larger inflammatory response
in the lungs of PD-1-deficient mice compared with wild-type controls. Thus, PD-1 appears to be
required to control infection and the inflammatory responses in the lungs of mice infected with
M. tuberculosis (Lazar-Molnar, et al. 2010); however, the pathogenesis of this observation has
not been clearly-defined. In particular, it is unclear whether the decreased survival reflects
rampant bacterial growth resulting from an inability to mount appropriate antibacterial
responses and/or whether it is a failure to downregulate the immune reaction that leads to
massive tissue destruction and organ failure.
In a recent publication, Kauffman et al. (2021) evaluated the role of PD-1 during Mycobacterium
tuberculosis (Mtb) infection of rhesus macaques. Monkeys (~2 years old; males) were infected
with 30-50 colony forming units of fluorescently labeled Mtb into the right lower lung lobe.
Tissue from Mtb infected monkeys was harvested 15-16 weeks post infection and assessed for
PD-1 expression using flow cytometry. Additional Mtb infected monkeys were intravenously
infused with 10 mg/kg of isotype control (DSPR4) or a primatized anti-PD-1 monoclonal
antibody (n=6/group) at 2, 4, 6-, 8-, 10-, and 13-weeks post infection to determine the role of
PD-1 during an Mtb infection. PET scans and 18FDG (18F-fluoro-2-deoxy-D-glucose) uptake,
granuloma size and number, and colony forming units per granuloma were used to evaluate
infection. Monkeys in both studies were necropsied at 15-16 weeks post infection. Treatment
of Mtb infected monkeys with an anti-PD-1 antibody led to early euthanasia in one monkey due
to severe pulmonary stress and another monkey developed cachexia and showed elevated
18FDG uptake in the lungs but survived until study termination. PD-1 expression in Mtb
infected monkeys occurred more frequently on antigen specific CD4 and CD8 T cells in lung
granulomas compared to other tissues. Mtb infected monkeys treated with an anti-PD-1
showed similar numbers of granulomas compared to controls, but these were characterized as
larger granulomas, with increased 18FDG uptake and a higher bacterial load. The increased
bacterial loads noted with PD-1 blockade occurred primarily within the site of infection
(pulmonary lymph nodes and granulomas), suggesting it did not result in disseminated
infection. The mechanism underlying the increased bacterial loads after PD-1 blockade in Mtb
infection are not clear, but IFNγ and TNF have been previously implicated. Evaluation of
cytokines in granulomas of isotype and anti-PD-1 treated monkeys indicated that IFNγ, TNF, and
46

5. Clinical Pharmacology
5.1. Executive Summary
The FDA’s Assessment
Penpulimab is a programmed death receptor 1 (PD-1) blocking antibody and it is a humanized
immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) immunoglobulin. The Applicant seeks accelerated approval of
penpulimab for the treatment of patients with metastatic non-keratinizing nasopharyngeal
carcinoma (NPC) in patients with disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy
and at least one other prior line of therapy. The proposed recommended dosage of penpulimab
(b) (4)
is 200 mg every 2 weeks (Q2W) in adult
The Clinical Pharmacology review team evaluated the immunogenicity, population
pharmacokinetic (PPK), and exposure-response (E-R) data obtained from Study AK105-202. PPK
analyses of the adult data suggest that there was no clinically significant effect of various
covariates (e.g., age, sex, body weight, mild and moderate renal or hepatic impairment, and
ECOG status) on penpulimab PK. The effect of race and ethnicity on penpulimab PK was not
fully characterized, given that the patients in PPK dataset did not represent the overall racial
and ethnic diversity of the US patient population. As part of the post-marketing requirement
(PMR), the Applicant will collect sparse PK samples in the confirmatory clinical trial that
includes sufficient representation of racial and ethnic diversity of the US patient population for
supportive PPK analyses. The E-R analysis for efficacy was considered to be inconclusive, given
that data were limited with one dose level. The E-R analyses for safety did not identify any
apparent correlation between exposures and treatment emergent adverse events (any TEAEs
or TEAEs ≥ Grade 3).
As Study AK105-202 was conducted in China, FDA assessed whether the proposed penpulimab
dosing regimen is appropriate for the US population. Simulation based on the PPK model
showed similar exposure of penpulimab in virtual patients from the US as compared to that of
patients from China with mean exposure (Cmax,ss, Cmin,ss, and AUCss) difference less than 20%
between these two populations. Therefore, the 200 mg Q2W dosing regimen appears
appropriate for US patients based this analysis; the confirmatory trial will provide additional
data to evaluate and confirm the acceptability of the recommended dosage in the US patient
population.

The incidences of treatment emergent anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) and neutralizing antibodies
(NAbs) against penpulimab were 27% and 7%, respectively in Study AK105-202. There was no
clear evidence of any clinically relevant impact of anti-penpulimab antibody development on
penpulimab PK. There is insufficient information to characterize the effects of anti-penpulimab
antibodies on the pharmacodynamics, safety, and efficacy of penpulimab.

Penpulimab

5.2. Summary of Clinical Pharmacology Assessment
Data
Penpulimab is a humanized immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) monoclonal antibody targeting
programmed cell death-1 (PD-1). Penpulimab binds specifically to human PD-1 with high affinity
and competitively blocks the binding of PD-1 to its ligand programmed cell death-1 (PD-L1) and
programmed cell death ligand-2 (PD-L2), thereby relieving immunosuppression of T
lymphocytes, promoting the proliferation of lymphocytes and the secretion of related
cytokines, and ultimately recovering cytotoxic activities of T cells to block tumor growth.
The typical antibody structure of penpulimab is composed of two heavy chains of IgG1 and two
light chains of kappa subclass, which are covalently linked to each other by disulfide bonds.
Penpulimab was engineered to eliminate Fc receptor mediated effector function, consequently,
may prevent ADCC and ADCP mediated depletion of PD-1 expressing T lymphocytes. This may
help preserve maximal anti-tumor activity of lymphocytes. The Fc mutation also causes reduced
induction of proinflammatory cytokines like IL-6 and IL-8, which may help reduce immune
related adverse events commonly seen for a typical PD-1 antibody.
Pharmacokinetic (PK) data of penpulimab were derived from 4 clinical studies. A total of 379
patients were included in the population PK analysis and 320 patients (including 31 patients
who underwent intensive sampling) were included in the non-compartmental model-based PK
analysis. The above patients received penpulimab at 1, 3 or 10 mg/kg or 200 mg Q2W.
According to the non-compartmental analysis, the drug exposure, expressed as peak
concentration (Cmax ) and area under the concentration-time curve from 0 h to day 14 postdose
(AUC0-14d) increased proportionally within the dose range of 1 mg/kg to 10 mg/kg. Following
single-dose and multi-dose IV infusion of penpulimab (200 mg Q2W, n=11), the mean peak
concentration at steady-state (Cmax,ss) was 136 μg/mL, the mean average concentration at
steady-state (Cavg,ss) was 88.5 μg/mL, the mean trough concentration at steady-state (Cmin,ss)
was 58.7 μg/mL, the mean area under the concentration-time curve at dose interval (AUC(0-tau))
was 29900 h*μg/mL. The mean accumulation rate (±SD) calculated based on Cmax and area
under the concentration-time curve (AUC) on Cycle3 Day15 (the 6th dose) was 1.84 ± 0.495 and
2.69 ± 0.749, respectively, a likely tendency of drug accumulation following multi-dose
administration of penpulimab.
Penpulimab is administered via IV infusion and the drug directly enters blood circulation.
According to population PK simulation, after a single IV infusion of penpulimab at 200 mg, the
volume of distribution (Vz )(±SD) was 7.18 ± 2.52 L, the volume of distribution at steady-state
(VSS)(±SD) was 6.59 ± 2.01 L, the clearance (CL)(±SD) was 0.223 ± 0.0740 L/d, and the half-life(
t1/2)(±SD) was 23.9 ± 9.98 days.
Receptor occupancy (RO) is an important measure of the in vivo biological activity of
penpulimab and also an important parameter underlying the determination of the
recommended dose in clinical studies. In the Phase Ia clinical study conducted in Australia

(AK105-101 study), patients with advanced solid tumors received penpulimab therapy (1, 3 and

cohorts. No apparent correlation between RO value and dose level was noted.
The Applicant’s Position
Penpulimab exhibited linear PK in patients who received penpulimab by intravenous
administration within the dose range of 1 mg/kg to 10 mg/kg. Population pharmacokinetic
analysis indicated that distribution of penpulimab was limited to the central vascular
compartment with an elimination half-life of 23.9 days and mild drug accumulation upon repeat
dosing.
The FDA’s Assessment
The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position that the exposure to penpulimab increased dose
proportionally over the dose range of 1 mg/kg to 10 mg/kg after a single dose. It is unknown
whether the clearance of penpulimab is time-dependent after multiple doses given the limited
availability of PK data.
5.2.1. General Dosing
Data
In the Phase Ia dose-escalation trial, no DLT occurred at the highest dose cohort of 10 mg/kg
Q2W and no maximum tolerated dose (MTD) was explored, therefore the maximum
administered dose (MAD) for this study was 10 mg/kg Q2W. Phase Ia PK data showed a linear
relationship between exposure of penpulimab and dose over the dose range of 1 mg/kg Q2W
to 10 mg/kg Q2W; receptor occupancy analysis showed 80% to 100% PD-1 receptor occupancy
starting on day 2 after administration. There was no significant difference in receptor
occupancy between 1, 3 and 10 mg/kg doses level. The efficacy results showed anti-tumor
activities at doses ranging from 1 mg/kg to 10 mg/kg Q2W. Since higher drug concentrations
can be obtained with the 3 mg/kg dosing regimen than with the 1 mg/kg dosing regimen, this
may ensure to achieve more stable blood concentrations after multiple doses for better
sustained receptor occupancy.
Results of study AK105-101 showed that, following administration of penpulimab 1 mg/kg, 3
mg/kg, and 10 mg/kg as a single IV infusion, drug exposure expressed as Cmax and AUC(0-14d)
increased proportionally with dose from 1 mg/kg to 10 mg/kg; the 90% confidence interval (CI)
of β values of AUC(0-14d) and Cmax was 0.676-1.15 and 0.844-1.13, respectively; namely, a linear
PK profile was exhibited.
Based on the final PopPK model, serum concentrations were simulated for 379 patients after IV
infusion of 200 mg penpulimab, and PK parameters were calculated by non-compartmental
modeling. Simulated PK parameters following single-dose IV infusion of penpulimab 200 mg are

Population PK simulation of steady-state drug concentrations following administration of
penpulimab 200 mg Q2W in 379 patients are presented. In vitro studies indicated 0.2 µg/mL
penpulimab was associated with a receptor occupancy close to 90%. Population PK analysis
showed that, with a penpulimab dose of 200 mg Q2W, the steady-state trough concentration in
more than 97.5% of patients was >10 μg/mL, which is 100-fold higher than those at which 80%
of the receptors (0.1 µg/mL) could be occupied or 20-fold higher than those at which
90%~100% of the receptors (0.5 µg/mL) could be occupied.
Simulated drug concentrations of 379 patients after IV infusion of penpulimab with fixed dose
regimen (200 mg Q2W) and body weighted adjustment (3 mg/kg Q2W) using a population PK
model showed that the trough concentration, peak concentration, and variation range were
basically the same between these two regimen, thus supporting a fixed dose regimen of 200 mg
Q2W.
A logistic regression analysis was performed to examine exposure-efficacy and exposure-safety
relationship. Results of the univariable analyses evaluating relationships between efficacy
(Complete response or partial response: CR/PR) and PK exposure (observed serum
concentration at: Cycle 1 Day 1 end of infusion, Cycle 2 Day 1 before infusion, Cycle 5 Day 1
before infusion, or simulated steady state exposure) demonstrated a relatively flat exposureresponse relationship without dose dependency.
The relationship between PK exposure (the same as above) and safety response (any TRAE or
TRAE >=3) were analyzed by logistics regression. And the result showed no apparent correlation
between safety and drug exposure.
The Applicant’s Position
The recommended dosage of penpulimab was 200 mg Q2W administered with intravenous
infusion (IV). Dose selection is based on the following considerations:
•

In all patients treated with penpulimab therapy, penpulimab 200 mg Q2W was safe and
tolerable, and there was no apparent correlation between the incidence of TRAEs and drug
exposure.

Penpulimab 200 mg Q2W showed notable clinical benefits in patients with NPC and

In vitro studies showed that 0.5 μg/mL of penpulimab resulted in 90-100% receptor

The FDA’s Assessment
FDA generally agrees that the proposed recommended dosage of 200 mg Q2W is supported by
the observed clinical safety, efficacy, and pharmacodynamic data. FDA disagrees that it can be
concluded that the E-R analysis for efficacy is relatively flat; FDA concludes that the E-R analysis
for efficacy is inconclusive given that the analysis only included one dose level. FDA also found
no correlation between safety and penpulimab exposure given FDA did not identify any
apparent correlation between the incidence of TEAEs and drug exposure (refer to Appendix
19.4 for details).
As Study AK105-202 was conducted in China, FDA assessed whether the proposed penpulimab
dosing regimen is appropriate for the US population. Simulation based on PPK model showed
similar exposure of penpulimab in US virtual patients as compared to that in Chinese patients
with mean exposure (Cmax,ss, Cmin,ss, and AUCss) difference less than 20% between these two
populations. Therefore, the 200 mg Q2W dosing regimen appears appropriate for US patients
based on PK comparability with Chinese patients.

Body Weight
The median weight was 62.0 kg (range: 35.2 - 113.0 kg). Population PK covariate screening
results showed that penpulimab Volume of distribution of central compartment (V1 ) increased

parameters (AUCSS, Cmax,SS, Ctrough,SS) in patients with weights at 10% and 90% quantile levels

differences were less than 30%. Hence, it is considered that the impact of weight on AUCSS,
Cmax,SS and Ctrough,SS was not clinically significant.
Renal Impairment
In accordance with the Guidance on Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal Function
released by FDA in 2020, renal impairment in the 379 patients included into the population PK
analysis set was graded by creatinine clearance (CLCr). The grading criteria and included
patients are summarized as follows. Normal renal function, CLCr ≥ 90 mL/min (n=220); mild
renal impairment: CLCr < 90 mL/min and CLCr ≥ 60 mL/min (n=113); moderate renal
impairment: CLCr < 60 mL/min and CLCr ≥ 30 mL/min (n=45); 1 patient with severe renal
impairment (CLCr < 30 mL/min) has been included.
Through population PK covariate screening, it was found that the renal function related factor
(CLCr) did not have a statistically significant impact on population PK parameters of
penpulimab .The results showed that there was no significant difference in clearance between
patients with mild or moderate renal impairment and patients with normal renal function.
Data of penpulimab in patients with severe renal impairment are not adequate.

Ctrough,SS was not clinically significant.

5.3. Comprehensive Clinical Pharmacology Review
5.3.1. General Pharmacology and Pharmacokinetic Characteristics
Data
The clinical pharmacology of penpulimab has been studied in patients with malignant solid
tumors such as NPC or non-solid tumors such as cHL who received penpulimab by intravenous
infusion administration once every 2 weeks. Levels of serum penpulimab were measured using
validated methods and the results were used to evaluate PK parameters.
PK data of penpulimab were derived from 4 clinical studies. A total of 379 patients were
included into population PK analysis, and 320 patients (including 31 who underwent intensive
sampling) into non-compartmental model-based PK analysis. The above patients received
penpulimab at 1, 3 or 10 mg/kg or 200 mg Q2W. The PK profile is outlined as follows:
Absorption
Penpulimab is administered via IV infusion, and the drug directly enters blood circulation.
Distribution
As the sampling interval after the first dose was short (Day 1 to Day 15), the serum
concentration of penpulimab had not reached the terminal part of the elimination phase, so Vz
calculated in non-compartmental PK analysis was analyzed based on population PK simulated
data.
According to population PK simulation, following administration of penpulimab 200 mg as a
single IV infusion, the Vz (±SD) of penpulimab was 7.18 ± 2.52 L, and the VSS(±SD) was 6.59 ±
2.01 L.
Elimination
As the sampling interval after the first dose was short (Day 1 to Day 15), the serum
concentration of penpulimab had not reached the terminal part of the elimination phase, so CL
and t1/2 calculated in non-compartmental PK analysis were analyzed based on population PK
simulated data.

Penpulimab
According to population PK simulation, following administration of penpulimab 200 mg as a
single IV infusion, the CL(±SD) of penpulimab was 0.223 ± 0.0740 L/d, and the half-life(t1/2)(±SD)
was 23.9 ± 9.98 d.
Linearity/Non-Linearity
According to the non-compartmental analysis, the drug exposure, expressed as Cmax and AUC(014d), increased proportionally with dose within the dose range of 1 mg/kg to 10 mg/kg following
single-dose IV infusion of penpulimab. Following multi-dose IV infusion of penpulimab (200 mg
Q2W, n=11), the mean accumulation rate (±SD) calculated based on Cmax and AUC on
Cycle3Day15 (the 6th dose) was 1.84 ± 0.495 and 2.69 ± 0.749, respectively.
Steady-State
According to population PK simulation, the penpulimab concentration was approximate to the
steady state at Week 16 following IV infusion of penpulimab 200 mg Q2W. The mean steadystate trough concentration (±SD) at Week 16 was 49.4 ± 17.5 μg/mL.
Other Population PK Analysis Results
The population PK profile of penpulimab could be described using a two-compartmental model
with first order elimination. Typical values of penpulimab PK parameters based on the final
model were as follows: CL, 0.233 L/day; V1, 3.40 L; distribution rate from central compartment
to peripheral compartment (Q), 0.706 L/day; volume of distribution of peripheral compartment
(V2) 3.02 L. Covariate analysis showed that age, race, immunogenicity, hepatic function related
factors (TBIL, AST, ALT, ALP), renal function (CLCr), tumor type and LDH score did not have an
impact on PK parameters of penpulimab; the impacts of weight, ALB, ECOG and sex on CL and
impacts of weight and sex on V1 were statistically significant, but these factors were not
clinically significant.
According to population PK analysis results, compared to patients with normal renal function,
mild or moderate renal impairment did not have a significant impact on PK and does not
necessitate dose modifications; compared to patients with normal hepatic function, mild or
moderate hepatic impairment did not have a significant impact on PK and does not necessitate
dose modifications; data in patients with severe hepatic or renal function are inadequate.
Immunogenicity Results
In clinical studies in patients treated with penpulimab at a dose of 1 mg/kg every 2 weeks, 3
mg/kg every 2 weeks, 200 mg every 2 weeks, or 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks, 43 (12.3%) of 349
evaluable patients tested positive for treatment-emergent anti-penpulimab antibodies of
whom 14 (4.0%) patients had neutralizing antibodies against penpulimab. The treatment
emergent ADA did not have a significant impact on the PK exposure or safety.

The Applicant’s Position
The information from clinical studies contributing to the clinical pharmacology evaluation of
penpulimab was included in the submitted reports (Module 2.7.2 Summary of Clinical
Pharmacology, Module 5.3.5.2 AK105-202 CSR). Penpulimab exhibited linear PK (from dose 1
mg/kg to 10 mg/kg) with an estimated terminal half-life of 23.9 days and indicating a likely
tendency of drug accumulation following multi-dose administration of penpulimab.
No dedicated clinical drug-drug interaction studies have been conducted in humans.
Penpulimab is a humanized monoclonal antibody, PK interactions with other drugs have not
been studied. As monoclonal antibodies are not metabolized by cytochrome P450 (CYP) or
other drug metabolizing enzymes, inhibition, or induction of these enzymes by co-administered
medicinal products is not anticipated to affect the pharmacokinetics of penpulimab.
Overall, penpulimab administered by intravenous infusion at fixed 200mg Q2W regimen,
demonstrated a favorable benefit-risk profile for patients with metastatic NPC patients in
patients with metastatic nonkeratinizing NPC with disease progression on or after platinumbased chemotherapy and at least one other prior line of therapy.

The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s summary of the PK characteristics of penpulimab.

and NAbs in the Phase 1 study conducted in Australia and the three Phase 2 studies conducted

patients for treatment emergent NAb. Per PPK analysis, treatment emergent ADA had no
significant impact on penpulimab PK. There is insufficient information to characterize the
effects of anti-penpulimab antibodies on the safety and efficacy of penpulimab.

5.3.2. Clinical Pharmacology Questions
5.3.2.1. Does the Clinical Pharmacology Program Provide Supportive
Evidence of Effectiveness?
Yes, the clinical pharmacology program provides supportive evidence of penpulimab
effectiveness in patients with metastatic nonkeratinizing NPC with disease progression on or
after platinum-based chemotherapy and at least one other prior line of therapy.
Data
For AK105-202 study, patients with stage IVb NPC who have failed at least 2 lines of prior
therapy containing platinum-based chemotherapy were enrolled in the study. Among the 111
patients included in the primary efficacy population, 33 patients had a BOR of confirmed CR or
PR based on IRRC assessment, with a confirmed ORR of 29.7% (95% CI: 21.4%, 39.1%).
To support the clinical efficacy observed with penpulimab dosed at fixed 200mg Q2W regimen,
exposure-efficacy relationship was evaluated in NPC population (AK105-202 study), see
[Module 2.7.2, Section 3.3.1]. Univariate logistic regression analysis was conducted to assess
the relationship between penpulimab PK exposures and model-predicted ORR response
(CR/PR). Results of the univariate analyses demonstrated a relatively flat exposure-response
curve without apparent correlation between efficacy (CR/PR) and PK exposure (observed serum
concentration: Cycle 1 Day 1 end of infusion, Cycle 2 Day 1 before infusion, Cycle 5 Day 1 before
infusion, or simulated steady state exposure such as AUCτ,SS, Cmax,SS, Ctrough,SS) .
The Applicant’s Position
Penpulimab 200 mg Q2W showed notable clinical benefits in patients with metastatic NPC and
demonstrated a relatively flat exposure-response curve as above without apparent correlation
between efficacy (CR/PR) and drug exposure. Penpulimab therapy is recommended treatment
until disease progression or intolerable toxicity to allow continued blockade of the PD-1
pathway. The safety profile of penpulimab 200 mg Q2W in 130 patients with NPC from AK105202 is consistent with the well-characterized safety profile of penpulimab 200 mg/kg Q2W in
372 patients with various solid tumors or blood tumors and in line with the known safety profile
of other mAbs with similar mechanism of action.
The FDA’s Assessment
FDA generally agrees with the Applicant’s position. However, FDA notes that the Applicant’s E-R
analysis for efficacy is inconclusive due to limited exposure range of penpulimab at one dose
level.
