5.3.2.2. Is the Proposed Dosing Regimen Appropriate for the General Patient
Population for Which the Indication Is Being Sought?
Yes, penpulimab administered by intravenous infusion at 200mg Q2W regimen is appropriate
for patients with metastatic nonkeratinizing NPC with disease progression on or after platinumbased chemotherapy and at least one other prior line of therapy. The proposed dosing regimen
is supported by the observed efficacy, safety, and PK data.
Data
In the Phase Ia dose-escalation trial, no DLT occurred at the highest dose cohort of 10 mg/kg
Q2W and no MTD was explored, therefore the maximum administered dose(MAD) for this
study was 10 mg/kg Q2W. Phase Ia PK data showed a linear relationship between exposure of
penpulimab and dose over the dose range of 1 mg/kg Q2W to 10 mg/kg Q2W; receptor
occupancy analysis showed 80% to 100% PD-1 receptor occupancy starting on day 2 after
dosing. There was no significant difference in receptor occupancy between the 1, 3 and 10
mg/kg doses. According to the non-compartmental analysis, the drug exposure, expressed as
Cmax and AUC(0-14d), increased proportionally with dose within the dose range of 1 mg/kg to 10
mg/kg following single-dose IV infusion of penpulimab.
In vitro studies showed that 0.5 μg/mL of penpulimab resulted in 90-100% receptor occupancy.
According to the population PK analysis of penpulimab, at the dose of 200 mg Q2W, more than
97.5 % of patients achieved steady-state trough concentrations (10µg/ml), which is at or above
20 times the concentrations corresponding to 90-100% RO.
Univariate logistic regression analysis was conducted to assess the relationship between
penpulimab PK exposures and model-predicted ORR response (CR/PR). Results of the univariate
analyses demonstrated a relatively flat exposure-response curve without apparent correlation
between efficacy (CR/PR) and PK exposure (observed serum concentration: Cycle 1 Day 1 end of
infusion, Cycle 2 Day 1 before infusion, Cycle 5 Day 1 before infusion, or simulated steady state
exposure such as AUCτ,SS, Cmax,SS, Ctrough,SS).
Similarly, univariate logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate the relationship
between safety and PK exposure. The same reference points described above were used for PK
exposure, while safety endpoints were any TRAE or TRAE ≥ grade 3 occurred in the integrated
penpulimab 200 mg population from 4 clinical monotherapy studies. The analysis showed no
apparent correlation between safety parameters of interest and PK exposure.
The population PK result showed that age, race, immunogenicity, hepatic function related
factors (TBIL, AST, ALT, ALP), renal function (CLCr), tumor type and LDH score have no impact
on PK parameters of penpulimab. While weight, ALB, ECOG and sex on CL and impacts of
weight and sex on V1 were statistically significant, but these factors were not clinically
significantly relevant. Renal function and hepatic function did not have a significant impact on
PK and does not necessitate dose modifications; data in patients with severe hepatic or renal
function are inadequate.

5.3.2.3. Is an Alternative Dosing Regimen or Management Strategy Required
for Subpopulations Based on Intrinsic Patient Factors?
No, penpulimab administered by intravenous infusion at 200mg Q2W regimen is appropriate
for patients with metastatic nonkeratinizing NPC with disease progression on or after platinumbased chemotherapy and at least one other prior line of therapy.
Data
The population PK profile of penpulimab could be described using a two-compartmental model
with first order elimination. Covariate analysis showed that age, race, hepatic function related
factors (TBIL, AST, ALT, ALP), renal function (CLCr), tumor type and LDH score did not have an
impact on PK parameters of penpulimab; the impacts of weight, ALB, ECOG and sex on CL and
impacts of weight and sex on V1 were statistically significant, but these factors were not
clinically significantly relevant. There was no significant difference in clearance between
patients with different grades of renal function or hepatic function.
In summary, mild or moderate renal impairment did not have a significant impact on
penpulimab PK as compared with patients with normal renal function. Data of penpulimab in
patients with severe renal impairment are not adequate. Mild or moderate hepatic impairment
did not have a significant impact on penpulimab PK as compared with patients with normal
hepatic function. Data of penpulimab in patients with severe hepatic impairment are not
adequate.
The Applicant’s Position
No dose adjustment is required based on age, race, body weight or sex. No dose adjustment is
required in patients with mild, moderate, or severe renal impairment, data of penpulimab in
patients with severe renal impairment are not adequate. No dose adjustment is required in
patients with mild or moderate hepatic impairment. Data of penpulimab in patients with
severe hepatic impairment are not adequate.

5.3.2.4. Are There Clinically Relevant Food-Drug or Drug-Drug Interactions,
and What Is the Appropriate Management Strategy?
No, penpulimab is intended for intravenous infusion administration; therefore, food-drug
interactions are not expected.
The Applicant’s Position
Penpulimab is intended for intravenous infusion administration; therefore, food-drug
interactions are not expected.
Penpulimab is a humanized monoclonal antibody, and PK interactions with other drugs have
not been studied. As monoclonal antibodies are not metabolized by cytochrome P450 (CYP) or
other drug metabolizing enzymes, inhibition, or induction of these enzymes by co-administered
medicinal products is not anticipated to affect the pharmacokinetics of penpulimab.
Penpulimab belongs to a class of drugs called immune checkpoint inhibitors. Because the
mechanism of action of this class of drugs is to block inhibitory signal that prevents activation of
T cells, there is a potential that these drugs may cause immune-mediated adverse drug
reactions. Withhold or permanently discontinue penpulimab depending on severity. In general,
if penpulimab requires interruption or discontinuation, administer systemic corticosteroid
therapy (1 mg to 2 mg/kg/day prednisone or equivalent) until improvement to Grade 1 or less.
Upon improvement to Grade 1 or less, initiate corticosteroid taper and continue to taper over
at least 1 month. Consider administration of other systemic immunosuppressants in patients
whose immune-mediated adverse reactions are not controlled by corticosteroid therapy.
The FDA’s Assessment
The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position that no food-drug or drug-drug interactions for
penpulimab are anticipated.

7. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation
7.1. Review of Relevant Individual Trials Used to Support Efficacy
7.1.1. Study AK105-202
7.1.1.1. Trial Design
The Applicant’s Description
Study AK105-202 is a single-arm, open-label, multicenter phase II clinical study to evaluate the
efficacy and safety of penpulimab in patients with metastatic nonkeratinizing NPC with disease
progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and at least one other prior line of
therapy. Patients were excluded from the study based on history of autoimmune disease,
medical conditions requiring systemic immunosuppression, prior organ or allogeneic stem cell
transplantation, prior treatment with anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1 or CTLA-4 antibodies, active central
nervous system (CNS) metastases, or ECOG performance score > 2.
Patients received penpulimab 200 mg intravenously every 2 weeks until disease progression as
determined by the investigator, or unacceptable toxicity, or a maximum of 24 months,
whichever occurred first. Administration of penpulimab was permitted beyond RECIST-defined
disease progression if the patients were assessed as clinically beneficial and tolerated to the
study drug by the investigator. Tumor measurements were performed every 8 weeks in first
year and every 12 weeks thereafter, to determine response by RECIST v1.1 criteria.
The primary objective of the study was to evaluate the objective response rate (ORR) assessed
by blinded independent radiology review committee (IRRC) per RECIST v1.1. Secondary
objectives included duration of response (DoR), progression-free survival (PFS) and overall
survival (OS).
The FDA’s Assessment
The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s description of the trial design for AK105-202. FDA notes
that the study was conducted at 26 sites in China.

7.1.1.2. Study Endpoints
The Applicant’s Description
•

•
•

Primary Efficacy Endpoint: ORR assessed by IRRC per RECIST v1.1.
– ORR is defined as the proportion of patients whose best overall response (BOR) is
confirmed CR or PR. The confirmation of CR or PR by repeated imaging assessments is
performed not less than 28 days (4 weeks) after the first observation of a CR or PR, and
there is no evidence of PD between the follow-up of the first observed CR or PR and
the follow-up for confirmation of CR or PR. BOR is defined as the best response
recorded from the start of treatment until progressive disease or the last evaluable
tumor assessment without prior to initiation of subsequent anti-cancer therapy.
Key Secondary Efficacy Endpoints: duration of response (DoR)
Other Secondary Endpoints:
1. ORR assessed by investigator, Disease control rate (DCR), time to response (TTR), PFS
assessed by IRRC and investigator per RECIST v1.1 and OS.
2. Pharmacokinetic (PK) and immunogenicity assessment
3. Safety: incidence and severity of adverse events, abnormal laboratory findings with
clinical significance.
4. Correlation analysis between the expression of EBV-DNA in blood and the anti-tumor
activity of penpulimab.

The FDA’s Assessment
The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s description of the study endpoints. The final efficacy
analysis is based upon a data cutoff of February 3, 2021. In a single arm trial such as Study
AK105-202, FDA considers time-to-event endpoints such as PFS and OS as not interpretable and
descriptive only. The efficacy evaluation of this study was based on ORR and DOR.
7.1.1.3. Statistical Analysis Plan and Amendments
The Applicant’s Description
The sample size calculation was based on the primary endpoint of ORR. A total of 110 patients
were needed for an ORR of 15% to be excluded using the lower limit of a two-sided 95% CI. If
an ORR of 26% is assumed for penpulimab, there is 82% chance of observing at least 25
responses (an ORR of 22.7%), with the lower limit of the 95% CI excluding a historical response
rate of 15%. In this study, an interim analysis was originally planned after at least 110 patients
were enrolled and completed at least 16 weeks of follow-up (an interval between the data
cutoff date and the date of first dose ≥ 16 weeks), and the results of the interim analysis was
planned to be used for communicating with the regulatory agencies. There were no plans to

7.1.2.3. Patient Disposition
Data
A total of 171 patients were screened and 130 patients were enrolled. The reason for all screen
failure was not meeting eligibility criteria. The first patient was enrolled on March 27, 2019, and
the last patient was enrolled on September 14, 2020.
As of the data cutoff, 114 patients with metastatic NPC had an opportunity to be followed for at
least 8 months (i.e., initiated penpulimab therapy at least 8 months prior to the data cut-off
date). Of those 114 patients, 1 patient had only one line of prior therapy, 1 patient did not have
measurable lesion at baseline as assessed by both the investigator and IRRC, and 1 patient did
not have measurable lesion at baseline as assessed by IRRC.
At the data cutoff for the interim analysis, 111 patients comprised primary efficacy population
that was used for efficacy data based on IRRC assessment, and 112 patients comprised primary
efficacy population that was used for efficacy data based on investigator assessment. The
median duration of follow-up was 14.7 months (range: 0.9 to 22.3) for the primary efficacy
population. In the primary efficacy population, 28 patients (25.2%) were continuing on
penpulimab, and 83 patients (74.8%) had patients discontinued penpulimab. Table 12
summarizes the reasons for discontinuation. The most common reason for discontinuation was
radiographic disease progression (53.2%).

7.1.2.7. Treatment Compliance, Concomitant Medications, and Rescue
Medication Use
Data
Treatment compliance was not analyzed because penpulimab was administered as an
intravenous infusion at the study center. No patient was discontinued from study treatment
due to protocol non-compliance. The most common concomitant medications were antiinflammatory and anti-rheumatic drugs, followed by analgesics.
The Applicant’s Position
Noncompliance, concomitant, and rescue medication use are variables unlikely to affect the
study results or the overall assessment of efficacy of penpulimab for patients with metastatic
NPC.
The FDA’s Assessment
The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position.

FDA generally agrees with the Applicant’s summary and position of the efficacy results of the

exploratory endpoint only. The subgroup results of ORR by PD-L1 expression (TPS <50 vs. TPS

results of an exploratory subgroup analysis of ORR by PD-L1 TPS <1%, TPS 1-49%, and TPS ≥50%.
The response rates across PD-L1 expression levels are somewhat discrepant, with a lower ORR
observed for patients with PD-L1 < 50%, although the 95% confidence intervals overlap with
those observed at patients with PD-L1 TPS ≥ 50%. Given that this post-hoc analysis is
exploratory in nature and that the impact of PD-L1 status and cutoff on NPC outcomes is not
well defined, the significance of these results is unknown and should be interpreted with
caution. In addition, the ORR of 21% (95% CI: 12, 33) for patients with TPS <50% likely
represents an improvement over available therapies for this refractory population.

7.1.2.10. Efficacy Results – Secondary and Other Relevant Endpoints
Data
DoR and TTR
The median TTR in the primary efficacy population was 1.84 months (range: 1.64 to 7.39
months). As of the data cutoff date, the longest durable response was 17.05+ months
(ongoing), 75.8% of responders remained ongoing, and the median DoR has not reached. The
DoR ≥ 6 months was 72.7% (24/33) at the data cutoff. The Kaplan-Meier estimate for the
percent of patients with a 6-month duration of response is 93.4% (95% CI: 75.9%, 98.3%), and
the estimate for the percent of patients with a 9-month duration of response is 77.6% (95% CI:
52.6%, 90.4%).

not yet been reached at the time of DCO, the DoR ≥ 6 months was 72.7% (24/33), and 25
(75.8%) of 33 responders had an ongoing response. The OS results were encouraging in this
heavily pretreated NPC population. The median OS was 18.63 months, and the 9-month OS rate
was 73.6% (95% CI: 64.1%, 80.9%). The percentage of DoR ≥ 6 months, median OS, and the 9month OS rate compare favorably with those seen with historical commonly used
chemotherapy agents.
The FDA’s Assessment
FDA generally agrees with the Applicant’s summary of the efficacy results of DoR. Per FDA’s
request, the Applicant also submitted the updated DoR data with a DCO of May 12, 2021, for
the 33 patients who had a response as assessed by IRRC. The data was reviewed and included in
the product labeling. At the updated DCO, the range of the DoR was (3.8+, 22.3+) and the
median DoR was still not reached; the percentage of responding patients with DoR ≥ 6 months
was 85% and the percentage of responding patients with DoR ≥ 9 months was 73%. The
updated DoR data showed a longer durability of response compared to the data from the DCO
of February 3, 2021.

7.1.2.12. Durability of Response
Data
A summary of DoR and TTR in the primary efficacy population is presented in Table 14 provides

The Applicant’s Position

seen with historical commonly used chemotherapy agents.

The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position regarding the durability of response.
7.1.2.13. Persistence of Effect
Data
Not Applicable.
The Applicant’s Position
As of data cut off, the median duration of follow-up was 14.7 months. The data can be used to
assess durability of response based on percentage of patients with DoR for at least 6 months,
but the data was not mature enough for assessing the durability of response for a longer
period. Additional follow-up past onset of response was warranted to better estimate the DoR
and assess persistence effect of penpulimab monotherapy in patients with metastatic NPC.
The FDA’s Assessment
The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position.

7.1.3. Assessment of Efficacy Across Trials

8. Integrated Assessment of Effectiveness
Data
The key efficacy results for the primary efficacy population were summarized below:
•
•
•

•
•

ORR: Confirmed ORR assessed by IRRC was 29.7% (95% CI: 21.4%, 39.1%).
DCR: The DCR assessed by IRRC was 49.5% (95% CI: 39.9%, 59.2%).
DoR: At of the data cutoff, 75.8% of responders had ongoing response, the median DoR has
not reached, and the DoR ≥ 6 months was 72.7%. The Kaplan-Meier estimate for patients
with a 6-month DoR is 93.4% (95% CI: 75.9%, 98.3%), and the estimate for patients with a 9month DoR is 77.6% (95% CI: 52.6%, 90.4%).
PFS: Median PFS assessed by IRRC was 3.65 months (95% CI: 1.87, 6.60) and the 9-month
PFS rate assessed by IRRC was 37.1% (95% CI: 27.8%, 46.4%).
OS: The median OS was 18.63 months (95% CI: 13.77, not estimable), and the 9-month OS
rate was 73.6% (95% CI: 64.1%, 80.9%).

The Applicant’s Position
Results based on an interim analysis of ORR and DoR demonstrate substantial evidence of
effectiveness of penpulimab monotherapy in patients with metastatic nonkeratinizing NPC with
disease progression on or after at least two prior lines of therapy, a serious disease where there
is a clear unmet medical need. The primary analysis showed promising ORR and DoR by IRRC in
the Primary Efficacy Population. The confirmed ORR of 29.7% (95% CI: 21.4%, 39.1%) compares
favorably with the overall response rate of < 10% of historical commonly used chemotherapy
agents. The responses were durable. After a median follow-up time of 14.7 months, median
DoR has not yet been reached at the time of DCO, the DoR ≥ 6 months was 72.7% (24/33), and
25 (75.8%) of 33 responders had an ongoing response.
The OS results were encouraging in this heavily pretreated NPC population. The median OS was
18.63 months (95% CI: 13.77, not estimable), and the 9-month OS rate was 73.6% (95% CI:
64.1%, 80.9%).
Collectively, these data provide compelling evidence of the clinically meaningful benefit of
penpulimab 200mg Q2W in patients with metastatic nonkeratinizing NPC with disease
progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and at least one other prior line of
therapy.

The FDA’s Assessment
The assessment of efficacy of penpulimab in patients with metastatic NPC with disease
progression on platinum-based chemotherapy and at least one other therapy was based on
results from the primary efficacy population enrolled on Study AK105-202, a single arm trial
conducted entirely in China. The ORR observed in the primary efficacy population was 30%
(95% CI 21, 39). The median DOR was not reached (range 3.8, 17.1+); 39% of responders had a
DOR ≥ 9 months.
The overall response rate and duration of response do not provide a meaningful advantage
over available therapy given the recent approvals of toripalimab-tpzi for the treatment of
patients with metastatic or recurrent, locally advanced NPC, with overlapping 95% confidence
intervals around the ORR observed in a similar population of patients who received toripalimabtpzi.
Another major limitation of the data is that the primary trial supporting this marketing
application was conducted exclusively in China and all patients enrolled were Asian. For
discussion of this issue, see Section 1 and Section 9.2 of this review. Regulatory flexibility is not
warranted in this instance as penpulimab does not address an unmet need.

8.1.2. Review of the Safety Database
8.1.2.1. Overall Exposure
Data
The summary of clinical safety includes safety data from 372 patients, including 130 patients
with NPC (target population) and 242 patients with various other solid tumors or classic
Hodgkin's lymphoma (cHL) (Study AK105-101 phase Ib, AK105-201, and AK105-204).
NPC Safety Population (Targeted Population)
In the NPC safety population, 130 patients were treated with penpulimab at a dose of 200 mg
Q2W. The median total duration of exposure was 139.5 days (range: 14-644 days), median
number of penpulimab doses was 9.5 (range: 1-43), median relative dose intensity was 97.67%
(range: 50.0% - 103.7%). Approximately 68.5% of patients were treated for more than 3
months, 43.1% for more than 6 months, 18.5% of patients received treatment for at least 12
months.
Integrated Penpulimab 200 mg Safety Population
A total of 372 patients have been treated with penpulimab at a dose of 200 mg Q2W. The
median duration of exposure was 168 days (range, 13 to 778 days). The median number of
doses received was 11.5 (range: 1-54), median relative dose intensity was 98.3% (range: 50.0% 103.7%). Approximately 66.1% of patients were treated for more than 3 months, 48.7% for
more than 6 months, 28.0% of patients received treatment for at least 12 months.
The Applicant’s Position
The eligibility criteria in the pivotal study were clinically relevant for the target population who
would receive penpulimab following regulatory approval in the proposed indication.
The exposure to study drug was considered adequate to support characterization of the safety
profile of penpulimab and allow for a comprehensive assessment of safety in all patients
treated with penpulimab.

The Applicant’s Position
Most death cases in the clinical studies were related to disease progression. This is consistent
with patients’ underlying medical conditions, and possibly concomitant medications.

The Applicant’s Position
The most commonly reported SAE was pneumonia. The frequency and nature of SAEs were
generally similar between the NPC safety population and studies on dosing regimen of
penpulimab 200 mg Q2W and there were no clinically meaningful differences between these
two populations for any SAEs.
The FDA’s Assessment
The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position that the type and frequency of SAEs were
generally similar between the two safety populations. The most common SAE across
populations was pneumonia. The four SAEs of death among the patients in the primary safety
population are described in further detail in Section 8.2.4.1 above. Overall, serious adverse
events excluding events of disease progression occurred in 19% of patients in the primary
safety population. Serious adverse events excluding events of disease progression occurred in
23% of patients in the pooled safety population.

8.1.4.3. Dropouts and/or Discontinuations Due to Adverse Effects
Data
NPC Safety Population (Targeted Population)
Disease progression was the primary cause of treatment discontinuation (66/130, 50.8%). AE
leading to discontinuation was reported in 5 (3.8%), the AEs were transaminase abnormal,
spinal cord compression, disseminated herpes zoster, pemphigoid, and pleural effusion (1
patient each).
Integrated Penpulimab 200 mg Safety Population
Disease progression was the primary cause of treatment discontinuation (176/372, 47.3%). AE
leading to discontinuation was reported in 22 (5.9%) patients. AEs resulting in permanent
discontinuation of penpulimab reported in > 1 patient each were immune-mediated
pneumonitis (in 3 patients), pleural effusion (in 2 patients), and gastrointestinal hemorrhage (in
2 patients).

in 25% of patients (n=33). Adverse events which required dosage interruption in ≥ 1 of patients
were hepatitis, hypothyroidism, pneumonia, anemia, pneumonitis, and rash.

occurred in 24% of patients (n=88). Adverse events which required interruption in ≥1% of
patients were hepatitis, hypothyroidism, anemia, pneumonia, musculoskeletal pain, rash, and
diarrhea.

8.1.4.6. Treatment Emergent Adverse Events and Adverse Reactions
Data
Study AK105-202
NPC Safety Population (Targeted Population)
One hundred and twenty-two out of 130 (93.8%) patients had at least one AE. Most patients
had Grade 1 or 2 events; 41(31.5%) patients had at least one ≥ Grade 3 AEs. The incidence of
drug-related AEs was 69.2% (90/130), and the incidence of ≥ Grade 3 drug-related AEs was 8.5%
(11/130).
The most commonly (the incidence of PT ≥ 20%) reported AEs, included: anemia,
hypothyroidism, and musculoskeletal pain. Common Grade 3-4 AEs (with an incidence of ≥ 2%)
were rash, hyponatremia, and anemia.
Integrated Penpulimab 200 mg Safety Population
Three hundred and fifty-seven out of 372 patients had at least one AE. Most patients had
Grade 1 or 2 events; 136 (36.6%) patients had at least one ≥ Grade 3 AEs was. The incidence of
TRAEs was 70.4% (262/372), and the incidence of ≥ Grade 3 TRAEs was 9.1% (34/372)
The most commonly (the incidence of PT ≥ 20%) reported AEs, included: anemia,
hypothyroidism, rash, and musculoskeletal pain. Common Grade 3-4 AEs (with an incidence of ≥
2%) were rash.

Data
Shift table for ECGs of clinical significance from baseline to worst post-baseline were

Electrocardiogram (ECG) assessments are part of routine safety monitoring. There was no

The FDA agrees with Applicant’s position.

8.1.4.11. Immunogenicity
Data
NPC Safety Population (Targeted Population)
The incidence of ADA positive after administration was 5.9% (7/119), with neutralizing
antibodies detected in 4.2% (5/119). Three patients with ADA positive had at least one AE, no
patient occurred drug related AE. Most frequently AEs for patients with ADA positive (≥ 1% of
patients) included weight decreased (2.3%), pyrexia (1.5%), and anemia (1.5%).
Integrated Penpulimab 200 mg Safety Population
The incidence of ADA positive after administration was 12.5% (42/335), with neutralizing
antibodies detected in 4.2% (14/335). Twenty-four patients had at least one AE, three patients
occurred drug related AE. Most frequently AEs for patients with ADA positive (≥ 1% of patients)
included alanine aminotransferase increased (2.2%), upper respiratory tract infection (2.4%),
pyrexia (2.4%), and anemia (2.2%).
The Applicant’s Position
In ADA-positive patients, the incidence and occurrence type of AE were generally similar to
those of all patients, with no specific type of AE and no increased incidence of infusion-related
reactions/hypersensitivities. Treatment emergent ADA had no significant impact on safety.

Immune-Mediated Pneumonitis
Immune-mediated pneumonitis occurred in 1.1% (4/372) of patients receiving penpulimab,
including two Grade 3 (0.5%), and two Grade 2 (0.5%) adverse reactions. Pneumonitis led to
permanent discontinuation of penpulimab in three of those four patients. High-dose of
systemic corticosteroids were administered to all four patients with pneumonitis. Pneumonitis
resolved with sequelae in 1 patient.

Penpulimab
Immune-Mediated Colitis
Immune-mediated colitis occurred in 0.8% (3/372) of patients receiving penpulimab. All were
Grade 2 (0.8%) adverse reactions.
Systemic corticosteroids were administered to all 3 patients with colitis. Colitis led to
withholding of penpulimab in all 3 patients. Of those 3 patients from whom penpulimab was
withheld for colitis, 2 patients reinitiated penpulimab after symptom improvement; 1 of those 2
patients experienced recurrence of colitis. Colitis resolved in 2 of those 3 patients.
Immune-Mediated Hepatitis
Immune-mediated hepatitis occurred in 0.5% (2/372) of patients receiving penpulimab.
Both were Grade 3 (0.5%) adverse reactions. Hepatitis led to withholding of penpulimab in
both patients.
Systemic corticosteroids were administered to those 2 patients with hepatitis. Hepatitis
resolved in one of those 2 patients. Of the 2 patients from whom penpulimab was withheld for
immune-mediated hepatitis, one reinitiated penpulimab after symptom improvement and this
patient experienced recurrence of hepatitis.
Immune-Mediated Endocrinopathies
Hypothyroidism
Immune-mediated hypothyroidism occurred in 9% (35/372) of patients receiving penpulimab,
including twenty-two Grade 2 (6%) and thirteen Grade 1 (3.5%) adverse reactions. No patient
permanently discontinued penpulimab due to hypothyroidism. Hypothyroidism led to
withholding of penpulimab in 1.9% (7/372) of patients.
All patients (35/35) received endocrine therapy. 1 patient received additional
immunosuppressant therapy. Of the 7 patients from whom penpulimab was withheld for
hypothyroidism, all reinitiated penpulimab after symptom improvement: 5 experienced
recurrences of hypothyroidism. Hypothyroidism resolved in 37% (13/35) of patients.
Hyperthyroidism
Immune-mediated hyperthyroidism occurred in 6% (23/372) of patients receiving penpulimab,
including four Grade 2 (1.1%) and nineteen Grade 1 (5.1%) adverse reactions. No patient
permanently discontinued of penpulimab due to hyperthyroidism. Hyperthyroidism led to
withholding of penpulimab in 0.5% (2/372) of patients. Events resolved in 87% (20) of the 23
patients. Endocrine therapy was administered in 13% (3/23) of patients.

Thyroiditis
Thyroiditis occurred in 0.5% (2/372) of patients receiving penpulimab. Thyroiditis led to

therapy. Events resolved in these two patients.
Immune-Mediated Nephritis With Renal Dysfunction
Immune-mediated nephritis occurred in 0.5% (2/372) of patients receiving penpulimab,
including one Grade 3 (0.3%) and one Grade 2 (0.3%) adverse reactions. All patients were
permanently discontinued penpulimab due to nephritis. Systemic corticosteroids were
administered to those 2 patients. Events resolved in one of these 2 patients.
Immune-Mediated Dermatologic Adverse Reactions
Immune-mediated rash or dermatitis occurred in 7.5% (28 /372) of patients receiving
penpulimab, including three Grade 3 (0.8%), eight Grade 2 (2.2%) and seventeen Grade 1 (4.6%)
adverse reactions. Systemic corticosteroids were administered in 17.9% (5/28) patients with
immune-mediated rash or dermatitis. Immune-mediated dermatologic adverse reactions led to
permanent discontinuation of penpulimab in 0.3% (1/372) of patients and withholding of
penpulimab in 1.1% (4/372) of patients. Of the 4 patients from whom penpulimab were
withheld for dermatologic adverse reactions, all reinitiated penpulimab after symptom
improvement; three experienced recurrences of hypothyroidism. Events resolved in 64.3%
(18/28) of patients.
Other Immune-Mediated Adverse Reactions
The following clinically significant, immune-mediated adverse reactions occurred at an
incidence of <1% in patients who received penpulimab 200 mg Q2W: nerve injury, and
arthralgia.
Infusion-Related Reactions
The infusion-related reactions occurred in 15 patients (4%) following dosing regimen of
penpulimab 200 mg Q2W, including Grade 1 in 3 patients, Grade 2 in 12 patients. No patients
occurred Grade 3-4 infusion-related reactions. One patient (0.8%) experienced Grade 1
hypersensitivity in proposed patient population (Study AK105-202).
The Applicant’s Position
The common irAEs (≥ 5%) were hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, and rash. The majority of
irAEs in studies on dosing regimen of penpulimab 200 mg Q2W were Grade 1 or 2 in severity. ≥

The FDA’s Assessment
The Applicant defined an immune related AE as a suspected event which based on medical
review is consistent with an immune mediated mechanism of action, and there were no
alternative etiologies. When applicable, serologic, immunologic, and histologic (biopsy) data
were used to support the characterization of an irAE. Potential irAEs, included but were limited
to immune-mediated colitis, dermatitis, pneumonia, hepatitis, encephalitis, nephritis,
hypothyroidism, and hyperthyroidism.
In the primary safety population (N=130), the most common irAEs (≥ 0.5%) were
hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, dermatitis, and pneumonitis. In the pooled safety population
(N=372), the most common irAEs (≥ 0.5%) were hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, dermatitis,
hepatitis, pneumonitis, colitis, and nephritis. There were no fatal irAEs observed in the pooled
safety population or the primary safety population. No IRRs were reported in the primary
safety population, and infusion related reactions occurred in 4% of patients in the pooled safety
population.

Additional results of FDA analyses and review used to inform Section 5 (Warnings and

Pneumonitis
Primary safety population (N=130): Immune-mediated pneumonitis occurred in 0.8% (1/130) of
patients receiving penpulimab (Grade 2), which required corticosteroids. There were no Grade
3 or 4 adverse events.
Pooled safety population (N=372): Immune-mediated pneumonitis occurred in 1.1% (4/372) of
patients, including two Grade 2 (0.5%) and two Grade 3 (0.5%) adverse reactions. Systemic
corticosteroids were required in all four patients. Penpulimab was permanently discontinued
due to pneumonitis in three patients and was interrupted and reintroduced following
resolution in one patient.
Colitis
Primary safety population (N=130): No patients developed immune-mediate colitis.
Pooled safety population (N=372): Immune-mediated colitis occurred in 0.8%, (3/372) of
patients; all were Grade 2 in severity and required systemic corticosteroids. Penpulimab was
interrupted and reintroduced following resolution in two patients and permanently
discontinued in one patient.

8.1.6. Safety Analyses by Demographic Subgroups
Data
This section summarizes the relationship between various intrinsic factors and the safety profile
of penpulimab. These data are relevant to patient management based on demographic or other
‘intrinsic’ factors. Only notable differences (≥ 10-percentage points) are discussed.
The safety profile of penpulimab was assessed in relation to the following intrinsic factors:
Sex (male, female)
Age (> 65, <= 65 years)
ECOG performance status (0, 1)

•
•
•
Sex

In proposed patient population, the AE profile of penpulimab was generally similar in both
females and males. AEs leading to drug discontinuation occurred at a higher rate in females
than males (6.5% vs 3.0%, respectively), this observation should be interpreted in the context of
the small sample size of the female subgroup.
For the integrated penpulimab 200 mg population, there was no appreciable difference
between females and males for any of the AE categories.
Age
For the integrated penpulimab 200 mg population, there was no appreciable difference
between age subgroups for any of the AE categories. The differences between age subgroups in
the proposed patient population cannot be assessed due to only 2 patients with age > 65 years
enrolled.
ECOG Performance Status
In proposed patient population, the incidence of events was similar in patients with a baseline
ECOG performance status of 0 and 1 for most AE categories. However, notable differences were
observed for Grade 3 or higher AEs (17.5% vs 37.8%) and SAEs (12.5% vs 26.7%), all of which
occurred at a higher rate in patients with an ECOG performance status of 1 compared with
ECOG performance status of 0.
For the integrated penpulimab 200 mg population, the AE profile of penpulimab was generally
similar in patients with a baseline ECOG performance status of 0 and 1, except for Grade 3 or
higher AEs (31.4% vs 40.3%) and SAEs (20.5% vs 29.6%), both of which occurred at a lower rate
in patients with an ECOG performance status of 0.

134 (36%) were female. In Study AK105-202, the incidence of Grade 3-4 AEs in male patients vs
female patients were 27 (28%) vs 4 (13%), respectively. In the pooled safety population, the
incidence of Grade 3 and 4 AEs among male patients vs female patients were 85 (38%) and 32
(24%), respectively.
In the primary safety population, 90 (69%) patients had an ECOG performance status (PS) of 1
and 40 (31%) patients had an ECOG PS of 0. The incidence of all grade AEs was similar among
ECOG PS of 1 or 0; however, Grade 3 or higher AEs occurred in 38% of patients with ECOG PS 1
compared to 18% of patients with ECOG PS of 0. In the pooled safety population, 216 (58%)
patients had an ECOG PS of 1 and 156 (42%) patients had an ECOG PS of 0. The incidence of
Grade 3 or higher AE occurred in 150 (40%) patients with ECOG PS of 1 and 117 (31%) with an
ECOG PS 0. The higher incidence of Grade 3 or higher AEs in patients with ECOG PS of 1
compared to those with an ECOG PS of 0 is likely due to the relatively poorer baseline condition
of these patients.
The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position that age and sex did not appear to have a major
impact on the safety profile of penpulimab.

8.1.8.2. Human Reproduction and Pregnancy
Data
Not Applicable.
The Applicant’s Position
Penpulimab has not been studied in pregnant or breastfeeding women. As of the DCO dates for
studies on dosing regimen of penpulimab 200 mg Q2W, there were no reports of pregnancies
or pregnancy-related events in either study. Based on its mechanism of action, penpulimab has
the potential to impact maintenance of pregnancy and may cause fetal harm when
administered to a pregnant woman. Human IgG1 is known to cross the placental barrier;
therefore, penpulimab has the potential to be transmitted from the mother to the developing
fetus. penpulimab is not recommended during pregnancy and in women of childbearing
potential not using effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 months after the
last dose.
There is no information regarding the presence of penpulimab in human milk, the absorption
and effects on the breastfed infant, or the effects on milk production. Human IgG is excreted in
human milk. Because of the potential for adverse reactions in breastfed infants from
penpulimab, advise a lactating woman not to breastfeed during treatment and for at least 5
months after the last dose.
The FDA’s Assessment
The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position.

8.1.8.4. Overdose, Drug Abuse Potential, Withdrawal, and Rebound
Data
There are no available safety data for penpulimab overdose.
The Applicant’s Position
There is no specific treatment in the event of penpulimab overdose and possible symptoms
have not been established.
As a result of its use, mode of action, physiological and pharmacological activity, and lack of
stimulant properties, penpulimab monotherapy is unlikely to be abused. Because penpulimab
has no known potential for dependence and is not continuously dosed, withdrawal or rebound
events are not relevant to penpulimab dosing.
The FDA’s Assessment
The FDA agrees with the Applicant’s position.

The FDA’s Assessment
FDA conducted the safety review of penpulimab in 130 patients with metastatic NPC who had
disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and at least one other prior line
of therapy who received penpulimab 200 mg Q3W on Study AK105-202 (primary safety
population) and in 372 patients with other solid tumors who received penpulimab 200 mg Q3W
across the development program (pooled safety population).
FDA’s review of deaths due to AEs, SAEs, irAEs, or AEs leading to treatment discontinuation in
patients enrolled in Study AK105-202 and in patients in the pooled safety population did not
raise concern for an unexpected safety signal relative to other agents in this class.
Serious adverse events occurred in 19% of patients in the primary safety population and in 23%
of patients in the pooled safety population. Among patients in the primary safety population,
the most common SAEs (≥ 2%) were pneumonia, death, and hepatitis.
Discontinuation of penpulimab due to an adverse event occurred in a total of 6% of patients in
the pooled safety population and in 3.8% of patients in the primary safety population. In the
primary safety population, the most common events leading to treatment discontinuation were
pleural effusion, herpes zoster disseminated, spinal cord compression, hepatitis, and
pemphigoid, occurring in 1 patient (0.8%) each.
Adverse events leading to drug interruptions occurred in 25% of patients in the primary safety
population and in 24% of patients in the pooled safety population. Among patients in the
primary safety population, the most common events (≥ 1%) leading to drug interruption were
hepatitis, pneumonia, hypothyroidism, anemia, pneumonitis, and rash.

Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) occurred In 22% of patients in the primary safety

There were no fatal irAEs observed in the primary safety population and the rates of irAEs
overall and Grade 3-4 irAEs are similar to that reported for other agents in this class, with the
exception of hypothyroidism. The relatively higher incidence of hypothyroidism observed in the
primary safety population (15%) is likely related to the high proportion of patients who received
prior radiation as treatment for NPC.
No infusion-related reactions (IRRs) were reported in the primary safety population; 4% of
patients in the pooled safety population had an IRR. All events were Grade 1-2 in severity.
In Study AK105-202, the most frequent AEs (≥ 10%) were hypothyroidism, hepatitis, weight
decreased, pyrexia, musculoskeletal pain, upper respiratory tract infection, and cough. The
most frequent laboratory abnormalities (≥ 20%) worsened from baseline were decreased
phosphate, decreased sodium, decreased lymphocytes, increased triglycerides, increased
gamma-glutamyl transferase, and decreased hemoglobin.
The safety profile of penpulimab is similar to other PD-(L)1 blocking antibodies when
administered as single agents. The most significant adverse reactions include immune-related
adverse events. Penpulimab, appears to have an acceptable safety profile when assessed in the
context of a life-threatening disease.

9. Summary and Conclusions
9.1. Statistical Issues
The FDA’s Assessment
There were no major statistical issues identified during review of this application. In the primary
efficacy population (n=111) enrolled in Study AK105-202, the confirmed ORR per IRRC
assessment was 30% (95% CI: 21%, 39%) at the DCO of February 3, 2021, and the tumor
responses appeared durable with a median follow-up time of 11.9 months at the DCO of May
12, 2021. The treatment benefit appeared to be similar across all relevant subgroups, with the
exception of patients with PD-L1 TPS < 50%, in which the point estimate of the ORR was 21%.
Follow-up was not sufficient to estimate the median duration of response and the upper limit
of its 95% confidence interval. In addition, there are limitations to interpretation of certain
study results from a non-randomized study; the analyses of time-to-event endpoints such as
PFS and OS are not interpretable in the absence of a comparator arm.
Study AK105-202 was conducted in a single country resulting in homogeneity of patient race
and region. FDA analyses of marketing application data generally include subgroup analyses by

key demographic characteristics such as age, sex, race, and region, to assess the consistency of
findings across these populations and whether the study results are applicable to the U.S.
population. Given the population of Asian patients enrolled on this trial, FDA was not able to
conduct subgroup analyses by race or region, resulting in the inability to examine the
consistency of the trial results by these factors.

9.2. Conclusions and Recommendations
The FDA’s Assessment
Study AK105-202 is a single-arm, open-label study conducted solely in China that enrolled 130
patients with metastatic NPC with disease progression on platinum-based chemotherapy and at
least one other line of therapy and received penpulimab 200 mg Q2W. The primary outcome
measure was ORR assessed by independent radiology review committee (IRRC) using Response
Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) v1.1. The key secondary outcome measure was
DOR. Among the 111 patients with measurable disease at baseline who had the opportunity for
at least 8 months of follow-up who comprised the primary efficacy population, the ORR was
30% (95% CI: 21, 39) (data cut off February 3, 2021). The median DOR was not reached (range
3.8, 17.1+); 39% of the 33 responding patients had a DOR ≥ 9 months. Given the approvals of
toripalimab-tpzi during the review period for this application, the magnitude of effect of
penpulimab on the ORR and DOR does not demonstrate a meaningful therapeutic benefit over
currently available therapies for the treatment of patients with metastatic non-keratinizing
NPC.
The safety profile of penpulimab is similar to that observed with other PD-1 blocking
antibodies. Safety issues identified as significant and serious during the BLA review were
immune-related adverse events and infusion-related reactions.
Study AK105-202 was conducted exclusively in China. Section 21 CFR 314.106(b) outlines three
requirements to establish the acceptability of foreign data as the sole basis for marketing
approval:
1.
2.
3.

The foreign data are applicable to the U.S. population and U.S. medical practice.
The studies have been performed by clinical investigators of recognized competence.
FDA is able to validate the data through an onsite inspection or other appropriate means.

FDA will apply this policy in a flexible manner according to the nature of the drug and data
being evaluated.
At the time of submission of this BLA, a flexible regulatory approach was warranted given that
there were no FDA-approved treatment options for the proposed population. The incidence of
NPC is much higher in China relative to the United States, where NPC is a relatively rare disease,
making enrollment to clinical trials more feasible in China. However, during the review of this
BLA for penpulimab, FDA granted traditional approval to toripalimab-tpzi, another anti-PD-1
antibody, in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine for the first-line treatment of adult

patients with metastatic or recurrent, locally advanced NPC. This approval was based on a
randomized (1:1) trial in 289 patients which demonstrated a 3.7-month improvement in
progression-free survival (PFS) with the addition of toripalimab-tpzi to cisplatin and
gemcitabine. This approval changed the standard of care for patients with metastatic or
recurrent, locally advanced NPC, with the inclusion of anti-PD-1-based therapy in the first-line
treatment setting. Toripalimab-tpzi also received traditional approval as a single agent for
patients with unresectable or metastatic NPC with disease progression on or after a platinumcontaining chemotherapy.
The Office of Pharmaceutical Quality (OPQ) also determined that the data submitted are not
sufficient to support a conclusion that the manufacture of penpulimab-kcqx is well-controlled
and will lead to a product that is pure and potent. See Section 3.2 for additional details.
The results from Study AK105-202 do not demonstrate a meaningful advantage over available
therapy, given the recent approvals of toripalimab-tpzi for patients with NPC and therefore do
not meet the requirements for accelerated approval as described in 21 CFR 314 subpart H.
Therefore, the FDA recommendation is Complete Response.

13. Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS)
The Applicant’s Position
The risks of penpulimab could be managed by routine pharmacovigilance activities and labeling.
REMS is not necessary to ensure that the benefits outweigh the risk for penpulimab for the
following reasons:
•
•

•
•

The benefit of penpulimab in the treatment of NPC was demonstrated in the pivotal study
of AK105-202.
The risks observed with penpulimab will be communicated through labeling. The risks
associated with penpulimab are in part due to its inhibitory effects of PD-1. If approved,
penpulimab will belong to a class with many other drugs (nivolumab, pembrolizumab,
atezolizumab, durvalumab and avelumab, etc.) in which irAEs are labeled in Warnings and
Precautions. The prescribers are likely aware of the risks of irAEs and the management with
other drugs in this class.
Sponsor has robust pharmacovigilance system, which includes data intake, case
management, regulatory reporting, literature monitoring, signal management and
aggregate reporting.
In the postmarket setting, Akeso will conduct routine surveillance of the safety profile of
penpulimab including all reports of adverse drug experiences and product compliant
reports, and will revise RMP, RSI, and USPI if an evaluation of the safety data yields
significant new information.

The FDA’s Assessment
A risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS) is not required given the Complete Response
action.

19.4.2.3.2. Adequacy of ADA Evaluation

Two ADA assays were used to identify ADA positivity and titer. These data were not
discriminated in PPK analysis. Pre-existing ADA was identified in >5% of subjects in Study
AK105-202 with titers of >800 in some patients. Since ADA records were imputed as the prior
ADA observation, most of the ADA records till 2nd infusion were the same as the baseline except
for the pre-2nd dose record. Due to the false positivity ADA rate and the high titer of 800
(compared to the lowest titer of 50), these ADA records may impact PPK assessment. In
addition, titer may have incremental impact on PK. As described in the decision tree (Figure 21),
FDA conducted sensitivity analysis to evaluate the impact of ADA with assays of adequate
sensitivity and specificity, evaluate treatment emergent ADA (treatment-induced and
treatment-boosted), and titer levels in PPK analysis. Overall, ADA was not found to produce a
statistically significant effect on PK.

19.4.3.3. Review Issues and Reviewer’s Independent Analysis
19.4.3.3.1. Steady-State Exposures Are Not Applicable in the Applicant’s ER
Analysis

Two errors were identified in the Applicant’s analysis: 1) The Applicant applied 200 mg Q2W
when simulating steady-state concentrations for all subjects, including those who did not
receive this dosage; 2) The Applicant’s PPK model is not adequate to describe steady-state PK
due to underprediction. Therefore, FDA only verified the E-R analysis with C1D1 EOI, C2D1 and
C5D1 pre-dose concentrations as the exposure metrics.
19.4.3.3.2. Discrepancies in the Subject Number (C2D1, C5D1) and p-value
in ER for Safety Assessment Identified

The Applicant identified a positive relationship between C5D1 pre-dose concentration and 2
safety events of hematology (decreased neutrophil count and decreased WBC), and 1 safety
event of clinical biochemistry (increased cholesterol). These TEAEs led to no dosage
interruption or discontinuation.

FDA verified the E-R analysis and found discrepancies in the subject number and p-value from
the Applicant’s analysis. The discrepancies are due to exclusion of C2D1 pre-dose records and
C10D1 (9 doses) of Study AK105-204; however, sample size reported in the Applicant’s analysis
enumerated exposure records including NAs. Of note, the cycle number of Study AK105-204 is
different in that each dose is counted as a cycle compared to 2 doses counted as a cycle in
other studies. The numbers of observed C2D1 pre-dose and C5D1 (and C10D1 of Study AK105204 for similar number of doses) pre-dose concentrations were 330 and 187, respectively
reported in FDA’s analysis compared to 283 and 176, respectively used in the Applicant’s
analysis.
FDA was only able to confirm the positive relationship (p<0.05) for decreased WBC (Figure 18).
For this particular AE, multivariate logistic regression was performed which included age, sex,
race, weight, albumin, baseline ECOG, LDH, ALP, AST as covariates. Stepwise covariate selection
using AIC criteria reduced the model to C5D1 pre-dose as the only covariate. With inclusion of
the imbalanced baseline covariates across quartiles of C5D1 pre-dose concentrations, namely
age, sex, weight, and baseline ECOG, C5D1 pre-dose concentration was still identified as a
significant covariate. Overall, given no dosage interruption or discontinuation, the positive
relationship between C5D1 pre-dose and decreased WBC is not considered clinically
meaningful.
